# Blobby — VS Code Pet for DSH

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Blobby is the official VS Code chat pet, ported to the DeepSeek Harness Web composer. It uses the
official sprite sheets, accessories, frame timings, physics and interaction rules from
`microsoft/vscode`, not a look-alike. On Windows it can also step out of the DSH window and live on
the desktop while DSH is minimized.

![Blobby state matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/96274zxc/vscode-pet/main/docs/states.png)

## Attribution

This is an independent DSH port, not a Microsoft product. All Blobby sprite art, accessory atlases,
animation timing, physics constants, achievement catalog, color palette and jump-game rules are
derived from the official VS Code implementation and are used under the MIT license.

- Upstream documentation: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/chat-pet
- Upstream sprite assets and runtime:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chatPet
- Pinned upstream commit: `ce233327f26ef7791b7fff0143c24e81a8126bd2`
- The plugin icon is a composite of the official idle body and wizard-hat atlas with the official
  thinking bubble, recolored to a white body. The master is 144×144 (4× the 36px plugin-card
  artwork); `icons/icon-{144,72,48,36,30}.png` keeps native variants, and `icon.svg` embeds the
  144px master.
- See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for the complete source-file list and Microsoft's MIT license text.

Thanks to the VS Code team and the original Blobby authors for the character and artwork.

## What it does

- Sits on top of the composer and reacts to chat: pointer gaze, typing, thinking, clapping when the
  agent needs input, sleeping after 20 seconds, and the red-button celebration when a turn finishes.
- Drag it, flick it, throw it with `Shift+←/→`, hop with `←/→`, catch it while it falls, and watch
  the despawn/respawn portal sequence. While the DSH window is visible the composer card is its only
  perch: it spawns and respawns above that card, follows it when the window or input grows/shrinks,
  bounces off the side walls, and its respawn drop is capped above the composer instead of falling
  from the top of the chat. On the desktop the taskbar (or the screen bottom while the taskbar is
  auto-hidden) is the floor.
- **Desktop display (Windows desktop app only)**: the pet's context menu gains a checkable
  **Show on Desktop** item, with **Smart Hide** directly below it once enabled. While DSH is active
  the native helper waits prepared, so as soon as DSH is minimized **or loses focus to another
  window** Blobby moves to the desktop through the official respawn portal and lands above the taskbar
  at the bottom-right; focusing DSH again plays the portal/fall return inside the window. Double-click
  the desktop pet to bring the DSH window back. The desktop right-click menu mirrors the DSH menu:
  Hats, Change Color and Play Jump Game restore DSH and open the existing panels/game, while Go on the
  Run, size controls, Show on Desktop and Smart Hide work on the desktop itself. Throws always land
  on the taskbar/screen floor and never trigger a fall respawn. The helper window ends exactly at the
  taskbar and only the pet/menu accept clicks, so the taskbar and windows underneath stay usable; the
  menu is positioned before it is shown and keeps its size rows open for repeated clicks, its size
  labels align to the outer edges of their halves like the in-window menu, and it follows the DSH
  light/dark palette and current UI language. While the menu is open the helper locks a single window
  rect that already covers the pet at the maximum scale and the menu, so growing/shrinking never
  moves or resizes the layered window and the menu cannot jitter. The helper renders on the
  composition loop with subpixel
  position compensation and no per-frame topmost churn, so its motion matches the in-window pet
  instead of sliding on the window's pixel grid. It also adopts the exact grab cursor used by DSH by
  capturing the rendered pet's cursor at runtime (no separate cursor asset), together with the same
  drag-resistance wobble and the crossed-out (X) eyes while the pet is held (the same eye-overlay
  geometry as the in-window CSS, baked into the frames at the matching size). Chat reactions stay in
  sync on the desktop (the thinking bubble appears
  while a turn is running). The desktop state machine also mirrors the window: typing while the
  composer has input, waking when facts wake it, **buttonPress** when a request completes (silent
  when cancelled), dizzy after quick cursor wiggles, reduced-motion variants, and eyes during the
  typing/buttonPress/love poses. Remaining known differences: the desktop never falls to a respawn
  death (taskbar floor), the jump game opens in DSH, the DSH port does not track achievements, and
  the periodic blink, cursor-following pupils, bounce counter and 20-bounce confetti are not baked
  into the desktop frames. The facing follows the cursor only in the idle pose; sleeping, waking,
  typing, rendering, clapping and reaction poses keep the direction they had when they started,
  matching the window's ChatPetFacingController.
  **Smart Hide** keeps the pet on the desktop only instead of above other applications. The native
  helper exits with DSH; on non-Windows the menu items are absent and the host refuses to start the
  helper, and the plain Web GUI hides the items as well.
- Right-click for **Hats**, **Play Jump Game**, **Go on the Run / Come Back**, inline
  **− Shrink / Grow +** and **Reset Size** controls, and **Change Color**.
- 13 hats from the official catalog plus the **Color Customization** custom-color entry, laid out with the
  DSH-only **No Hat** option as a 3-column, 15-card grid. The counter keeps VS Code's "14 of 14
  unlocked" wording; only the 13 hats and Color Customization are counted. The DSH port does not track
  achievements, so every hat is unlocked by default and the initial look is **Insiders + Cowboy
  Hat**; unlock hints, rewards and "new" badges are not shown. `/blobby` still unlocks **Color
  Customization** for the solid and custom colors.
- Click reactions include a rare (~1%) **yapping** fall: Blobby tips over and opens its mouth; the
  light gap is the official sprite's open mouth, not missing artwork.
- Stable/Insiders colors plus the eight official solid presets and a custom hex color (unlocked by
  `/blobby`). Hats and colors are applied immediately and persist.
- Blobby's jump game: Space to charge, release to jump, Left/Right to aim or hop, Escape to exit,
  with moving/crumbling platforms, wall bank shots, hop score and a persisted high score.
- Reduced-motion support, keyboard access, and a live status region for screen readers.

## Install in a DSH profile

From the public npm package (after release):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add vscode-pet
```

Source install from the public repository (always available):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:96274zxc/vscode-pet
```

For the Electron desktop app, use **Plugins → Add plugin → `vscode-pet`**, or the same CLI with
`--profile desktop` where the CLI is allowed to manage that profile.

For development from this checkout, link the package into a profile:

```powershell
$node = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe"
$pnpm = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\pnpm\bin\pnpm.mjs"
$profile = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop"
& $node $pnpm --dir $profile add "vscode-pet@link:C:/path/to/vscode-pet"
```

Then add `vscode-pet` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` (or enable it in Plugins). Reload the
page; if the Electron app does not recompose the loader live, restart it. To uninstall, remove the
dependency and the bundle selection.

## Build and test

```powershell
node scripts/fetch-assets.mjs   # re-download the pinned VS Code assets
node scripts/build.mjs          # validate dimensions and build client.js
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

`client.js` is generated. Edit files under `src/` and rebuild; do not edit `client.js` directly.
Assets are embedded as PNG data URLs so the plugin works under both `http://` and the desktop
`dsh-app://` scheme without cross-origin canvas issues. The test suite also compiles and runs the
Windows desktop helper's deterministic self-test (`desktop/blobby-desktop.ps1 -SelfTest`); the
helper is a local PowerShell/.NET WPF process that the host half starts only in the Windows desktop
app.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Click / Enter / Space | Random reaction; wakes Blobby; opens the hats panel while the star is visible |
| `←` / `→` | Hop along the composer |
| `Shift+←` / `Shift+→` | Throw toward a wall |
| Right-click / `Shift+F10` / ContextMenu | Context menu |
| Drag | Move Blobby; release with speed to throw |
| Bounce while falling / Enter / Space | Bounce |
| `/blobby` | Unlock Color Customization and open the color tab |
| `/vscode-pet` | Show/hide Blobby (keeps the plugin installed) |
| Right-click → **Show on Desktop** | Windows desktop app only: move Blobby to the desktop while DSH is minimized or unfocused (✓ when enabled) |
| Right-click → **Smart Hide** | Windows desktop app only: show the desktop pet on the desktop only, never above other apps |
| Alt+Tab / click another window / minimize | Windows desktop app only: move Blobby to the desktop above the other window |
| Focus the DSH window | Windows desktop app only: return Blobby into the DSH window |
| Double-click the desktop pet | Bring the DSH window back |

## Compatibility

- Target: DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.1` Web and Desktop profiles.
- The desktop display is Windows desktop only. It uses `connection`-authenticated host routes on the
  loopback server plus a local PowerShell/.NET WPF helper; the plain Web GUI hides the menu items and
  non-Windows hosts return `501` for desktop-start requests. While the display is enabled the helper
  stays prepared in the background for an immediate handoff and exits when DSH exits. No DSH source is
  modified and no model tools or routes outside `/api/blobby/desktop/*` are added.
- Preferences, hats, colors and the jump-game high score stay in
  `localStorage['dsh.vscode-pet.prefs.v1']` on the local device. Desktop frames and settings are
  generated on the client; the helper only receives PNG frames, labels and local geometry.

## Source and license

Sprite art, animation timing and interaction logic are derived from
[Microsoft VS Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode) commit
`ce233327f26ef7791b7fff0143c24e81a8126bd2`, MIT licensed. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for the exact
paths. The plugin code is MIT licensed (see `LICENSE`).

## Verification

The plugin was exercised in a temporary DSH web profile with headless Chrome: idle/typing/thinking/
clapping/sleep/reactions, drag and throw, despawn/respawn, the context menu, both customization
tabs, hat and color selection, Color Customization unlock, and the jump game. `docs/states.png` is the
state matrix and `docs/hats.png` / `docs/color.png` are the customization panels from that
run.

It was then verified in the real Electron desktop profile (not headless): composer-card landings,
default spawn, maximize/restore repositioning, rotated wall bounces, capped respawn, and resizing
while the pet is airborne. The fall and respawn paths were also compared frame by frame against
VS Code 1.144's Blobby on the same machine.

Desktop display was verified in the same Windows Electron profile: the trailing check mark and the
conditional Smart Hide item, the portal/respawn handoff when minimizing and restoring, landing on
the taskbar, throwing without a fall respawn, Smart Hide against a foreground app, double-click
restore, the desktop Hats command opening the existing panel, and the helper exiting when DSH's
host closes its stdin. After the handoff optimizations it was re-checked for the prepared helper
(desktop portal visible within about half a second of clicking away), focus-based switching
(Alt+Tab/click-away), the ~60 fps composition loop during throws, subpixel-exact pet placement
(`appliedScreenX` equal to the physics position instead of the window's rounded pixel), the exact
DSH grab cursor captured at runtime (byte-identical icon/hotspot), the drag resistance wobble, the
thinking bubble while a turn runs, a taskbar that stays clickable under the pet window, and a desktop
context menu that appears at its final position without a flash.
The helper's geometry, physics and state-machine self-test runs in the test suite.

# @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle

A DSH profile layer that mounts the D1 providers over a stock profile.

The bundle itself has no runtime code. Its `cordis.patch.yml` inserts:

| Entry | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dsh-cu-client` | `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-client`: the browser half that renders DSH-CU tool cards in the DSH client |
| `browser-use-registry` | The single browser-use registration slot (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-browser-use`) |
| `dsh-cu-browser` | `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-browser-use-d1` in launch mode, headless off macOS, locale `zh` |
| `computer-use-registry` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-computer-use`, disabled |
| `dsh-cu-computer` | `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1`, disabled (needs macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording) |

## Install

```bash
# 1. Build and register the packages in a profile.
dsh plugin --profile dsh-cu add \
  link:/path/to/dsh-cu-bundle \
  link:/path/to/dsh-cu-core \
  link:/path/to/dsh-browser-use-d1 \
  link:/path/to/dsh-computer-use-d1

# 2. Add the bundle to the profile's layer list.
#    ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-cu/package.json
#    "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle"] } }

# 3. Compose and verify without starting a browser or a model.
dsh --profile dsh-cu --dump-config | grep dsh-cu
```

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm, so a published package can be installed by name
instead of by link.

## Configuration

The bundle reads the environment at profile load:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_CU_DECISION_ENDPOINT` | `http://127.0.0.1:8765` | Local D1 decision service |
| `DSH_CU_DECISION_TOKEN` | `dsh-cu-local` | Bearer token for that service |
| `DSH_CU_CONTROL_TOKEN` | `dsh-cu-control` | Token for the loopback control page |
| `DSH_CU_HEADLESS` | unset | `1` forces the headless browser path |
| `DSH_CU_CAPTURE_SKILLS` | unset | `1` enables Skill candidate capture (needs `skillStorePath`) |

Per-profile overrides belong in `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`, not in
this package: a patch entry with `id: dsh-cu-browser` replaces the bundled config.

## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0` (`engines.dsh` on every package).
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `~4.0.5`.
- The profile must not already mount another browser-use provider: the slot is
  exclusive, and a second registration fails at startup.

## Native provider

The native entries ship disabled. Before enabling both, read the native section
of the provider README: it needs a local CUA helper, macOS Accessibility and
Screen Recording grants, and an authorized application per run.

# DSH CU Decision Lab

Experiments using [LiquidAI/d1-2B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-2B) as a System 1 decision model for DeepSeek Harness Browser Use and Computer Use.

## Repository

[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20topic-dsh--plugin-2563eb)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
[github.com/Alyosha28/dsh-cu-d1](https://github.com/Alyosha28/dsh-cu-d1) · MIT

This repository is an installable DSH plugin, not a directory: `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle`
declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-client` declares `dsh.client`, and every
package declares `engines.dsh`. The plugin path is a profile, so the concrete
install is:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Alyosha28/dsh-cu-d1.git
cd dsh-cu
npm install --include=dev && npm run build

# One command: links the packages, mounts @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle, runs the doctor.
npm run install:plugin -- --profile=dsh-cu

# Equivalent by hand:
dsh plugin --profile dsh-cu add \
  link:$PWD/packages/dsh-cu-bundle link:$PWD/packages/dsh-cu-core \
  link:$PWD/packages/dsh-browser-use-d1 link:$PWD/packages/dsh-computer-use-d1 \
  link:$PWD/packages/dsh-cu-client
```

Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`; another runtime is refused by the Harness
compatibility gate with an explicit message.

## Install as a DSH plugin

The packages target DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.5** (`engines.dsh: >=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`) and cordis `~4.0.5`, the versions the desktop application runs. A different runtime is refused by the Harness compatibility gate with an explicit message instead of loading a mismatched plugin.

```bash
# Build the packages once.
npm install --include=dev && npm run build

# Install into a profile: links the packages, mounts the bundle, backs up the
# manifest, and runs the doctor. --dry-run prints the steps only.
npm run install:plugin -- --profile=dsh-cu

# Or run each step by hand:
#   dsh plugin --profile dsh-cu add link:$PWD/packages/dsh-cu-bundle ... 
#   add "@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle" to ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-cu/package.json
#   npm run plugin:doctor -- --profile=dsh-cu
```

The plugin is consumed at the profile level, not inside the desktop application:
any profile that lists `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-bundle` mounts it, whether that profile is booted
by the CLI (`dsh --profile dsh-cu …`) or shipped another way. Installing into the
Electron-owned `desktop` profile is optional and not required for the plugin to
be a DSH plugin; if you ever do it, quit DSH first so the running app cannot
overwrite the manifest on exit.

`plugin:doctor` composes the profile with `dsh --dump-config`, checks that both entries exist and are enabled, fails on a competing browser provider, and compares the plugin's DSH package version with the host. It never starts a browser, a helper, or a model.

The bundle disables the native provider by default. Enable both native entries only after granting macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording and reading the native section below. When a native run needs a missing grant, the provider opens the macOS privacy dialog once (`promptPermissions`, default true), returns `prompted` plus a deep link to the exact System Settings pane, and the control page's permission button does the same. `npm run plugin:doctor` prints the current Accessibility and Screen Recording state, so the gap is visible before a run fails. `DSH_CU_DECISION_ENDPOINT`, `DSH_CU_DECISION_TOKEN`, `DSH_CU_CONTROL_TOKEN`, and `DSH_CU_HEADLESS` configure the browser entry at profile load; see [`packages/dsh-cu-bundle/README.md`](packages/dsh-cu-bundle/README.md).

Without Playwright's own browser build, the provider launches an installed Google Chrome or Edge and reports `browser_unavailable` with a recovery step when neither exists, so a fresh machine does not need `npx playwright install` first.

## Reuse-first execution

Use the official execution providers for general automation instead of reimplementing their capabilities:

- **Browser:** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-playwright-mcp` supplies the upstream Playwright MCP tools, including tabs, upload/drop, snapshots, and attach-mode access to an existing browser's tabs and login state.
- **Native macOS:** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cua/api` supplies the authorized application/window object API. `getApp` owns consent, launch, and initial AX observation; callers must not poll it as an application launcher.

The D1 providers below remain experimental decision and Verified Skill layers. Deterministic workflows should use the official tools directly. The D1 Browser provider is not a replacement for Playwright MCP's broader browser surface.

Opt-in live checks use real installed applications and no accounts:

```bash
npm run test:live:browser
DSH_CU_REAL_APPS=1 npm run test:live:native

# D1 comparison only; requires the local decision service.
D1_DECISION_TOKEN=test-token npm run test:live:d1
```

`test:live:native` refuses to touch an existing TextEdit process and tests only a new unsaved document. The broader matrices below use newly launched controlled applications and reversible synthetic state.

The real ordinary application matrix covers fresh TextEdit documents and a resettable Calculator, including dynamic AX actions, Skill capture/rerun/approval/replay, stale-input recovery, multiwindow and occlusion availability, active-run stop, and sensitive-data persistence. Run three independent rounds and aggregate their timing evidence:

```bash
DSH_CU_REAL_APPS=1 DSH_CU_REAL_APP_ROUND=1 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/real-app-matrix.e2e.ts
DSH_CU_REAL_APPS=1 DSH_CU_REAL_APP_ROUND=2 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/real-app-matrix.e2e.ts
DSH_CU_REAL_APPS=1 DSH_CU_REAL_APP_ROUND=3 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/real-app-matrix.e2e.ts
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.real_app_acceptance
```

These rounds use a deterministic decision fixture through the D1 Provider contract to isolate execution and lifecycle reliability; they do not measure real-model decision quality. Existing TextEdit or Calculator processes cause an immediate refusal, including localized process names. Reports are written to `results/real-apps/` and `results/REAL_APP_ACCEPTANCE.md`. The current release accepts all nine scenarios in each round, including real multiwindow selection guards, overlapping-window occlusion, Skill lifecycle, active-run stop, and sensitive-data retention.

The third-party matrix covers LibreOffice Writer, WPS Writer, Visual Studio Code, and Chrome. LibreOffice and Chrome use independent AX readback; WPS and Visual Studio Code use independent macOS Vision OCR readback. A controlled foreground anchor and a 20 ms process monitor verify that execution does not switch the frontmost application. Run three independent rounds and aggregate their evidence:

```bash
DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_APPS=1 DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_ROUND=1 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/third-party-apps.e2e.ts
DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_APPS=1 DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_ROUND=2 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/third-party-apps.e2e.ts
DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_APPS=1 DSH_CU_THIRD_PARTY_ROUND=3 npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/third-party-apps.e2e.ts
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.third_party_acceptance
```

Reports are written to `results/third-party/` and `results/THIRD_PARTY_ACCEPTANCE.md`. Acceptance covers all four measured applications and foreground-preserving execution. Existing LibreOffice or WPS processes cause an immediate refusal. VS Code and Chrome use isolated profiles and exact child-PID attachment, so existing user instances remain outside the run. Locked-session execution and unattended production remain outside the accepted scope.

## Current capabilities

- Offline browser/desktop operation and target benchmarks.
- Local Browser Use control with real Chrome DOM snapshots and Playwright.
- A TypeScript DSH Browser Use Provider using official `SessionResources`, with standard direct-tool execution and independent structured verification.
- A read-only `browser_observe` path that returns the current element table for planning and postcondition writing without D1 or input.
- DSH-CU tools render as first-class cards inside the DSH client: `@albaincompleta/dsh-cu-client` declares `dsh.client`, the client module scanner serves its bundle, and each tool result shows a status chip, a one-line summary, and an expandable payload in the transcript.
- The controlled tab is marked while a run is active: a title prefix (`● DSH-CU 控制中 · `) and a favicon dot stay visible in the browser tab strip, survive navigation, and clear on finish, stop, failure, and takeover.
- A menu-bar item (`◉ DSH-CU`) appears for the duration of a native run and of a visible browser run, with the target in its tooltip and a localized "stop" action. It is an accessory status item: no Dock icon, no activation, no focus change.
- Direct `browser_navigate`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_upload`, and `browser_downloads` tools: open a URL, list/select/open/close tabs, upload local files into one file input, and collect page downloads without a decision call. Selecting a tab moves the provider's owned page, its indicator, and every later subgoal to that tab. Upload requires a per-call approval naming every path and refuses relative paths, missing files, directories, and non-file inputs before prompting.
- Deterministic, typed DOM extraction through `browser_extract`, with explicit locators, per-field evidence, and zero decision-model calls.
- A localized run-control page with status, pause/resume, stop, takeover, system permissions, Verified Skill management, and an audit timeline.
- Synthetic and real-browser D1 `box` localization benchmarks.
- Official macOS CUA evaluations covering AX-first actions, AX-less screenshot fallback, Retina/window-point conversion, stale snapshots, resize guards, and independent fixture-state verification.

The visual work is an experimental research prototype. It controls only newly launched, explicitly authorized applications and does not use existing user processes or online accounts.

## Python setup

```bash
uv sync --extra dev
uv run pytest
```

The model loader pins revision `cfe5760ff5d5998f91d9ac56bd4b2dbd96996d41` because `trust_remote_code=True` executes the model repository's custom Python code. The first run downloads approximately 3.84 GB of weights.

## Browser benchmarks

```bash
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.benchmark --local-files-only
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.browser_benchmark --local-files-only
```

Both runners accept `--text-strategy speculative|on-demand`. The A/B evidence is in [`results/TEXT_STRATEGY_AB.md`](results/TEXT_STRATEGY_AB.md).

The browser runner serves only checked-in fixtures over loopback HTTP and uses an isolated Chrome instance. Successful status requires independent DOM postconditions.

## DSH Browser Use Provider

```bash
npm install --include=dev
npm run build
npm test
npm run test:plugin
```

`npm run test:plugin` loads the built provider through the cordis loader with the real DSH services, then calls `browser_extract`, `browser_observe`, and `browser_control` on a loopback fixture in headless Chromium. It is the plugin-level check; see [`results/PLUGIN_DSH_TEST.md`](results/PLUGIN_DSH_TEST.md).

The provider packages are `packages/dsh-browser-use-d1` and `packages/dsh-computer-use-d1`, with shared contracts in `packages/dsh-cu-core`. They expose `d1_browser_subgoal`, `browser_observe`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_upload`, `browser_downloads`, `computer_subgoal`, and control/publication tools. Subgoals require a narrow goal and structured `verify` assertions. `browser_observe` returns the owned page's current element table without a decision call or input. Browser resources belong to the exact live Agent through the official runtime; PTC is not required. Native actions use official CUA application authorization and AX snapshots. `TYPE_TEXT` uses `setValue` for compatible fields; `PASTE_TEXT` focuses the selected element through relative window coordinates when geometry is available, or uses a screenshot box, then issues one official Paste. Clipboard uncertainty triggers independent readback and stops without automatic input replay. `STALE_APP` permits one fresh application selection before any input. Screenshot fallback uses explicit pixel/window-point mapping.

### Visible control without foreground interruption

Visible Browser launch mode uses a background Chrome session and a nonactivating macOS preview panel. The panel displays the controlled tab, live page title, software cursor, current phase and step, and pause/resume, stop, takeover, and close controls. Pause suspends the active run without aborting it; resume continues the same step. Completion, failure, and takeover keep a result card until it is dismissed. On takeover in launch mode, the provider opens a headed browser with the current cookies, local storage, session storage, scroll position, and typed form values so the user can continue in a real window; attach mode brings the existing owned tab forward. Restored fields are matched by id or name first, and a control whose identity disappeared is left empty instead of receiving another field's value. Native execution uses a nonactivating `NSPanel` cursor and status overlay that follows the authorized window, with the application name and window title. Dynamic D1 execution and zero-model Skill replay share the same activity events and cleanup lifecycle. `headless: true` disables the Browser preview and the takeover window for controlled tests and headless environments.

The Browser Provider accepts `tabUrl` or `tabTitle` in attach mode. A missing or duplicate match, or several open tabs with no selector, fails with `tab_selection_required` instead of silently controlling the first tab. Both providers accept `locale: zh | en` for panel and approval text; model-facing guidance stays English. Visible helpers are compiled once per source build and reused from a private temporary cache.

### Decision latency

The decision service downscales screenshots wider than 800 pixels before vision encoding and leaves normalized boxes untouched. Measured on a 2508-wide window, one decision falls from 879 ms to 310 ms, while six consecutive trials keep selecting `CLICK` on a dense article list. `DSH_CU_VISION_WIDTH` overrides the threshold for interfaces with small targets. `scripts/cua-session.mts` is a resident execution session that reuses the CUA connection, window handles, and indicator across commands, so repeated steps pay only capture and inference. Start the service with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1`; without them the first load retries a model-repository request and stalls for minutes. Screenshot capture costs 350–970 ms depending on window content and is not reducible through the official capture interface. Measurements and boundaries are recorded in [`results/CU_PERFORMANCE.md`](results/CU_PERFORMANCE.md).

The indicators are driven by execution adapters rather than model output. Local input in a native controlled window returns `takeover_detected`; an operation that needs foreground access returns `foreground_required` without automatic activation. Stop, completion, failure, helper exit, and heartbeat loss release input and remove the indicators. Helper processes are compiled into private temporary directories unless `indicatorHelperPath` selects a prebuilt binary.

Run the focused visible-control checks:

```bash
npm test --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-browser-use-d1 -- tests/indicator.spec.ts
npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-browser-use-d1 -- tests/visible-browser.e2e.ts
npm run test:e2e --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/indicator.e2e.ts
npm test --workspace @albaincompleta/dsh-cu-computer-use-d1 -- tests/provider.spec.ts -t "preserves continuous foreground input"
```

These checks inspect real macOS windows, exercise all three controls through Accessibility, verify foreground and system-pointer preservation, confirm continuous foreground typing during dynamic and Skill execution, and cover normal cleanup and forced helper termination. Evidence is recorded in [`results/VISIBLE_CONTROL_ACCEPTANCE.md`](results/VISIBLE_CONTROL_ACCEPTANCE.md).

The Browser Provider also exposes `browser_extract`, a read-only structured extraction tool. It accepts 1–40 fields with explicit `label`, `role`, `text`, or `css` locators and `string`, `number`, `boolean`, or `url` result types. `all: true` returns an array (capped at 200 values), `attribute` reads an attribute instead of element content, and `required: false` records an absent element in `missing`. An element that exists with a blank value is data, not absence: a `string` field returns `""` and is listed in `empty`, while `number`, `boolean`, and `url` fields reject a blank value as `empty_value`. Required fields whose element is absent, ambiguous locators, and values that cannot be coerced to the requested type fail closed. Results include the source URL, page title, per-field match counts, and `trusted: false`; extracted page content remains untrusted data. Extraction does not call D1 or dispatch input. Fields are read sequentially rather than as an atomic multi-field snapshot. Cancellation stops the caller's wait, but a Playwright navigation or read already in progress may still complete in the background.

```json
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/filters.html",
  "fields": [
    { "name": "adults", "type": "number", "locator": { "kind": "label", "text": "Adults" } },
    { "name": "nonstop", "type": "boolean", "locator": { "kind": "label", "text": "Nonstop only" } }
  ]
}
```

Browser control and publication tools are `browser_control` and `browser_skill_publish`; navigation, tab, upload, and download tools are `browser_navigate`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_upload`, and `browser_downloads`; native equivalents are `computer_control` and `computer_skill_publish`. The defaults are disjoint, so both providers can be mounted in one composition. `toolPrefix` changes every browser tool name (for example, `web` produces `web_extract`, `web_observe`, `web_navigate`, `web_tabs`, `web_upload`, `web_control`, and `web_skill_publish`).

Verified URL Skills are pinned to an exact HTTP(S) origin and path; built-in fixture Skills only match loopback URLs. Explicit replay at another origin stops with `skill_origin_mismatch`, and the origin is rechecked before every replay action and every successful return. Same-origin path navigation remains allowed. Every publishable Skill carries independent postconditions. Before persistence, captured input values in those assertions are replaced with `{{inputs:...}}` placeholders; replay hydrates them with the current structured inputs and checks both the Skill's assertions and the caller's `verify` assertions. Candidates whose URL, window title, or step metadata contains raw captured input are not created. Repeated text-entry steps receive collision-free per-step input keys, so redaction and replay preserve every value in order. Conflicting structured/captured values and URL-encoded representations of captured input also prevent candidate creation. Legacy records without an origin or persisted postconditions can be read for migration, but cannot be published or replayed. Native Skills use an exact `appBundleId` scope when the application supplies it, with exact `windowTitle` matching as the fallback. Built-in fixture Skills require an explicit `skillId`. Native `paste` steps preserve structured-input placeholders and use the same bounded replay path as other Skill actions.

The control page URL returned by `*_control` carries a per-server page token in a fragment; the fragment itself is not sent to the server, and the configured `controlToken` never enters a tool result. The page stores the page token in session storage and sends it as a bearer credential. The page shows current and last run state, system permission rows with settings shortcuts, Verified Skill records with removal, and the audit timeline. `browser_observe` and `browser_extract` results remain untrusted data.

The shared subgoal and safety contract is `benchmarks/computer-subgoal-v1.schema.json`. Runtime controls include credential/login gates, consequential-action confirmation, duplicate-target escalation, pending-UI waits, stale-input rejection, independent postconditions, and per-run wall-clock/input-token/output-token budgets covering model decisions, input, Skill replay, and waits. P2 adds Verified Skill → D1 → DeepSeek/human routing; every result records `route`, `skillId`, and `fallbackReason`. P3 adds candidate generation, independent rerun verification, explicit user approval, immutable publication, persistent Skill stores, and versioned evolution through `evolvedFrom` after a bounded repair. P4 adds DSH `userQuestions` approval, run control, pause/resume/stop/takeover, a localized loopback control page, and durable audit. Action approvals name the operation, target, and scope, and cover one action; login approval triggers on credential input or a sign-in click, not on merely observing a password field. Thrown permission and stale-state errors carry a stable reason and recovery text. `auditRetentionDays` configures audit retention with a 30-day default; audit and Skill files use private permissions, while decision and CUA debug logs retain structural metadata without raw goals, inputs, typed values, or screenshots. P5 completes the scenario matrix and scope decision. See `results/REAL_APP_ACCEPTANCE.md`, `results/THIRD_PARTY_ACCEPTANCE.md`, `results/P5_EVALUATION.md`, `results/P4_CONTROL.md`, `results/P3_SKILLS.md`, and `results/P2_ROUTING.md`.

Run the real-model e2e after starting the loopback decision service:

```bash
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.server \
  --port 8765 --token test-token --local-files-only

D1_DECISION_TOKEN=test-token npm run test:e2e
```

The comparison suite uses the same local flight task with scripted official Playwright MCP and the D1 Provider. Its scope is a control-layer comparison, not a DeepSeek planner comparison.

## D1 box benchmarks

```bash
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.visual_benchmark --local-files-only
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.visual_browser_benchmark --local-files-only
```

Reports:

- `results/d1-box-synthetic.json`
- `results/d1-box-browser.json`

## Official macOS CUA visual prototype

Checkout `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` at `dsh-v0.2.2-alpha.2`, then build the native helper:

```bash
swift build \
  --package-path /tmp/dsh-official-alpha2/packages/experimental/cua-macos/native \
  --configuration release
```

Run the AX-present visual evaluation and the true AX-less fallback:

```bash
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.official_cua_visual \
  --execute --local-files-only

uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.official_cua_axless_visual \
  --local-files-only
```

These commands compile and control only disposable official AppKit fixtures. They require macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions and an unlocked session. They do not change system permissions, select user applications, or use user data.

See [`results/VISUAL_DECISION_REPORT.md`](results/VISUAL_DECISION_REPORT.md) for raw metrics, native outcomes, and the bounded integration verdict.

## P0 task suite and baseline

```bash
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.workflow_e2e --local-files-only
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.browser_benchmark \
  --case login-blocked --case ambiguous-save --case delayed-results \
  --local-files-only --output results/P0_BROWSER_NEGATIVE.json
uv run python -m dsh_cu_decision.p0_report
```

The reproducible scenario catalog is `benchmarks/scenarios.json`. The generated baseline is `results/P0_BASELINE.md`; it preserves the current credential, ambiguity, and repeated-action failures instead of treating all controlled successes as production readiness.

## Agent Skill evaluation

The repository root is also an Agent Skill (`SKILL.md`) with a 12-case skill-up routing suite in `evals/`. It evaluates tool selection, control, publication, and refusal behavior, not live browser or native execution.

```bash
skill-up validate evals/eval.yaml
skill-up run evals/eval.yaml
skill-up run evals/eval.yaml --iteration 3
```

Results and limitations are in [`results/SKILL_EVAL.md`](results/SKILL_EVAL.md).

## Safety and model license

D1 is not a permission or completion authority. Fresh-state checks, application ownership, verification, and escalation remain outside the model. Current results do not justify unattended desktop control.

`d1-2B` uses the LFM Open License v1.0, not Apache-2.0 or MIT. Review the [license](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-2B/blob/main/LICENSE) before redistribution or commercial use; it includes a commercial-use revenue threshold condition.

# @askdkc/dsh-auth English | [日本語](README.ja.md) > Provider authentication for [dsh-cli](https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli) and > [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Use **ChatGPT, Claude, SuperGrok, OpenCode Zen/Go, OpenRouter, Nous Portal, and Infron** as model providers with OAuth, device code, or an API key according to the provider. No dsh source patch is needed. This plugin is developed alongside (and bundled into) [dsh-cli](https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli), the terminal front door for DeepSeek Harness; it also installs standalone into any dsh profile. ``` dsh-cli → /provider → Provider authentication → sign in /auth login openai-codex ← the plugin command /model → OpenAI Codex → gpt-5.6-sol ← routes & models ``` **Status: experimental.** Catalog OAuth flows are [pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai)'s shipped implementations (device-code and loopback callback included); this plugin adds the hosting: credential storage, automatic token refresh, adapter registration, and a login surface over the `userQuestions` seam that works in the TUI, the web client, and refuses cleanly on headless hosts. ## Install **With dsh-cli** — nothing to do: dsh-auth ships inside the dsh-cli package (bundled dependency). Update dsh-cli and the `/provider` wizard gains its provider authentication branch automatically. **Standalone, into any dsh profile:** ```sh dsh plugin --profile add @askdkc/dsh-auth ``` Then restart the host; `/` lists `auth`, and every model picker gains the signed-in providers' catalogs (credential-gated — see below). ## What it does - Mounts pi-ai catalog providers as `llm` registry routes: `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, `xai`, and `openrouter`. OpenCode Zen/Go use an owned DSH adapter with bundled Messages, Responses, Chat Completions and Google transports. **Models appear in a picker only after that provider is signed in** (credential-gated listing) — sign in and the catalog appears, sign out and it disappears. Verified current models stay resolvable after logout; retired models fail explicitly and never trigger an automatic switch. - Loads those Provider objects from the exact pi-ai dependency owned by the installed `dsh-llm-pi-ai`. rc and alpha hosts therefore keep their supported pi-ai versions without passing Provider objects across package instances. - `/auth login [provider]` runs the selected authentication method interactively. The waiting panel behaves the way pi's host does: the authorization URL is **opened in your browser automatically** (never hand-copied — the URL is hundreds of characters and wrap artifacts corrupt its `redirect_uri`), and the panel offers *Copy authorization link* / *Open browser again* / *Cancel sign-in*. Device-code flows open the verification page and make the short code the copy target. OpenAI Codex also offers a device-code login method — the most robust path on headless or locked-down machines (no localhost:1455 callback needed). - OpenCode Zen/Go accept API keys. OpenRouter offers pi-ai's OAuth PKCE flow or a manual API key. `nous` and `infron` use Chat Completions; their `/models` listings must provide capacity and pricing metadata before a model is selectable. `nous` offers device-code OAuth and an explicitly selected manual Bearer token compatibility path. The latter has not been validated against a real Nous account. - Stored access tokens refresh automatically before each request, serialized per provider under the credential store's lock — concurrent requests never double-refresh a rotated token. - `/auth status` / `/auth logout `; the `ctx.dshAuth` service exposes the same api for UIs (the dsh-cli `/provider` wizard and `/login` ride it). ## Usage ``` /auth # status: which providers are signed in /auth login # pick a provider interactively /auth login openai-codex # ChatGPT (Plus/Pro) /auth login anthropic # Claude (Pro/Max) /auth login xai # SuperGrok / X Premium /auth login opencode # OpenCode Zen API key /auth login opencode-go # OpenCode Go API key /auth login openrouter # OAuth PKCE or API key /auth login nous # device code or manual Bearer /auth login infron # Infron API key /auth logout anthropic /auth models opencode # source, last success, excluded models /auth refresh opencode # immediate catalog refresh ``` Model requests against a provider you have not signed in to fail loudly with the `/auth login ` hint — never silently. ## Configuration ```yaml - id: dsh-auth name: '@askdkc/dsh-auth' config: providers: [openai-codex, anthropic, xai, opencode, opencode-go, openrouter, nous, infron] nous: clientId: hermes-cli # infron: # serviceTier: flex # standard or flex; omit for gateway defaults # credentialsFile: /secure/path/credentials.json ``` - `credentialsFile` defaults to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-auth/credentials.json` (`~/.dsh/dsh-auth/credentials.json`), overridable with the `DSH_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` environment variable. The directory is created `0700`, the file `0600` (best-effort on Windows), and every write is atomic (temp file + rename). - Aliases `opencode-zen`, `hermes`, and `infron.ai` resolve to `opencode`, `nous`, and `infron`. Credentials are stored under canonical IDs. - The Nous client ID defaults to `hermes-cli`; third-party reuse of this ID is not guaranteed by Nous. Set `nous.clientId` if your deployment has its own. - Set `infron.serviceTier` to `standard` or `flex` to select the routing tier for all Infron models, including `z-ai/glm-5.3`. Requests send `{"provider":{"service_tier":"flex"}}` at the body root; there is no `extra_body` wrapper on the wire. Omit the setting to keep gateway defaults. Flex may fall back to Standard when unavailable; see the [Infron API reference](https://models.infron.ai/models/z-ai/glm-5.3/api-reference). - A route another adapter family already owns — an `llm-pi-ai` settings profile naming the same provider — is refused by the registry; the plugin logs the refusal and mounts the remaining routes. Keep one provider on one adapter. - OpenCode Zen/Go own their catalog and transports independently of the host's pi version. Each startup fetches the official `/models` listing and its model metadata; subsequent updates run hourly. The verified cache or bundled snapshot remains available while the request runs and if it fails. `/auth models [provider]` shows freshness and excluded model reasons; `/auth refresh [provider]` requests an update. Failed updates keep the last verified catalog. Unsupported or incomplete models are excluded individually; no sibling metadata or another route's prices are guessed. - Public catalog caches live at `$DSH_HOME/dsh-auth/catalog-v1/` and contain no credentials. Existing provider IDs, API keys and capacity overrides are retained. A new wire protocol requires a package update; new IDs on supported protocols do not require a pi update. - In auth 0.2, pi-specific construction helpers are internal to `pi-routes`; consumers should use `DshAuthApi` and the DSH adapter contract. ## Security notes - The credential file holds **API keys and long-lived refresh tokens**. It is never logged, never echoed through status surfaces (`/auth status` shows expiry metadata only), and a corrupt file fails loudly instead of being overwritten. - dsh-cli masks API-key input and redacts it from questionnaire summaries. - Login refuses to run where no interactive surface is registered (no browser/GUI assumptions — remote and headless hosts get a clear error, per the ecosystem spec's remote-determinism rule, TUI-RUN-001). - Subscription authentication and API-key access are different products: ChatGPT Codex and Claude Pro/Max use their subscription backends; the new API-key routes use each service's API backend. ## Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm verify # build + headless smoke (credential store, refresh # serialization, prompt bridging, gating, service api) ``` The smoke suite runs without cordis or a harness: the pure modules are exercised directly. Real end-to-end login needs an interactive host (dsh-cli) and is verified manually per release. The plugin is developed in the [dsh-cli repository](https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli) in the tracked `dsh-auth/` directory. Auth and CLI changes can be committed together. The initial in-repository snapshot came from [dsh-auth-fork](https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-auth-fork) commit `a48e59ec502fa0a3238c78955ffcffdfa8ae5abb`. Development and releases of this copy are now managed in dsh-cli. ## Roadmap - **M2** *(landed)* — dsh-cli integration: `/provider` OAuth branch, `/login` account section, two-level `/model` picker with a pinned recently-used group. - **M3** — `dsh-ecosystem-spec` conformance (manifest validation, admission fixtures) plus the remaining pi-ai OAuth providers (GitHub Copilot, Kimi); community list entry. - **M4** — Gemini: a custom Google device-code flow (pi-ai ships none; this is the one wheel this project plans to build itself). ## License [MIT](LICENSE). The original ccch1mneyyy copyright notice is retained; dkc is listed for the fork's independent development.

# dsh-cli > An interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness. This is dkc's independently developed fork of [dsh-TUI by chimney](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI). ## Run without Kiokuko for one launch ```sh dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko --resume ``` `dsh-cli` works independently; Kiokuko is optional. `--ignore-kiokuko` prevents `kiokuko-dsh` and its subpath plugins (including model integration) from loading for this launch, before their imports, services, tools or hooks run. It omits Kiokuko's bundle effects while preserving explicit profile, home and `--patch` overrides and other plugins. Kiokuko-provided providers/tools are unavailable. Existing session history remains; resuming does not re-enable the plugin. The option does not uninstall anything or save an opt-out setting. Temporary composition files are removed after use; the next launch without the flag uses the ordinary profile again. It is a startup option, not an unload command for an already-running session. `--dump-config` shows the effective startup tree; schema/default-only dumps and profile replacement cannot be combined with this option. If the host cannot safely compose the exclusion, startup fails with a diagnostic rather than silently loading Kiokuko. Normal host startup housekeeping and explicit in-session settings edits still follow the host's normal behavior. ## Preview
## Highlights - Streaming Markdown, tool cards, images, Mermaid diagrams, and keyboard completion. - A pixel whale, live work status, context bar, TPS gauge, and clickable timeline. - Session management with resume, fork, rewind, background work, and export. - DSH presets, skills, MCP, goals, subagents, provider authentication, and extensions. - Authentication for OpenAI, Claude, OpenCode, OpenRouter, Hermes Agent, and Infron. - Virtualized rendering and bounded caches for long sessions. - Optional scoped code analysis through the separate LSP provider; see [code-analysis setup and current acceptance limits](docs/code-intelligence.en.md). - Optional Common Lisp mode through the separate `kiokuko-dsh` plugin, which must be installed in the same profile; see [Kiokuko Lisp setup](#optional-kiokuko-lisp-mode). ## Quick Start Requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) `>=22.19.0`, pnpm 11, a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) source checkout with dependencies installed, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. We aim to support current DSH APIs. Compatibility is checked against installed packages and the upstream default branch, without a release allowlist; see [ADAPTER.md](ADAPTER.md). Clone recursively to fetch submodules. In an existing checkout, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` before installation. ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli.git cd dsh-cli pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm build node scripts/with-publish-manifest.mjs npm pack --ignore-scripts TARBALL="$PWD/askdkc-dsh-cli-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").tgz" cd ~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness pnpm dsh plugin --profile dsh-cli add "@askdkc/dsh-cli@file:${TARBALL}" pnpm dsh --profile dsh-cli ``` Replace `~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness` with your checkout path. The first interactive launch registers `dsh-cli`; open a new shell, then run it from your project directory. The managed command saves the built Harness checkout path, so a separate global DSH installation is unnecessary. Harness `plugin add` refreshes an existing managed command during updates; no manual registration is needed. An explicit `DSH_CLI_DSH_ROOT` overrides the saved path. To update this fork, rebuild and reinstall the tarball. `/update` uses the registry. Use the named `@askdkc/dsh-cli@file:...` form for local tarball updates. A bare tarball path can fail with `ENOENT` when pnpm resolves a previous `file:` dependency whose archive has been deleted. `TARBALL` holds the archive's absolute path; pass it to the install command instead of executing it. For PATH setup and install issues, see [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md). ## Optional Kiokuko Lisp mode Lisp mode is provided by the separate [`kiokuko-dsh`](https://github.com/askdkc/kiokuko-dsh) plugin. dsh-cli supplies the terminal prompt and `/kioku-lisp` command handling, but the plugin must be installed in the same DSH profile: ```sh cd ~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness pnpm dsh plugin --profile dsh-cli add kiokuko-dsh ``` Enable Lisp in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (by default `~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-cli/cordis.patch.yml`), then restart `dsh-cli`: ```yaml - id: kiokuko-dsh config: enabled: true lisp: enabled: true sbclPath: sbcl ``` A working SBCL is required; Linux also needs Bubblewrap with user, PID, and network namespaces. Profiles are isolated, so adding the plugin to another profile, such as `web`, does not enable Lisp mode in `dsh-cli`. Without the plugin, `/kioku-lisp` is unavailable and no Lisp-mode choice appears. With the plugin enabled, startup waits for it, and activation that exceeds 30 seconds stops startup with a diagnostic. After restart, `/kioku-lisp status` reports whether Lisp is available. A coding request can then offer the Lisp choice, or `/kioku-lisp enable` turns it on for the session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#optional-kiokuko-lisp-workflow) for consent, managed operations, and command timing. ## Use `Enter` sends, `Tab` completes, `Ctrl+Enter` interrupts and sends, and double `Esc` rewinds. Press `?` for shortcuts. The working-status line follows each accepted request in English, Japanese, or Chinese. Ambiguous short requests keep that session's previous progress language; `/lang` controls the rest of the interface separately. `/resume` opens the session manager; `/auth` connects providers and `/model` selects a model. `/bg` keeps a session running until the TUI exits. See [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md) for the full reference. `/model` opens a centered picker with Favorites, Recent, and provider sections. `/model seek deep` opens it with an order-independent search; an exact `/model provider/model-id` switches directly. # dsh-cli > An interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness. This is dkc's independently developed fork of [dsh-TUI by chimney](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI). ## Run without Kiokuko for one launch ```sh dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko --resume ``` `dsh-cli` works independently; Kiokuko is optional. `--ignore-kiokuko` prevents `kiokuko-dsh` and its subpath plugins (including model integration) from loading for this launch, before their imports, services, tools or hooks run. It omits Kiokuko's bundle effects while preserving explicit profile, home and `--patch` overrides and other plugins. Kiokuko-provided providers/tools are unavailable. Existing session history remains; resuming does not re-enable the plugin. The option does not uninstall anything or save an opt-out setting. Temporary composition files are removed after use; the next launch without the flag uses the ordinary profile again. It is a startup option, not an unload command for an already-running session. `--dump-config` shows the effective startup tree; schema/default-only dumps and profile replacement cannot be combined with this option. If the host cannot safely compose the exclusion, startup fails with a diagnostic rather than silently loading Kiokuko. Normal host startup housekeeping and explicit in-session settings edits still follow the host's normal behavior. ## Preview
## Highlights - Streaming Markdown, tool cards, images, Mermaid diagrams, and keyboard completion. - A pixel whale, live work status, context bar, TPS gauge, and clickable timeline. - Session management with resume, fork, rewind, background work, and export. - DSH presets, skills, MCP, goals, subagents, provider authentication, and extensions. - Authentication for OpenAI, Claude, OpenCode, OpenRouter, Hermes Agent, and Infron. - Virtualized rendering and bounded caches for long sessions. - Optional scoped code analysis through the separate LSP provider; see [code-analysis setup and current acceptance limits](docs/code-intelligence.en.md). - Optional Common Lisp mode through the separate `kiokuko-dsh` plugin, which must be installed in the same profile; see [Kiokuko Lisp setup](#optional-kiokuko-lisp-mode). ## Quick Start Requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) `>=22.19.0`, pnpm 11, a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) source checkout with dependencies installed, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. We aim to support current DSH APIs. Compatibility is checked against installed packages and the upstream default branch, without a release allowlist; see [ADAPTER.md](ADAPTER.md). Clone recursively to fetch submodules. In an existing checkout, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` before installation. ```sh git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli.git cd dsh-cli pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm build node scripts/with-publish-manifest.mjs npm pack --ignore-scripts TARBALL="$PWD/askdkc-dsh-cli-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").tgz" cd ~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness pnpm dsh plugin --profile dsh-cli add "@askdkc/dsh-cli@file:${TARBALL}" pnpm dsh --profile dsh-cli ``` Replace `~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness` with your checkout path. The first interactive launch registers `dsh-cli`; open a new shell, then run it from your project directory. The managed command saves the built Harness checkout path, so a separate global DSH installation is unnecessary. Harness `plugin add` refreshes an existing managed command during updates; no manual registration is needed. An explicit `DSH_CLI_DSH_ROOT` overrides the saved path. To update this fork, rebuild and reinstall the tarball. `/update` uses the registry. Use the named `@askdkc/dsh-cli@file:...` form for local tarball updates. A bare tarball path can fail with `ENOENT` when pnpm resolves a previous `file:` dependency whose archive has been deleted. `TARBALL` holds the archive's absolute path; pass it to the install command instead of executing it. For PATH setup and install issues, see [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md). ## Optional Kiokuko Lisp mode Lisp mode is provided by the separate [`kiokuko-dsh`](https://github.com/askdkc/kiokuko-dsh) plugin. dsh-cli supplies the terminal prompt and `/kioku-lisp` command handling, but the plugin must be installed in the same DSH profile: ```sh cd ~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness pnpm dsh plugin --profile dsh-cli add kiokuko-dsh ``` Enable Lisp in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (by default `~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-cli/cordis.patch.yml`), then restart `dsh-cli`: ```yaml - id: kiokuko-dsh config: enabled: true lisp: enabled: true sbclPath: sbcl ``` A working SBCL is required; Linux also needs Bubblewrap with user, PID, and network namespaces. Profiles are isolated, so adding the plugin to another profile, such as `web`, does not enable Lisp mode in `dsh-cli`. Without the plugin, `/kioku-lisp` is unavailable and no Lisp-mode choice appears. With the plugin enabled, startup waits for it, and activation that exceeds 30 seconds stops startup with a diagnostic. After restart, `/kioku-lisp status` reports whether Lisp is available. A coding request can then offer the Lisp choice, or `/kioku-lisp enable` turns it on for the session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#optional-kiokuko-lisp-workflow) for consent, managed operations, and command timing. ## Use `Enter` sends, `Tab` completes, `Ctrl+Enter` interrupts and sends, and double `Esc` rewinds. Press `?` for shortcuts. The working-status line follows each accepted request in English, Japanese, or Chinese. Ambiguous short requests keep that session's previous progress language; `/lang` controls the rest of the interface separately. `/resume` opens the session manager; `/auth` connects providers and `/model` selects a model. `/bg` keeps a session running until the TUI exits. See [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md) for the full reference. `/model` opens a centered picker with Favorites, Recent, and provider sections. `/model seek deep` opens it with an order-independent search; an exact `/model provider/model-id` switches directly. In the picker, use `Ctrl+F` to toggle a favorite, `Ctrl+A` to connect a provider, and `Esc` to close. To import Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversations, run `dsh-cli migrate` to see available histories, then `dsh-cli migrate [--dry-run]`. Tool traffic is not imported. See [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md). ## Documentation - [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) · [VS Code](docs/vscode.en.md) - [Interaction](docs/interaction.en.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.en.md) · [Themes](docs/themes.en.md) - [Architecture and limitations](docs/architecture.en.md) · [All docs](docs/README.md) - [Plugin development](docs/plugins.en.md) · [Contributing](docs/contributing.en.md) ## Acknowledgments The pixel whale's 22 hand-drawn frames and idle animations come from [dsh-ui-whale](https://github.com/lhh010/dsh-ui-whale) by [@lhh010](https://github.com/lhh010) (BSD-3-Clause). Thank you for the art and inspiration 🐋💜 Community projects and companion tools: [Friends' links](docs/links.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE). The original copyright notice for chimney is retained; dkc's copyright notice covers the fork's independent development.

# dsh-working-activity input-language fork This local fork starts from `dsh-working-activity` 0.5.0 (BSD-3-Clause). It adds Japanese progress copy and a per-session `lang: input` mode. The original `auto`, `zh`, and `en` modes retain their behavior. The dsh-cli workspace links this package locally; its source manifest names `@askdkc/dsh-working-activity@0.5.0-input.0` through an npm alias. Build with `npm run build:working-activity` from the dsh-cli root. The publish-manifest helper bundles the compiled fork under the runtime dependency name, so an external dsh-cli installation does not need a separate fork release. `client-snapshot/` is the unchanged 0.5.0 Web client bundle and declarations. The build copies it into `lib/` after compiling the server side, so a fresh checkout still has the existing optional Web entry. This change targets the TUI; Web client language-aware ticking is not expanded here.

Ambiguous short requests keep that session's previous progress language; `/lang` controls the rest of the interface separately. `/resume` opens the session manager; `/auth` connects providers and `/model` selects a model. `/bg` keeps a session running until the TUI exits. See [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md) for the full reference. `/model` opens a centered picker with Favorites, Recent, and provider sections. `/model seek deep` opens it with an order-independent search; an exact `/model provider/model-id` switches directly. In the picker, use `Ctrl+F` to toggle a favorite, `Ctrl+A` to connect a provider, and `Esc` to close. To import Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversations, run `dsh-cli migrate` to see available histories, then `dsh-cli migrate [--dry-run]`. Tool traffic is not imported. See [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md). ## Documentation - [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) · [VS Code](docs/vscode.en.md) - [Interaction](docs/interaction.en.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.en.md) · [Themes](docs/themes.en.md) - [Architecture and limitations](docs/architecture.en.md) · [All docs](docs/README.md) - [Plugin development](docs/plugins.en.md) · [Contributing](docs/contributing.en.md) ## Acknowledgments The pixel whale's 22 hand-drawn frames and idle animations come from [dsh-ui-whale](https://github.com/lhh010/dsh-ui-whale) by [@lhh010](https://github.com/lhh010) (BSD-3-Clause). Thank you for the art and inspiration 🐋💜 Community projects and companion tools: [Friends' links](docs/links.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE). # dsh-ask-first

A clarification button for the DeepSeek Harness composer — it asks what you meant before it rewrites anything. [中文说明](README.zh.md) · [Source](https://github.com/BAIYE0303/dsh-ask-first) Most prompt-rewriting plugins assume you can already say what you want, and only tidy up the wording. This one assumes the opposite: the draft is vague because **the person could not say it yet**. So it restates what it understood, asks two or three questions that can be answered by clicking, and only then rewrites — into a request an agent can start on without asking again. --- ![The clarification panel: a restatement, then questions with clickable options](assets/screenshot-2.png) It says what it thinks you meant, asks what would actually change the answer, and hands back a request with a goal, the constraints, and a definition of done. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ask-first ``` Or in the GUI: **Plugins → Add plugin**, and paste `dsh-ask-first`. The plugin has a browser half, so **restart the host** after installing. The button then sits at the bottom-left of the composer, on the send row. There is nothing to configure and no key to paste. ## Try it on one vague draft ### 1. Type three words, then click 说清楚点 Put something short in the composer — even "make me a page" — and click **说清楚点** (Say it clearer) before sending. The button's tooltip reads *不用会描述：点几下选项，我替你把需求问清楚*. ![The button at the bottom-left of the composer, before sending](assets/screenshot-1.png) The panel opens with the title **说清楚点** and the line **先问清楚，再发送**. Your draft is untouched, and nothing has been sent. ### 2. Read the restatement, then answer by clicking The first block in the panel is one sentence under the label **我理解你想要的是** — the model's own words for what it took from your draft. That sentence is the only thing that tells you whether it understood you, which is why it gets its own block instead of being folded into the result. Below it: **理解对了吗？下面几问点一下就行，不用打字。** Two or three questions follow, picked because their answers would change the result. Every question comes with clickable options, and every question ends with **我不知道，你替我定** — so a user who cannot answer still has a way to answer. Typing is optional throughout. Each question also takes a free-text line, labelled **或者自己写一个答法（可留空）**, and the panel says so: **不想答的留空就行；一个都不选也能直接重写。** ### 3. Take the rewrite back into the composer Click **按这些重写** and you get **正在按你的选择重写……**, then the result under **觉得可以就直接填回输入框；还能再改。**, with a character count. ![The rewritten request, ready to put back into the composer](assets/screenshot-3.png) The rewrite is one request an agent can start on: goal first, then the constraints, then what counts as done. Anything the model does not actually know stays as a visible `[待补充：…]` placeholder instead of being invented. Three buttons: **填回输入框**, **重新问一遍**, **关掉**. **It never sends.** Writing the draft back is the last thing it does; the send key stays yours. ## What distinguishes it from other prompt rewriters - **It restates before it asks** — the panel opens with *"what I understand you want is …"* in its own block, so a wrong reading is visible before you spend a rewrite on it. - **Questions you can answer without typing** — options are generated from that specific draft, not pulled from a fixed questionnaire, and the last option of every question is **我不知道，你替我定**. - **The zero-typing path is enforced in code** — if the model returns no options, or forgets the escape option, the host half adds them before the panel renders. It is not left to the prompt. - **It will not invent parameters** — anything genuinely unknown stays as `[待补充：…]`, to fill in or delete. - **It never sends** — the result goes back into the composer through `inputActions.setDraft()` and stops there. - **Your current model, no setup** — no API key, no provider config, no settings page. - **A bad model reply is not a failure** — if the answer is not parseable JSON, the raw text becomes the restatement and the panel goes straight to rewriting. ## When not to use it - **You already write clear requests.** Then every click costs you two model calls to learn nothing. - **You want the agent to just start.** This button's whole job is to ask first — the opposite of "stop asking me, go". - **You want different wording for the same request.** Tone, translation and shortening are rewrite jobs; this one changes what the request *is*. - **No LLM service is wired up in your host.** The panel says it cannot reach the local rewriter rather than producing a fake result. ## How it works Two halves, one package. | Path | Role | | --- | --- | | `lib/index.js` | Host half. Registers three loopback-only `POST` routes and makes every model call (`ctx.llm.stream`). | | `lib/client.js` | Browser half. Registers the button and the panel in the `conversation.input.left` slot, and writes the result back with `inputActions.setDraft()`. | | `cordis.patch.yml` | Lets the host insert this package into the plugin tree. | | `test-offline.mjs` | Offline self-check. No network, no host: `node test-offline.mjs`. | ### Routes | Method | Path | Body | Response | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | POST | `/api/dsh-ask-first/health` | `{}` | `{ ok, value: { llm, provider?, model? } }` | | POST | `/api/dsh-ask-first/ask` | `{ draft }` | `{ ok, value: { guess, questions: [{ id, question, hint, options[] }] } }` | | POST | `/api/dsh-ask-first/rewrite` | `{ draft, answers: [{ question, answer }] }` | `{ ok, value: { text } }` | All three accept loopback requests only: the socket address must be `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, the `Host` header must be loopback, and a request whose `Origin` points at another host — or which carries `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` — is refused with `403`. ### Which model it uses No API key, no provider config, no settings page. The plugin calls `ctx.llm.stream` with the provider and model that `agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()` reports — the same one shown in the corner of the composer. If that service is unavailable it omits both and lets the host fall back to the last target used. The honest cost: one click is **two model calls** — one to ask, one to rewrite — billed to whatever your current session is billed to. ### When the model misbehaves The model is asked for strict JSON and does not always comply. If the reply cannot be parsed, that is not an error: the raw text becomes the "what I understand you want" sentence and the panel goes straight to rewriting. Questions are capped at three, options at four, and long fields are truncated, so a runaway reply cannot wreck the panel. --- The rest of this file is for people checking the package, not for people deciding whether to install it. ## Self-check ```bash node test-offline.mjs ``` 39 checks, no network and no host process: route registration, request validation, JSON extraction from fenced replies, option normalisation, cross-site rejection, and the request body sent to the model. ## Notes for reviewers - `lib/client.js` is a single `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` wrapper. That is the standard shape for a DeepSeek Harness client plugin, not a bundler artefact: the module body is plain readable source, unminified, and the only `require` calls are `react` and `react-dom`, which the host provides. - No credentials, no telemetry, no outbound requests. The only network calls are the loopback routes above, and the only model calls go through the host's own `ctx.llm` service. - No install-time scripts. - `preview/shot.html` is the page the README screenshots were taken from. It loads the real `lib/client.js` against a stub host and a stub backend, so the shots show the actual panel. It is not part of the published package (see `files` in `package.json`), and it needs a React UMD build in `preview/vendor/` to run — that directory is git-ignored, fetch it from jsDelivr if you want to regenerate shots. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT npm version gitHead matches the fixed source; versioned DSH engines and peers are explicit. Native host/client entries are captured. POST handlers check loopback address, allowed Host, Origin and fetch-site; configured LLM calls rewrite the draft without sending it automatically. Local-process trust and model data transfer remain risks. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
