# dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp **DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 插件：通过 Google ACP 协议接入 Antigravity 运行时与 Gemini 3.x 模型** [简体中文](README.md) · [English](README_en.md) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-Plugin-blue.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.1.0-brightgreen.svg)](package.json) [![ACP SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/@agentclientprotocol/sdk-v1.8.0-purple.svg)](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol)
--- ## 简介 `dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp` 是 DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 的扩展插件。通过标准的 ACP (Agent Client Protocol) 协议连接 Google Antigravity 运行时，让 DSH 可以直接调用 Gemini 3.8 Flash 模型。 插件自带设置页面和后台服务，安装后通过 Google 官方 OAuth 授权登录即可使用，支持思维链推理展开、流式输出、输入框左侧额度与 1M 上下文实时看板、ACP 思考轨迹与计划同步，以及跨进程失效透明自愈。 --- ## 特性 - **输入框模型旁额度与 Context 看板**：在聊天窗口底部模型选择框左侧常驻展示额度胶囊（`⚡ 5h 95% | 上下文 7.2%`），悬停自动展开 Popover 浮层，鼠标移出 300ms 平滑隐藏，避免遮挡聊天输入区。 - **5 小时滚动周期与倒计时**：清晰呈现 Google 官方独特的 5 小时动态滑动窗口（5-Hour Rolling Window）机制与精准重置倒计时，解除周重置误解。 - **1M 上下文占用与超限告警**：基于 Gemini 3.8 Flash 的 1,048,576 Token 上限，实时计算已占比例；当超过 75% 时主动呈现高危黄色/红色警示卡片，提醒及时归档或压缩会话。 - **DSH 轨迹原生工具调用发射**：重构流式事件映射器，完整实现 DSH 官方原生的 `block-start` (`blockType: 'tool-call'`)、`tool-call-delta` 与 `block-end` 协议，彻底解决 DSH 轨迹看板中「0 工具调用」统计缺失的问题，工具名与参数清晰可查。 - **ACP 轨迹跟踪与思维链**：将 ACP 运行时的思考过程（Reasoning Delta）、工具执行（Tool Calls）、代码补丁（Diff）与计划（Plan）完整映射并流入 DSH 思考链与轨迹面板，调试排错一目了然。 - **上下文自动保全与系统时间戳穿透**：智能识别并穿透 DSH 系统注入消息（如 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context` 时间戳），精准提纯用户真实提问，彻底解决多轮对话历史丢失或答非所问问题。 - **跨进程会话失效透明自愈（Auto-Recovery）**：当遇到 DSH 客户端退出重启、服务重启或服务端 Session 过期（`Session not found / code: -32603`）时，自动静默创建新会话并打包前序历史完成重试，无感自愈，彻底杜绝 `Internal error` 报错。 - **自带设置界面**：安装后自动在 DSH【设置】->【插件】顶部注入专属「Google Antigravity」标签页，并在设置侧边栏提供独立入口，无需手动修改配置文件。 - **自动下载官方运行时**：无需手动安装 Python、GCC 或配置编译环境。首次运行时自动识别系统（Windows / macOS / Linux），从 Google 官方 CDN 下载对应架构的 `agy_acp_server` 并校验 SHA256。 - **官方 OAuth 2.0 个人授权**：支持 ACP `oauth-personal` 流程。点击登录后调用系统默认浏览器打开 Google 官方页面授权，无需手动抓取 Cookie 或填写 API Key，插件不接触账号密码明文。 - **本地存储与隐私安全**：无第三方中转服务器，无遥测埋点。授权凭证仅保存在本机 `~/.gemini/antigravity-acp/` 目录，请求由本地进程直连 Google 官方接口。 --- ## 版本更新日志 (Changelog) ### v1.1.0 (2026-10-31) - **全量解锁 Google Antigravity 官方模型矩阵（Full Model Matrix Matrix Unlock）**： - 重构模型注册机制，解除单一模型硬编码限制，支持完整 9 款核心旗舰模型（Gemini 3.8 Flash、Gemini 2.5 Pro、Gemini 2.5 Flash Thinking、Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite、Claude Opus 4.6 Thinking、Claude Sonnet 4.6、GPT-OSS 120B 等）； - 支持动态上游端点探针与标准矩阵自动合并排重，无缝透传 ACP 多模型切换选项。 - **Token 记账、真实上下文比例与缓存精度校准（Accurate Context & Token Accounting）**： - 修复 0% 上下文比例异常计算，消除伪缓存失真，确保 5H 滑动窗口与周配额真实精准呈现。 - **生产级架构加固与韧性管道（Architecture Hardening & Resilience Pipeline）**： - 落地流式传输背压水线保护（Backpressure Guard），防止海量数据冲击； - 引入配额 429 断路器与超时熔断；实现异步防抖与原子级安全会话持久化。 ### v1.0.15 (2026-10-31) - **架构加固与生产级管道背压保护**： - 完成全面架构审计加固，集成流式队列高低水位保护与会话原子持久化； - 构建全链路单元测试套件（32 个全绿 Vitest 用例）。 ### v1.0.14 (2026-10-31) - **Token 暴涨与 49% 缓存命中率失真根治（Token Multiplier & Cache Accounting Fix）**： - 阻断流式中间工具步高频发射全局 `usage` 数据块，解决 DSH `addUsage` 累加器将单步累积水位重复叠加数十次导致单轮飙升 10M+、全会话虚增至 120M 的假账问题； - 修正底层 Token 记账算式（`total = input + output`，剔除把 `cachedTokens` 作为独立加数的双重叠加），恢复真实 **85%~95%+** 缓存命中率。 - **历史上下文脱敏与工具输出折叠（Context De-bloating & Pruning）**： - 历史回溯自动折叠既往 Assistant 轮次中动辄数千行的原生工具控制台输出代码块（`> \`\`\`...`），防止多轮历史滚雪球式打爆上下文； - 纯化用户真实提问，剔除 DSH `` 冗余标签与空转时间戳元数据。 - **真实周配额接口对接与木桶短板约束（Official Quota & Constrained Engine）**： - 对接 Google 官方主力端点 `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary`（带多级备用降级），淘汰假数据与硬编码； - 参考 `Antigravity-Manager` 机制，实现 5H 削峰速率窗口与 7 天周配额的双向木桶短板约束、周总额度熔断（`isWeeklyExhausted`）与 5H 冷却标识（`is5hCooling`）； - 悬浮卡片中呈现 **🔷 Gemini 官方核心模型池** 与 **🟣 Claude & GPT 托管模型池** 全量分组健康看板。 ### v1.0.13 (2026-10-31) - **浅色与深色模式自适应适配（Light & Dark Theme Parity）**： - 重构底栏状态胶囊（Pill）与悬浮框 Popover 的全部样式 token，全面对齐 DSH 官方规范（`--dsw-alias-label-primary`、`--dsw-alias-label-secondary`、`--dsw-alias-fill-tsp-*`）； - 彻底修复在 DSH 浅色主题下文字发白、5H与周配额看不清、悬浮框卡片与进度条槽底隐形的问题，深浅色主题自由无缝切换。 - **全模态多模态视觉图片识别支持（Vision / Multimodal Support）**： - 在模型声明中正式开启多模态输入能力（`inputModalities: ["text", "image"]`），彻底消除 DSH 发送图片时「当前模型不支持图片」的拦截提示； - 后端打通 DSH `attachments` 服务与 ACP `ContentBlock::Image` 传输链路，支持通过拖拽、点击上传和剪贴板粘贴向 Gemini 3.8 Flash 发送图片进行视觉理解与问答，与官方 `antigravity.exe` 完全一致。 ### v1.0.12 (2026-10-31) - **工具调用步骤序号归一化**： - 引入 `AcpStepTracker`，将 Antigravity ACP 内部的轨迹步数（底层将首轮初始分析作为 Step 1，首个工具作为 Step 2）按用户交互轮次统一规整为从直观的 `[步骤 #1]` 开始自增计数； - 保证工具执行与状态更新严格对齐 `[步骤 #N]` 与 `[步骤 #N 完成]`。 - **Slot 精简（仅保留底栏 Dock）**： - 移除输入框控制栏内部右侧重复的 slot 挂载，仅保留最下方状态底栏（`conversation.composer.dock`）的单胶囊展示，界面清爽统一。 - **额度展示深度优化（对标 GitHub 社区主流项目）**： - 彻底移除冗余的上下文百分比（`上下文 100%`）与 1M 上下文占用进度条、警报及 Token 记账卡片； - 胶囊与 Popover 浮层全面聚焦双重配额：**5小时滑动速率窗口**（实时百分比、进度条、平滑恢复倒计时）与 **7天自然周配额**（周重置时间点与剩余倒计时看板）。 ### v1.0.10 (2026-10-30) - **新增周额度结算时间与倒计时看板**： - 后端实现 Google 官方自然周结算点（每周一 00:00 UTC / 北京时间周一 08:00）精准算法，输出自然周重置倒计时（`X天X小时X分`）； - 额度 Popover 浮层升级为「5小时滑动速率窗口」与「自然周额度重置」双重周期看板。 - **全状态常驻双 Slot 挂载（解决额度面板被隐藏问题）**： - 除了输入框右侧（`conversation.input.right`）外，同时挂载到 DSH 底栏状态条（`conversation.composer.dock`）； - 彻底解决任务运行/深度求索期间（`activity === true`）输入框控制组被 DSH `hidden: activity` 隐藏导致胶囊不可见的问题，全生命周期常驻可见。 - **方案 A 结构化思维链与防 Token 爆炸护甲**： - 优化 Antigravity 自治 Agent 的工具调度、参数摘要与代码 diff 的卡片式结构化输出； - 增设工具超长输出熔断保护（单工具最大 1,200 字符限制），自动截断冗余文本，杜绝巨量长命令输出打爆会话 Token 与 API 网关长连接。 ### v1.0.9 (2026-10-30) - **修复工具调用导致的 `unknown tool` 异常与报告消失**： - 彻底阻断对外层 DSH 调度器发射未注册工具块（`blockType: 'tool-call'`），将 ACP 内部工具执行完整收拢流入思维链轨迹； - 彻底修复 `DshStreamWriter` 状态机 Block Index 冲突，防止 index: 1 文本槽位被冲刷覆盖； - 解决 PTC 模式下因宿主调度失败导致的多轮空转死循环与 5M+ Token 异常消耗。 ### v1.0.8 (2026-10-30) - **工具调用原生轨迹发射**：重构 `DshStreamWriter`，实现官方 `blockType: 'tool-call'` 结构化流式发射，修复 DSH 轨迹看板中工具调用显示为 0、无详细工具名和参数的问题。 - **浮层交互易用性提升**：浮窗支持鼠标离开 300ms 后平滑自动隐藏；底栏胶囊支持悬停自动展开，彻底杜绝浮窗遮挡聊天发送区域。 - **额度恢复机制详解**：浮窗新增「Google 5 小时动态滑动窗口（5-Hour Rolling Window）」机制卡片与实时重置倒计时，明确非自然周重置规则。 - **1M 上下文超限健康预警**：当单会话上下文突破 75%（>78万 Tokens）时主动弹出警示卡片，提示 Google API 硬顶崩溃风险与上下文压缩建议。 ### v1.0.7 (2026-10-30) - **跨进程 Session 失效透明自愈**：解决 DSH 重启或服务端过期导致的 `Session not found / code: -32603` 内部错误。 - **时间戳穿透与历史净化**：穿透 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context` 注入的消息并纯化真实上下文。 ### v1.0.6 (2026-10-30) - **输入框模型旁额度与 Context 看板**：首发常驻底栏胶囊，展示 5h 额度、1M 上下文占用比例与输入/输出/思考 Token 记账。 --- ## 安装 ### 方式 1：在 DSH 界面中安装（推荐） 1. 打开 DSH 桌面端； 2. 进入【设置】->【插件】； 3. 在安装输入框中粘贴仓库地址： ```text https://github.com/Lovexiaoxiaowo/dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp ``` 4. 点击【安装】，等待安装完成。 --- ### 方式 2：通过命令行安装 在终端执行： ```bash dsh plugin add https://github.com/Lovexiaoxiaowo/dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp ``` --- ## 使用步骤 ```mermaid flowchart LR A[安装插件] --> B[进入设置 -> Google Antigravity 页面] B --> C[点击【一键登录 Google】完成授权] C --> D[聊天窗口选择 Gemini 3.8 Flash 开始使用] D --> E[查看左侧额度与 1M 上下文胶囊面板] ``` 1. **打开设置面板**：安装完成后，进入 DSH【设置】->【插件】-> 顶部【Google Antigravity】标签页（或左侧导航栏的【Google Antigravity】入口）。 2. **完成 Google 授权**：在面板中点击【一键登录 Google】，系统会打开浏览器前往 Google 官方登录页。授权完成后返回 DSH，面板会更新为已连接状态。 3. **选择模型并使用**：新建或打开任意对话，在模型下拉列表中选择 `Gemini 3.8 Flash (Antigravity)`，即可开始对话。 4. **实时看板交互**：在输入框右下方模型选择器左侧，点击 `⚡ 5h 95% | 上下文 x%` 胶囊，即可随时查看当前额度倒计时与 Token 消耗。 --- ## 安全性与方案对比 | 项目 | 常见网页抓取 / 第三方镜像方案 | 本插件 (dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **接入协议** | 模拟网页请求、逆向非公开接口 | Google 官方规范 ACP (Agent Client Protocol) | | **可执行文件** | 来源不明的第三方二进制 | Google 官方 CDN 签名发布 + SHA256 完整性校验 | | **认证方式** | 提取 Cookie 或私有 Session Token | Google 官方标准 OAuth 2.0 个人应用授权 | | **数据链路** | 经第三方中转服务器，存在泄露风险 | 零中间服务器，本地进程直连 Google 官方接口 | | **风控与安全** | 容易触发平台风控导致封号 | 走官方授权通道，正常个人应用调用 | --- ## 版本历史 (Changelog) ### v1.0.7 - **跨进程失效全自动静默自愈**：底层捕获 `Session not found` 及 `-32603` 内部错误时，自动清理陈旧 Session、重新创建 ACP 实例并打包历史重新执行，彻底杜绝客户端重启后的 `Internal error` 报错。 - **任务防挂起清理**：排查并彻底清除多余后台挂起任务。 ### v1.0.6 - **穿透 DSH 系统时间戳**：精准识别并穿透 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context` 注入的时间消息，锁定用户真实提问，彻底根治“答非所问/上下文错位”问题。 - **修复 1M 模型匹配与 Token 虚标**：精准过滤 16K 代码补全小模型，准确绑定 1,048,576（1M）真实上下文；修正高频流式通知累加导致的 350 万 Token 虚标与 100% 爆表假象。 ### v1.0.5 - **全新额度与上下文胶囊看板**：在输入框模型下拉框左侧注入原生交互胶囊与 Popover 浮层，提供 5 小时额度滑动窗口、重置倒计时及 Token 明细。 - **ACP 轨迹映射**：支持将 ACP 的 Plan 规划与 Tool 轨迹流式同步至 DSH 思考链。 - **持久化会话管理器**：实现 `DshSessionManager`，保障多轮对话连贯。 ### v1.0.4 & 早期版本 - 修复重复标签页唤起与多平台二进制下载自举，支持标准 OAuth 2.0 授权。 --- ## 常见问题 ### Q1：安装或更新插件后，为什么聊天界面没有出现模型？ - **原因**：Windows 桌面端点击窗口右上角 `X` 默认最小化到系统托盘，旧进程仍在后台运行。 - **解决方式**：在任务栏右下角托盘找到 DSH 图标，右键选择【退出】，然后重新打开 DSH 即可。 ### Q2：为什么未授权时在模型列表中看不到 Antigravity？ - **原因**：为避免未登录时请求报错，插件只在完成 Google 授权后才会向聊天列表注入可用模型。 ### Q3：支持哪些操作系统？ - 支持 Windows (x64 / arm64)、macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel)、Linux (x64 / arm64)。启动时会自动识别平台并下载对应二进制文件。 --- ## 项目结构 ``` dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp/ ├── cordis.patch.yml # DSH bundle patch 规范声明 ├── dsh/ │ └── client.js # DSH 前端扩展（向设置页与输入框底栏注入 UI） ├── src/ │ ├── index.ts # 插件服务入口、LlmAdapter 注册、Web 路由与自愈状态机 │ ├── bootstrapper.ts # 官方二进制跨平台下载与 SHA256 校验 │ ├── auth.ts # OAuth 凭据管理、本地存储与 Token 刷新 │ ├── acp-client.ts # @agentclientprotocol/sdk 双向通信与流式处理 │ ├── quota-service.ts # Google 账号配额与 Tier 状态查询 │ ├── session-manager.ts # 会话生命周期、真实提问提取与上下文绑定 │ ├── event-mapper.ts # ACP 协议事件转 DSH 流式事件 │ └── runtime-manifest.json # 官方下载源与哈希列表 ├── dist/ # 预编译产物（包含在仓库中，无需本地编译） ├── package.json ├── README.md # 中文说明文档（默认） └── README_en.md # 英文说明文档 ``` --- ## 参与贡献 欢迎提交 Issue 和 Pull Request： - 项目仓库：[GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Lovexiaoxiaowo/dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp) - 问题反馈：[Issues Tracker](https://github.com/Lovexiaoxiaowo/dsh-plugin-antigravity-acp/issues) --- ## 开源协议 本项目采用 [MIT License](LICENSE) 协议。

# 按需规划模式介绍

## 1. 一句话概述

**作者从reasonix得到的灵感，实现权限控制+子代理角色分配的agent模板**

**兼容性**：DSH = v0.2.1-rc.1 ~ v0.2.1-rc.5、dsh-qqbot 0.5.2。旧版本兼容详见Releases

## 2. 核心优势

通过设定 主会话、探查者、pro规划、执行者、验收者 五个角色，让DSH工作时按照明确的流程进行分工
  - 主会话：作为与用户直接交互的入口，负责日常沟通、需求接收与任务分派。它是整个工作流的发起者和协调者，确保用户意图被准确传达
  - 探查者：承担后台批量数据探查与线索回传工作。主动运行，将原始信息预处理后再转交主会话，有效避免主会话上下文过载，保持对话轻量与高效
  - pro规划：调用高级模型对用户需求进行深度分析与结构化规划，输出包含实施方案和验收标准的正式文档。为后续执行与验收提供权威依据
  - 执行者：严格按照规划方案进行机械式执行，并在每一步操作中持续对照验收文档，确保过程与预期一致，最大限度降低人为偏差
  - 验收者：严格按照验收方案进行机械式执行，确保最终交付物完全符合既定质量要求

并合并了DSH Agent预设模式中的 PTC模式、创造模式 包含的功能，可以直接在本模式同时体验
  - PTC模式：将多个工具调用合并为一次执行，大幅减少与模型的交互轮次，显著降低了重复传输的冗余开销。手动切换开关
  - 创造模式：创建自定义Agent preset时自动遵守DSH规范。手动切换开关

## 3. 安装及卸载方式（面向 DSH 环境用户）

### 核心安装

1. dsh web - 插件 - 添加插件 - https://github.com/luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan#path:/plugins/dsh-extra-plan 或 [解压路径]/dsh-extra-plan-main/plugins/dsh-extra-plan - 允许脚本并重试 - 立即启用
2. **重启 DSH 进程**使插件生效
3. 新建会话，在预设列表中选择「按需规划模式」

### qqbot兼容插件安装

1. 安装
```powershell 7+ 在线
dsh plugin --profile qqbot add 'luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan#path:/plugins/dsh-extra-plan-qqbot' --allow-build='dsh-extra-plan-qqbot@git+https://github.com/luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan.git'

if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
    dsh plugin --profile qqbot rebuild dsh-extra-plan-qqbot
}
```
```powershell 7+ 离线
$pkg = (Resolve-Path '[解压路径]\dsh-extra-plan-main\plugins\dsh-extra-plan-qqbot').Path -replace '\\', '/'

dsh plugin --profile qqbot add "file:///$pkg" --preserve-absolute-paths --allow-build="dsh-extra-plan-qqbot@file:$pkg"

if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
    dsh plugin --profile qqbot rebuild dsh-extra-plan-qqbot
}
```
2. **重启 DSH 进程**使插件生效
3. qqbot下使用 /preset 切换预设

### 卸载步骤

1. 核心卸载
```powershell 7+
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-extra-plan
```
2. qqbot兼容插件卸载 (如装)
```powershell 7+
dsh plugin --profile qqbot remove dsh-extra-plan-qqbot
```

    手动删除qqbot环境下的文件夹：dsh-extra-plan

4. **重启 DSH 进程**

### 平台实测说明

仅在 **Windows 环境实测正常**，**Linux/macOS 尚未在真实环境验证**

## 4. 可配置项

DSH web界面 -> 插件 -> 按需规划模式配置

**通用设置**：
  - 首轮引导开关：首轮极简工具 + 提示词
  - 创造模式开关：是否开启dsh官方创造模式
  - web_fetch开关：是否开启web_fetch
  - 工具呈现模式：工具呈现方式切换（默认/PTC模式），无法进行会话内切换
  - run_code 容错检查：PTC模式下，增加每个工具调用需要try catch的闸门。通过限制+建议的模式保障仅单个调用报错

**pro规划**：
  - 跨提供方：允许跨提供方选择模型。开启时将以 其他提供方 - 主会话提供方 - deepseek官方 的顺序，获取可用模型。关闭时仅从主会话提供方获取。默认关闭
  - pro规划 | 使用模型：pro规划默认使用模型。未匹配/置空时：使用主会话模型

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Tool Guardian

Seven MCP servers for 1,084 tokens instead of 20,005 — and tool results that stop flooding the window.

One MCP server in front of all your others. Tested with Claude Code, OpenCode, Cline and Continue (one scripted-model turn per client, see Works with); Claude Desktop, Cursor and other stdio MCP clients: expected, not yet tested.

mcp-name: io.github.LuminariSoftwares/tool-guardian The headline is this repo's bench, run against the recorded `tools/list` answers of seven public MCP servers (no network, no model; abridged where marked): ```text $ python bench/bench_tokens.py # Tool-Guardian Token Benchmark Token counting method: estimate:chars/3.5 | server | tools | tokens (full schemas) | ... | **Total** | **95** | **20005** | **Every request:** 20005 tokens of tool schemas without tool-guardian, 1084 with it (94.6% less). ```

Quick start · Works with · DeepSeek Harness · Install both · First 5 minutes · Why · Two ways to run it · Architecture · Install · Measure it · Output ladder · DSH bundle · Compatibility · Changelog

An MCP server that sits in front of your other MCP servers and exposes **6 router tools** (8 with [skills](#skills)) instead of dozens of specific ones: four generic ones to list, search, describe and call the tools behind it, plus two for tool-group costs and archived results (see [Tools](#tools)) — discovering the rest **on demand** — so tool definitions stop eating your context window before the model reads a word. The router never talks to the model backend, so it does not matter whether Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or llama.cpp serves your model; what matters is that your client's model calls tools (run with Ollama; the others expected, not yet tested). Companion to [Context Guardian](https://github.com/LuminariSoftwares/context-guardian): **Context Guardian compacts the conversation before the window fills; Tool Guardian keeps the tools from filling it in the first place.** Two halves of the same problem. | | Without Tool Guardian | With it | |---|---|---| | 7 MCP servers on a 32K model ([bench](#measured-savings)) | **20,005 tokens** of schemas on every request (61 % of the window) | **1,084 tokens** (3 %); a schema is fetched only when the model asks | | A 3,000-line build log with one error ([bench](#measured-savings)) | 115,945 characters land in the conversation | **4,540 characters**, the full original archived and one call away | | A backend that fails to start | an empty tool list the model silently works around | status `UNKNOWN` plus the real error (e.g. `could not start: …`), never an empty list | ## Quick start (60 seconds) Or tell your coding agent: `Install tool-guardian (docs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuminariSoftwares/tool-guardian/main/llms.txt) and route my MCP servers through it.` Nothing to install: [`uvx`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) runs it from PyPI. The example server below is the MCP filesystem server, which runs with `npx`, so that one line needs Node.js — the router itself is Python 3.9+ and standard library only. ```bash uvx tool-guardian --version uvx --from tool-guardian tool-guardian-setup add files -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem "$HOME" uvx tool-guardian --selftest claude mcp add --scope user tool-guardian -- uvx tool-guardian # or any client: see "Run" below ``` Prefer it installed? `pip install tool-guardian`, then drop the `uvx` prefixes (`tool-guardian-setup add ...`, `tool-guardian --selftest`). Success looks like `added 'files' to ~/.tool-guardian/mcp.json`, then from `--selftest` `1 backend(s) up, 14 tools reachable.` and a `router tools cost ~N tokens vs ~M` line. Already have servers in Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf? `tool-guardian-setup import` copies them instead of `add`. In the client, ask for something one of your servers does; the model should call `list_capabilities` (or `search_capabilities`) and then `call_tool`. ### What it looks like in practice A real session against two servers (`files` and `git`), abridged only where marked. The model asks for the catalogue, narrows to one server, checks one tool's arguments, then calls it: ``` > list_capabilities() [files] 14 tools: read_file, read_text_file, read_media_file, read_multiple_files, write_file, edit_file, create_directory, list_directory, list_directory_with_sizes, directory_tree, move_file, search_files, get_file_info, list_allowed_directories [git] 12 tools: git_status, git_diff_unstaged, git_diff_staged, git_diff, git_commit, git_add, git_reset, git_log, git_create_branch, git_checkout, git_show, git_branch NEXT STEP: use search_capabilities with a keyword (or list_capabilities with one server name) to see a tool's args, then call_tool. > list_capabilities(server="files") files.read_file: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file... args: path:string, ?tail:number, ?head:number files.read_text_file: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as... args: path:string, ?tail:number, ?head:number ... 11 more tools ... files.list_allowed_directories: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access.... args: (no arguments) NEXT STEP: you have not answered the user yet. Pick the tool above that does the job and use call_tool with server files, that tool's name, and the args listed under it. > describe_tool(server="files", tool="read_text_file") files.read_text_file: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as... required args: path:string NEXT STEP: use call_tool with server files, tool read_text_file, args: path:string, ?tail:number, ?head:number. > call_tool(server="files", tool="read_text_file", args={"path": "project/README.txt"}) hello from tool-guardian NEXT STEP: answer the user from this result. ``` Only the router's own six tools were in the model's context the whole time; the 26 backend tools were never sent. ## When *not* to use the router It is the wrong tool in two cases, and saying so is cheaper than finding out: - **Your client already searches tools for you.** Some clients (and some model APIs) load tool definitions on demand themselves. Putting a router under that adds a hop and a second catalogue for no saving. - **You run a handful of small servers.** The router's own tools cost about 1,100 tokens of `tools/list`; one small server behind it is close to break-even (`--selftest` prints the real arithmetic for *your* servers before you commit to it). The saving grows with every server added and is largest where it matters most — a 32K local model with half a dozen servers. It also does not help if your model will not call tools reliably in the first place: see [Model requirement](#model-requirement-read-this-before-you-switch). ## Works with `pip install tool-guardian`, then one entry in your client. Every example below starts the same command, `tool-guardian`, which reads `~/.tool-guardian/mcp.json`: `tool-guardian-setup import` fills it from the servers you already use. | Client | Example | Where it goes | Tested | |---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | [`project.mcp.json`](examples/claude-code/project.mcp.json), hook: [`settings.json`](examples/claude-code/settings.json), [notes](examples/claude-code/README.md) | `claude mcp add --scope user tool-guardian -- uvx tool-guardian`, or copy to `.mcp.json` in a project (Claude Code asks once to approve a project server — that file is the client's config, not the router's) ; the hook goes in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.json` | 2.1.296: full turn; hook in a live session | | **OpenCode** | [`opencode.json`](examples/opencode/opencode.json) | `opencode.json` in the project, or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | 1.18.35: full turn | | **Cline** | [`cline_mcp_settings.json`](examples/cline/cline_mcp_settings.json) | VS Code: Cline → MCP Servers → Configure MCP Servers; CLI: `~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json` | CLI 3.0.70: full turn | | **Continue** | [`tool-guardian.yaml`](examples/continue/tool-guardian.yaml) | `.continue/mcpServers/` in the workspace (IDE), or its `mcpServers` entry in `config.yaml` | `cn` 1.5.47: full turn (entry in `config.yaml`) | **What "full turn" means.** On Linux, 2026-10-10, each client got the example's `tool-guardian` entry unchanged (Claude Code through `claude mcp add-json`; OpenCode and Continue with a test model provider added beside it; Cline the file as is) and talked to a scripted model ([`tests/clients/mock_model.py`](tests/clients/mock_model.py), no real model, no API key). The client sent tool-guardian's router tools to the model. The model's `list_capabilities` call went through tool-guardian to a stub MCP server, and the answer came back to the model. tool-guardian's call log recorded the client by name (`claude-code`, `opencode`, `@cline/core`, `continue-cli-client`). Re-run it: `pip install -e .` then `python tests/clients/run_clients.py`. This proves the wiring, not that *your* model will use the router: see [Model requirement](#model-requirement-read-this-before-you-switch). **The Claude Code hook in a live session.** The hook command from [`settings.json`](examples/claude-code/settings.json) with `--mode deny` added (wrapped to record its input) blocked a Bash call naming a router tool inside a running Claude Code 2.1.296 session. Claude Code showed the hook's reason, `Use call_tool(server="probe", tool="tg_live_probe_tool", args={...}) instead of the shell`, and the call log got its `bypass` row. The payload Claude Code sent is a test fixture now ([`tests/test_claude_code_hook.py`](tests/test_claude_code_hook.py)), next to the example from Claude Code's hook docs. Not tested yet: the Cline VS Code extension (same file name and shape; tested through the Cline CLI), Continue's `.continue/mcpServers/` folder (read by the IDE extension; `cn` reads only `config.yaml`), and client runs on Windows or macOS (the unit tests run on all three in CI). On Windows, if a client cannot find `tool-guardian`, put the full path from `where tool-guardian` in the `command`. ## DeepSeek Harness results

Tool Guardian also ships as a native [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle, `dsh-tool-guardian` ([what it adds](#native-deepseek-harness-dsh-bundle)). These two figures come from DSH runs only and are not reproduced by anything in this repo: - **Sessions that ended on a tool call written as text instead of made: 7/16 → 0/32** — DeepSeek Harness (version not recorded), qwen3-coder:30b, 8 tasks; 16 sessions (8 × 2) on dsh-tool-guardian 0.4.0-beta.2, 32 sessions (8 × 4) on 0.5.0-beta.1; the repair runs in the DSH bundle only; measured by the author, script and raw runs not yet published (see the 0.5.0-beta.1 entry of the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)); not yet measured on other setups. - **DSH first request:** 46 tools and 37,154 characters of schema without the bundle, 22 tools and 18,503 characters with it — one DSH setup, measured by the author, script not yet published. ## Install both (DeepSeek Harness, about 5 minutes) Context Guardian and Tool Guardian are two halves of one problem: **Tool Guardian** keeps tool schemas and tool results from filling the window, and **Context Guardian** compacts the conversation before it fills and keeps what matters. They share no files and install separately. You need DSH 0.1.2-alpha.2 or later, Node.js `^22.19` or `>=24`, and Python 3.9+ on `PATH` for Tool Guardian's router. ```bash # 1. Add both bundles to the DSH profile you use (`web` is the one `dsh web` uses) dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tool-guardian dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-context-guardian # 2. Tool Guardian: copy in the MCP servers you already use (Claude Desktop / Cursor / Windsurf / .mcp.json), then check them cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-tool-guardian # Windows: cd %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-tool-guardian npm run setup # asks before it writes ~/.tool-guardian/mcp.json, then prints a doctor report # 3. Context Guardian: add its compaction row to your agent preset (a dry run until --apply) cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-context-guardian # Windows: cd %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-context-guardian npm run setup npm run setup -- --apply # 4. Start DSH and open a NEW session with the preset setup named dsh web ``` In that session, type `/guardian`. It shows Context Guardian's engine revision and your model's window. Then type `/toolguardian`. It shows each MCP server Tool Guardian started, the tokens the router saves on every request, and whether an update is out. Not on DSH? Context Guardian's proxy (`python context_guardian.py`, see its README) works with any OpenAI-compatible CLI. Tool Guardian runs as a plain MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client (see its README). New to it? [Your first 5 minutes](docs/first-5-minutes.md) goes from nothing installed to proof that your model uses the router, on DSH or Claude Code. ## Why this exists MCP tool definitions are re-sent on **every single request**, whether the model touches them or not. A handful of servers routinely comes to tens of thousands of tokens — often most of a small local model's window — before the first user message. On one real setup, seven MCP servers came to **28,689 tokens, 87.6% of a 32K window**, as a fixed floor under everything else. You have two ways to deal with that today, and both cost you something: | Approach | The cost | |---|---| | Load fewer MCP servers | You lose the capability entirely | | Live with it | Two-thirds of the window is gone before you type | Tool Guardian is a third option that costs neither. It fronts all your servers and shows the model just a handful of small tools plus a one-line catalogue of server names (1,084 tokens with seven servers behind it, measured below). The full schema for a tool is fetched only when the model asks for it: ``` list_capabilities(server?) one line per tool — names and purpose describe_tool(server, tool) the full argument schema for ONE tool call_tool(server, tool, args) invoke it, return the result ``` Same idea as a search index: cheap catalogue always visible, detail on demand. Every tool carries the MCP annotations (`title`, `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). All of them are read-only except `call_tool`, which is marked destructive and open-world because it runs whatever the backend tool does; the DSH bundle's `tg__*` direct tools carry the same values. ## Model requirement (read this before you switch) The whole design rests on one behaviour: the model must **proactively call `list_capabilities` (then `call_tool`) when it needs a tool.** Capable/frontier models do this reliably. Small local models are less certain — and, as the two measurements below show, **the harness the model runs in matters as much as the model.** **Measurement 1 — August 2026, OpenClaude, router mounted over MCP.** Against a real multi-server stack, **gpt-oss:20b and qwen3-30b-a3b both bypassed the router** on ordinary tasks — even with the `NEXT STEP` nudge in every result *and* a dedicated router sub-agent priming them. They treated a tool name as a shell command or scripted their way around it. Part of that was the harness, not the models: gpt-oss:20b did call `list_capabilities` correctly but could not carry the discovery into `call_tool` inside a general task, and the one approach that completed the sequence (the sub-agent) was blocked by the harness's own agent-tool argument validation before it ever reached the router. **Measurement 2 — 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-21, DeepSeek Harness, router tools registered natively by the [DSH bundle](#native-deepseek-harness-dsh-bundle).** The same model family (`qwen3:30b-a3b-instruct-2507`, 32K window) **used the router with no bypass.** 09-19, two sessions whose prompts named the tools: `list_capabilities` once, then `list_capabilities` ×8 → `call_tool(ops-scripts, service_status)`. 09-21, one session, three ordinary prompts that named no tool ("Which of the project's services are running right now?", "How many n8n workflows do we have, and which were edited most recently?", "What did we learn last time a bridge commit wrote stale bytes?"): the call log shows `list_capabilities(jobs)` → `call_tool(jobs, pipeline_status)`, then `call_tool(n8n, list)` (wrong name, `ok: false`) → `call_tool(n8n, n8n_list_workflows)` (`ok: true`, 12,963 chars shaped by the ladder) — the model corrected itself from the router's error — and **zero `bypass` rows**; the third prompt was answered with the companion plugin's `recall`/`search` plus built-in `glob`/`read`, which is the right tool, not a bypass. That is three sessions and one model: enough to show Measurement 1 is **not a verdict on these models**, not enough to promise yours will behave. So: `--selftest` proves the *saving* and that your backends start — it does **not** prove your model will drive the router in your harness. **Test discovery→call with your actual model and harness before committing**, and measure rather than guess: every router call is appended to `~/.tool-guardian/calls.jsonl` (`TOOL_GUARDIAN_CALL_LOG`) with a session id, and under DSH a shell call that does a router tool's job is logged there as `kind: "bypass"` (and can be nudged or denied). After a few real tasks, **`/toolguardian bypass`** (DSH) or **`tool-guardian --bypass-summary`** (any client) reads that file for you: router calls, every bypass with the exact `call_tool(...)` it should have been, and sessions that never touched the router. Over plain MCP, see [bypass detection and its limits](#bypass-detection-over-plain-mcp-and-its-limits). If it won't, expose a small *curated, visible* subset of servers instead of routing everything behind a catalogue the model never opens. ## Two ways to run it It is one repo and one Python router. Pick the front door that matches your harness — both stay supported. | | **MCP server** (any MCP client) | **Native DSH bundle** | |---|---|---| | Works with | Claude Code, OpenCode, Cline, Continue ([tested configs](#works-with)), Claude Desktop, OpenClaude, Cursor, anything that speaks MCP over stdio | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) | | Install | `pip install tool-guardian` | `dsh plugin --profile add dsh-tool-guardian` | | Hides MCP schemas behind 6 router tools (8 with [skills](#skills)) | yes | yes, registered natively | | Output ladder on results | results of `call_tool` | **every** tool's result (`bash`, `grep`, `web_fetch`, ...) | | Tool groups with token prices | `list_groups_with_costs` | plus `activate_group`, and DSH's own built-in tools can be grouped and hidden too | | Notices a shell call doing a router tool's job | — | logs, nudges or denies it | | Configured by | `tool-guardian.json` + `TOOL_GUARDIAN_*` env | the `tool-guardian` patch row or DSH settings; the same env vars win | ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Your agent
(Claude Code, DSH, any MCP client)"] -->|"6 tools, ~1,700 tokens for 7 servers"| B["Tool Guardian"] B -->|"on demand"| C["filesystem"] B -->|"on demand"| D["git"] B -->|"on demand"| E["n8n, database, ..."] B -. "big result" .-> F[("archive
retrieve_spill")] B -->|"shaped result"| A ``` ## Tools The router exposes these tools. The first four are always there; `list_groups_with_costs` and `retrieve_spill` (while the output ladder is on) are the other two of the 6 router tools; the two skill tools appear only when a skill folder is configured. | tool | arguments | what it does | |---|---|---| | `list_capabilities` | `server` (optional) | tool names with one-line summaries for one server, or all; start here | | `search_capabilities` | `query`, `server` and `limit` (optional) | find a tool by keyword across servers | | `describe_tool` | `server`, `tool`, `detail` (optional) | the arguments of one tool (`detail=full`: its whole schema) | | `call_tool` | `server`, `tool`, `args` (optional) | run a backend tool and return its (shaped) result; this is the step that answers the user | | `list_groups_with_costs` | none | tool groups and the context-token cost of loading each | | `retrieve_spill` | `id`, `grep`, `start_line`, `max_lines` (optional) | read back the full original of a shortened result | | `list_skills` | none | one line per skill (only with `TOOL_GUARDIAN_SKILLS`) | | `read_skill` | `name` | the full text of one skill (only with `TOOL_GUARDIAN_SKILLS`) | All but `call_tool` only report (read-only, no network: the catalogue is in memory, the archive and skills on local disk); `call_tool` does whatever the backend tool does. Each tool's description says what it is for, when a sibling is the better call, what it touches and what comes back — in about one clause each, because the whole `tools/list` payload is capped at 1,100 tokens by a test. Every parameter is typed and explained exactly once, by its own description, by its `enum`, or by the tool description naming it; `tests/test_tool_definitions.py` checks that, and checks this table's argument names against the schemas the server really lists. ## Search by meaning (optional) `search_capabilities` matches words. Ask it to "persist a memo" and it finds nothing, because no tool says "persist" or "memo"; the tool is `add_note`. Search by meaning fixes that with an embedding model you run yourself. **It is off by default**: with `TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_URL` unset the output is byte for byte what it was and nothing is sent anywhere. Turn it on by pointing it at an embeddings endpoint. The URL path tells tool-guardian which shape to speak: ```bash # Ollama (the path ends in /api/embed) export TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed # or any OpenAI-compatible server (the path ends in /embeddings) export TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/embeddings ``` | variable | default | meaning | |---|---|---| | `TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_URL` | unset (off) | the embeddings endpoint; a path that ends in neither `/api/embed` nor `/embeddings` is refused and search stays on keywords | | `TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_MODEL` | `nomic-embed-text` | the model name sent in the request | | `TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_MIN` | `0.5` | the cosine similarity a tool needs to be listed at all | | `TOOL_GUARDIAN_EMBED_CACHE` | `~/.tool-guardian/embed_cache` | where the tool vectors are kept, one `.json` per model and catalogue | What changes: a tool is listed only when its meaning is close enough to the query (cosine at or above the minimum), so an unrelated query can answer "no tools match". The listed tools are ranked by cosine, with the old keyword score counted at 1/100 only to break ties. The header, the `args:` lines and the NEXT STEP line are unchanged. If the endpoint is down, times out or answers badly, `search_capabilities` returns the keyword answer, byte for byte, and tool-guardian logs one `search by meaning off` line to stderr per run, not one per search. Measured with `python bench/bench_search.py` (seven bench catalogues, 95 tools; 40 queries: 20 paraphrases, 10 exact names, 10 that nothing should match; minimum 0.5; 2026-10-31). A query counts when an expected tool is in the first three lines, or, for the ten negative ones, when nothing is listed: ``` nomic-embed-text recall@3 keyword=35.0 semantic=80.0 blended=80.0 over 40 queries mxbai-embed-large recall@3 keyword=35.0 semantic=85.0 blended=82.5 over 40 queries ``` Run it on your own model: `python bench/bench_search.py --url http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed --model --min 0.5`. Why meaning first: a blend that let keywords outweigh meaning scored only 45 to 47.5 on real embeddings, because a substring hit ("store" inside "storemanager") lists tools for unrelated queries and ranks them above the paraphrase match. So a keyword hit alone lists nothing, and keywords only order tools that already passed on meaning. Cost: one embedding call per search (the query), plus one call for the whole catalogue whenever a tool is added, removed or re-described. Nothing else is sent, and the tool descriptions go only to the endpoint you chose. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR client["MCP client
(Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ...)"] -- "stdio JSON-RPC" --> serve dsh["DSH bundle
index.js"] -- "line JSON
tg_bridge.py" --> router subgraph tg["tool-guardian (Python, standard library only)"] serve["serve()
MCP over stdio"] --> router["Router
catalogue · search · arg checks · loop guard"] router --> ladder["tg_ladder
shape result by type"] ladder -- "lossy?" --> spill[("tg_spill archive
~/.tool-guardian/spill")] router --> groups["tg_groups
token price per group"] router --> state[("calls.jsonl · state.json")] end router -- "stdio, started at launch,
respawned once" --> b1["backend MCP server"] router --> b2["backend MCP server"] ``` You point your client at **one** MCP server, Tool Guardian, and give it the same `mcpServers` config you would have given the client. It starts every backend as a child process at launch, reads each `tools/list` once, and from then on answers `list_capabilities`, `search_capabilities` and `describe_tool` from memory. Only `call_tool` reaches a backend. Its arguments are checked against the backend tool's schema first, and the result goes through the output ladder before the model sees it. The DSH bundle reaches the same `Router` through a private bridge process instead of MCP. Key decisions, each with its trade-off (full records in [docs/adr/](docs/adr/)): | Decision | What it buys | What it costs | |---|---|---| | Generic router tools, schemas on demand ([0001](docs/adr/0001-router-with-on-demand-discovery.md)) | 91 % fewer schema tokens on every request (bench) | every capability is 2–3 calls away; the model must choose to look | | Loud failure, named catalogue ([0002](docs/adr/0002-loud-failure-and-a-named-catalogue.md)) | a dead server is never mistaken for "no such tool" | the description grows a few tokens per server | | Descriptions budgeted and pinned ([0003](docs/adr/0003-descriptions-are-paid-on-every-request.md)) | tools a model can choose between without guessing | 1,090 tokens of `tools/list` with no backends, pinned at ≤ 1,100 by a test | | Lenient inputs, strict backend checks ([0004](docs/adr/0004-lenient-inputs-strict-checks.md)) | small models' near-miss calls still work; impossible calls cost no round trip | schemas are looser than what the router enforces | | One stdlib Python core; DSH bundle is a bridge ([0005](docs/adr/0005-one-python-core-stdlib-only.md)) | installs anywhere; one router to fix | MCP stdio is hand-written; the npm package needs a Python | | Archive before shortening ([0006](docs/adr/0006-archive-before-shortening.md)) | big results stop flooding the window, nothing is lost | originals are kept on local disk | ## Install ```bash pip install tool-guardian ``` Pure standard library — nothing else to install. > PyPI and npm now ship the same code: `pip install tool-guardian` (0.3.0+) for the MCP server, `dsh-tool-guardian` on npm for DSH. Which install is which: the Python package `tool-guardian` **0.9.1** is the MCP server (`pip install tool-guardian`, or `uvx tool-guardian`); the npm package `dsh-tool-guardian` **0.9.1-beta.1** is the DeepSeek Harness bundle. They are versioned separately. ## Configure **Quickest way:** you probably already have your servers set up in another MCP client. ```bash tool-guardian-setup import # copies them from Claude Desktop / Cursor / Windsurf / .mcp.json, asks before writing tool-guardian-setup doctor # checks the config, each server's command, your .env and ${VARS}, and says how to fix each problem ``` **Adding one more server is one command** -- everything after `--` is the server's command line, exactly as you would type it: ```bash tool-guardian-setup add git -- uvx mcp-server-git tool-guardian-setup add github --env GITHUB_TOKEN='${GITHUB_TOKEN}' --descr

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-token-usage **Token 用量面板，为 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的 Web GUI 而做。** 逐请求账本 · 四桶计量 · 全年热力图 · 实时并发，以及一份**落盘账本**——它让用量记录不再随会话滚动而消失。

--- ## 它解决什么问题 DSH 的 durable session log 里其实**已经**记着每次调用的 provider 计费用量，但没有任何页面把它摊开：用了多少、花在哪、什么时候用的，都看不见。 更麻烦的是，会话投影每个会话只保留**最近 600 行**。会话一长、或者会话被删，早期用量就从界面上消失了——数字变小，但数据从来没丢，只是没人再去读它。 这个插件做两件事： 1. 把那份权威数据折成一张**请求日志**，一次计费尝试一行； 2. 额外落一份**盘上账本**，不受投影窗口限制，并在启动时从全部会话日志回扫补齐。 ## 功能 ### 概览 - 四张主指标卡：请求数、合计 tokens、缓存命中率、输出速度；「更多指标」展开四桶明细、平均耗时、平均首字 - **趋势图**：按桶堆叠的柱子，与**同一根 x 轴**上的缓存命中率折线。两者永远读同一个数据源、同一个窗口——一眼能看出哪次改动把缓存打掉了 - **全年热力图**：53 周 × 7 天，铺满卡片宽度，月/周标签齐全 - **渠道排行**：占比、四色构成条、请求数、命中率、合计 - 标题下的**今日**读数（不随筛选变化）与**实时并发** ### 下钻：每个数字都能点 概览不是一张图。每处都在回答「这是哪几条请求」，点下去就带着筛选跳到请求日志： | 点这里 | 结果 | | --- | --- | | 趋势图的柱子 | 只看那一天（24 小时窗口下是那一小时） | | 热力图的格子 | 只看那一天 | | 渠道排行的行 | 只看这个渠道 | | 请求 / 合计 / 命中率 / 速度 卡片 | 请求 → 请求日志；合计 → 日期；命中率、速度 → 模型 | | 「更多指标」里的卡片 | 请求日志并按这一列降序（缓存读、补全、耗时、首字…） | | 分组视图的任意一行 | 日期行下钻到那天；渠道 / 模型行变成对应筛选 | | 请求日志的日期条 | 只看这一天 | 下钻是一次**筛选**，不是新页面：它和渠道 / 模型 / 搜索叠加，工具栏上出现 `10-22 全天 ×` 的胶囊，点掉它或「清除筛选」即可回退。柱子、卡片、分组行、渠道行都能用键盘操作（Tab 到目标，Enter 或空格）。 账本只有全量聚合，切不出一段时间，所以下钻时数字回到**保留记录**口径——页脚会写明来源；若账本对这一天知道的比列表里的行更多，条数旁边会同时给出两个数字，避免把小的那个当成一整天。 ### 请求日志

- 12 列逐请求明细：时间 / 会话 / 渠道 / 模型 / 提示 / 缓存读 / 补全 / 合计 / 耗时 / 首字 / 速度 / 流式 - 按天分组的**粘性日期条**，表头与日期条都随滚动钉住 - 点任意一行展开该条的四桶明细（含缓存写、推理子集、轮次与步骤） - **点会话名直接跳到那个对话** - 筛选：时间范围 / 渠道 / 模型 / 全文搜索；**暂停**冻结表格而顶部数字照常更新 - 列头点击排序、CSV 导出、页码直达 ### 分组视图

模型、渠道、日期三张表共用一套列：占比（带条）、请求、提示、缓存读、补全、合计（带四色构成条）、命中率、平均耗时、速度。 ### 实时并发 标题下的活体指示 `● 运行中 N`，数据来自会话列表自带的 `running` 标志——Host 推送，不是轮询。 一个会话里同时有多个调用在飞时，追加 `· M 步在飞`：Host 按 `step/start` → 结算事件计数，`turn/end` 清空。会话的 `running` 是布尔值，说不出一段对话里有几个调用在跑，这个计数可以。 ## 安装 插件是一个普通的 DSH bundle，纯 JS，**无构建步骤**。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/menglian001/dsh-token-usage.git ~/dsh-token-usage # 1) 装插件自己的依赖（必做，见下） cd ~/dsh-token-usage && npm install # 2) 在 profile 里登记，然后安装 cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web pnpm install ``` profile 的 `package.json` 需要这两处： ```jsonc { "dependencies": { "dsh-token-usage": "link:~/dsh-token-usage" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["...", "dsh-token-usage"] } } } ``` 然后重启 dsh。 > **为什么第 1 步必做** > `link:` 包按**真实目录**解析依赖，不经过 profile 的 `node_modules`。插件目录里没有 `node_modules/zod` 时，Host 半会以 `Cannot find package 'zod'` 加载失败——而 Host 半失败会连带 Client 半不注入，表现是侧边栏根本没有这个图标。`npm install` 只装一个 `zod`，几秒钟。 > > **Host 半改动需要重启**才生效；Client 半热更新，刷新页面即可。 ## 数据从哪来 | 数字 | 来源 | |---|---| | 四桶（未命中输入 / 缓存读 / 缓存写 / 补全）与推理 | **provider 回包上报**，不是估算 | | 提示 / 补全 / 合计 / 缓存命中率 | 四桶的算术 | | 耗时 / 首字 / 生成时间 | **本地时钟**，含网络往返，不是上游服务端延迟 | | 输出速度 | 补全 ÷ 生成时间，池化；仅计入补全 ≥ 100 且生成 ≥ 100 ms 的请求 | 链路：provider 响应 → `stream.ts` 的 `usage` 事件 → `assembler` → `assistant/message.data.usage` → 本插件的 `requestLog` 投影。 走中转时，"准确"的含义是**忠实反映中转上报的数字**。中转少报，面板就跟着少报。 ## 落盘账本 每次请求结算时追加一行 JSONL 到 `$DSH_HOME/token-usage/requests.jsonl`。 - **键**：`session|turn|step|attempt`，读时后写覆盖。崩溃重放、重复回扫都不会重复计数 - **回扫**：启动后读遍磁盘上的全部会话日志，把投影窗口早已丢掉的行补回来 - **保留** 730 天 - **压实**：启动时若文件 ≤ 32 MB 且（总行数 ≥ 2000 且 总行数 > 唯一键数 × 1.25，即重复行占比 > 20%；或存在超 730 天的记录）则压实（写临时文件再 rename）。超过 32 MB 的文件只读、不再压实 数据有两条来源，页脚会说明当前用的是哪条： - **账本**：保留窗口内只增不减，但只有聚合（天 / 模型 / 渠道）与最近若干行明细（服务端留 2000 行，面板按需取 400 行） - **保留记录**：浏览器手里的投影行，能按任意条件切片，但受每会话 600 行窗口约束 切换规则只看**完整性**：账本尝试数 ≥ 保留行数，且无筛选时读账本。天数跨度不参与判断——图表的天数下限是画图用的，不能拿来仲裁数据源。 ## 已知边界 - **缓存写 / 推理恒为 0**：上游若为 OpenAI 口径（prompt 里已含缓存命中），不会单独上报 `cache_creation` / `reasoning`。显示 0 是没报，不是漏读 - **速度显示 `—`**：中转把首字和落盘报在同一瞬间时，生成时间≈0，除出来的速度是假的，因此按门槛显示 `—`。`—` 表示"没测到"，不是 0 - **请求日志明细受投影窗口约束**：明细仍读投影（每会话 600 行）；分组视图与趋势在无筛选时读账本聚合，不会缩水 - **热力图空格 = 那天没有记录**，不是"那天没用" - **账本从启用那天开始记**：更早且日志已被清理的会话，总数可能补回，明细补不回来 ## 架构 ``` index.js Host 半 ├─ requestLog 会话投影 一次计费尝试一行 ├─ Ledger JSONL 落盘 + 内存聚合（天/模型/渠道/会话） ├─ 磁盘回扫 sessionPersistence.list() → 逐会话 read() → 补写 ├─ LiveSteps 在飞步骤计数 └─ GET /token-usage/ledger 浏览器 cookie 鉴权，失败关闭 client.js Client 半（纯 JS，React.createElement，无构建） ├─ 三个槽位 侧边栏 / 主面板 / 设置页 ├─ 投影补拉 pump 游标轮转，避免老会话饿死 └─ 视图 概览 / 请求日志 / 模型 / 渠道 / 日期 ``` ## 开发与校验 纯 JS，没有构建。校验脚本在 `test/`，Node 直接跑，不依赖 dsh： ```bash npm install # 装 zod（仅测试/开发需要） npm test # 跑 12 套离线校验 node test/render-check.mjs # 跑单个 # 安装验收：把本包当成陌生用户从零装一遍 node test/install-check.mjs # 或随套件一起跑 DSH_TU_INSTALL_CHECK=1 npm test ``` 覆盖：投影折叠语义、账本写入 / 覆盖 / 压实 / 回扫幂等、聚合视图切换、pump 覆盖率、面板渲染（含空数据与缺 seat 的降级）、在飞步骤计数，以及**下钻**——真的点柱子、格子、渠道行、卡片、分组行，断言点完之后的那棵树（视图、条数、胶囊、排序、覆盖披露）。 `install-check` 单独存在是有原因的：其余 harness 都在本仓库内 `import ../index.js`，那里 `node_modules` 已经存在，恰好掩盖了唯一真把人绊倒的失败模式。这个 harness 用 `git archive` 造出干净树、经 `link:` 解析、先断言 import **必须失败**、装完依赖再断言**必须成功**。 截图可以重新生成（需要 Playwright 与一个本地 Harness checkout）： ```bash node scripts/screenshots.mjs --harness ../deepseek-harness ``` ## English A token-usage panel for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI. It folds the Harness's own provider-reported usage into a per-request ledger and keeps a durable copy on disk, because a session projection only retains the newest 600 rows per session. - **Overview** — four headline cards, a stacked-by-bucket trend with the cache-hit line on the same x axis and the same source, a 53-week heat map, a channel ranking. - **Request log** — one row per billed attempt (12 columns) under sticky day rules, expandable into the four-bucket breakdown, sortable, filterable, pausable, CSV export; a session name opens its conversation. - **Model / channel / day tables** — share, requests, prompt, cache read, completion, total with a composition bar, hit rate, latency, speed. - **Drill-down** — every mark on the overview is a filter: a trend bar or a heat cell opens that day (that hour, under a 24-hour window), a channel row narrows to that channel, a card opens the view that explains it or the log sorted by its column, and any grouped row becomes the picker value it was aggregated under. - **Live concurrency** — the session list's `running` flag, plus a Host-side count of open steps, so several calls in flight inside one conversation are visible. - **Durable ledger** — every settled request is appended to `$DSH_HOME/token-usage/requests.jsonl`, keyed by `session|turn|step|attempt` (last write wins), swept from every stored session log at startup, retained for 730 days, compacted at startup when it is small enough. **Install** — clone it, run `npm install` inside the clone (a `link:` package resolves its dependencies from its real directory, so without it the Host half fails with `Cannot find package 'zod'`), add `"dsh-token-usage": "link:~/dsh-token-usage"` to your profile dependencies and `dsh-token-usage` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, run `pnpm install`, restart dsh. **Tests** — `npm install` then `npm test` runs the offline harnesses in `test/`. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-workspace-split

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@metal-huang/dsh-workspace-split)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@metal-huang/dsh-workspace-split)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@metal-huang/dsh-workspace-split)](LICENSE)
[![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%E2%89%A50.2.1--rc.2-blue)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

English · [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

Keep several **live** sessions of DeepSeek Harness side by side and type in any
of them. Built for supervising several projects at once: you see every session's
progress on one screen instead of clicking through tabs.

<!-- A screenshot lives at docs/assets/split-view.png once captured. -->

## What it does

- **A grid of live sessions.** Rows and columns are yours to choose, up to 5 × 6.
  Each tile holds a running session with its full transcript.
- **Every tile is typable, attachments included.** Each cell has its own
  composer; paste, drop, or pick a PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF, or attach any other
  file through the `+` menu. Uploads are staged through `ctx.fileUpload` and sent
  as file parts with the text. The split layout never changes on its own.
- **Model, reasoning effort, and access mode per tile.** The seat under the
  composer reads the same Session projections and Remote catalogs as Chat, and
  writes through `session.selectModel` / `/permission <preset>`; switching to
  full access asks for the same risk confirmation.
- **Slash commands and `@` references.** A `/command` line runs through
  `session.command` without spending a turn, and `@` lists files and sessions
  through the public reference providers before inserting the same plain-text
  token Chat uses.
- **Approvals and questions answer in the tile.** An approval or
  `ask_user_question` waiting on that Session replaces the composer with a
  compact card; answering calls the same pending object Chat's panel uses.
- **Context occupancy.** The footer shows the same `projected / window` token
  reading as Chat, and hides itself when the projection is absent.
- **Session or project per tile.** Pin one session, or pin a project and switch
  between that project's sessions inside the tile.
- **Real-time status.** A dot on each title shows whether the session is working,
  and a colored project badge before the title keeps the Session's project
  visible after the tile has been open for a while.
- **Density that follows the tile.** Narrow tiles shrink their text
  automatically so a small cell still shows a useful amount; `Ctrl` + wheel over
  one tile changes that tile alone. The header stays unscaled, so titles remain
  aligned even when two tiles use different zoom levels.
- **Markdown and math.** Tables, code, task lists, and TeX rendered with KaTeX.
- **The process, not just the answer.** Reasoning and tool calls fold into one
  per-turn process group with its elapsed time, a tool call marks itself running
  until its result arrives, and a status line names what the session is doing. A
  failed turn shows the provider error instead of ending in silence; with an
  empty draft the send seat becomes Stop.
- **Queue, steer, remove.** Prompts queued behind a running turn are listed above
  the composer with Steer and Remove, matching Chat's QueueDock.
- **Tool calls you can open.** Arguments and output inline, failures marked.
- **Turn rail.** Ticks down the right edge jump between turns, including turns
  not loaded yet.
- **Layout survives restarts.** Grid, assignments, and per-cell zoom are restored.

## How sessions are wired

Sessions come from the public `ctx.sessions` API (`list`, `retain`, the event
source), and input goes out through `session.prompt`. Each tile's transcript,
Markdown, tool cards, and composer are rendered by this plugin itself, with
styles built on DSH's theme variables and visual rules so they match the app.

Everything DSH-specific is consumed through public services and Remote
namespaces — `ctx.fileUpload`, `ctx.uiSession`, `ctx.remote.session`,
`ctx.remote.permissionPresets`, `ctx.remote.fileReferences`, and
`ctx.remote.sessionReferenceResolver`. `test/dsh-contract.test.js` asserts those
methods and type names against the installed DSH build, so an upstream rename
fails a gate with the exact missing symbol instead of silently breaking a tile.
Set `DSH_CONTRACT_ROOT` to check another installation; the test skips when no DSH
install is present.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** or newer (desktop or web).
- Desktop app or `dsh web`; the same build works in both.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin add @metal-huang/dsh-workspace-split
```

Then restart the app (or reload the web page). The toggle appears at the bottom
of the sidebar, next to your account.

<details>
<summary>Installing from a local checkout</summary>

```bash
git clone https://github.com/metal-huang/dsh-workspace-split.git
cd dsh-workspace-split
npm install
cd packages/dsh-workspace-split && npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin add "$PWD/packages/dsh-workspace-split"
```

</details>

## Use

| Action | Where |
|---|---|
| Enter or leave split view | Left-click the ⊞ at the sidebar's bottom |
| Choose the grid | Right-click that same ⊞ |
| Assign a session | Use a tile's header picker, or drag a session row from the sidebar into the tile |
| Rename a session | The ✎ next to the tile's title |
| Resize text in one tile | `Ctrl` + wheel over that tile |
| Raise the cell limit | Settings → General → Split grid |

The cap defaults to 10 cells for the whole screen (12 hard limit per window,
both configurable). Six cells fit comfortably; past six, opening more asks for
confirmation.

## Development

```bash
npm install          # repo tooling
npm run check        # lint + duplication + format + tests
npm run build        # rebuild the client bundle
npm run release      # publish a snapshot for the desktop profile
```

`packages/dsh-workspace-split/src/client.js` is the source. `client.js` next to
it is generated and not tracked by git — `npm install` in that package builds it
through `prepare`, and `npm run build` rebuilds it. Never edit it by hand.

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the repository rules and [docs/](docs) for the
product and design notes.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-mcp-autoload

Auto-discover project-level MCP servers for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).

Place a `.agents/mcp.json` at your project root (the nearest ancestor with a
`.git` marker). Every DSH agent session whose working directory is inside that
project automatically mounts the declared servers; connections close when the
session ends. Servers from other projects never leak in.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

## Install

Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0` and Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. `dsh plugin`
forwards its arguments to pnpm inside the profile directory.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mcp-autoload
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the CLI registers it under the
profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` for you. Restart `dsh web` afterwards — the host
half loads at startup — then hard-refresh the browser (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R).

Working on the plugin from a local clone instead (the dependency is recorded as
a `link:`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-mcp-autoload
```

Update with `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mcp-autoload@latest`; uninstall with
`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-mcp-autoload`.

## Minimal example

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "playwright": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Full example

Four entries cover every field and both toggle spellings:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"],
      "env": { "PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH": "~/.cache/ms-playwright" }
    },
    "postgres_local": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer local-dev-token" }
    },
    "experimental_server": {
      "enabled": false,
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["some-experimental-mcp@latest"]
    },
    "legacy_server": {
      "disabled": true,
      "url": "http://old-mcp.internal/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Field reference

| Field | Transport | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | stdio | Executable: a bare name resolved from `PATH` (`npx`, `uvx`) or an absolute path. Required for stdio |
| `args` | stdio | Optional string array, passed through without shell interpolation |
| `env` | stdio | Optional string map merged over the scrubbed child environment; explicit entries survive the scrub |
| `url` | Streamable HTTP | Absolute `http(s)://` URL. Required for HTTP |
| `headers` | Streamable HTTP | Optional string map of extra request headers |
| `type` | — | Optional; accepted values are `stdio` and `http`. `sse` is rejected with a log line |
| `disabled` / `enabled` | — | Optional; `disabled: true` or `enabled: false` skips the entry silently (both Claude Code and Codex spellings). The popover removes both fields to enable, or writes `disabled: true` to disable |

**Transport selection:** an entry with `url` mounts over Streamable HTTP;
otherwise `command` mounts a stdio child process whose working directory is
the session's cwd. An entry with neither is skipped with an error log.

**Server names.** A name matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}` passes through
unchanged (`postgres_local`, `experimental_server` stay as-is). Any other name — Chinese
characters, spaces, over-long — is normalized to a deterministic slug (the
same algorithm the DSH ACP bridge uses), e.g. `我的服务器` → `server_<hash>`.

**Tool names.** Each server's tools register for that session as
`mcp__<serverName>__<rawToolName>`, e.g. `mcp__playwright__browser_navigate`.

## Behavior

- **Per-session scope.** Each server mounts inside the agent's Cordis scope:
  tools apply to that session only, and connections close when the agent is
  disposed. Two sessions in different projects can use the same server name
  independently.
- **Startup.** Mounting happens during agent creation and awaits the initial
  connection, so tools are available in the first turn. Servers connect in
  parallel; one slow or broken server never blocks the others
  (`failOnStartupError` stays false). A server that fails to connect is
  skipped with an error log and the rest keep working.
- **In-session management.** The popover can enable/disable project MCP servers
  after a browser confirmation. The manifest is locked, backed up (only the five
  newest backups are kept) and replaced atomically; a symlinked manifest is
  followed so the link itself survives. Disabling unloads its tools at once. If
  re-enabling cannot mount, the manifest is rolled back to its previous state and
  the failure is reported — the file never claims a state the session could not
  actually mount.
- **User-level MCPs.** Profile-configured entries are listed but cannot be toggled here; only project manifest entries are writable.
- **No external hot reload.** The manifest is read once per session start (including resume). Manual edits require a new session to apply.
- **Plugin config** (in the patch row):

```yaml
- id: mcp-autoload
  name: dsh-mcp-autoload
  config:
    configPath: .agents/mcp.json   # absolute, or relative to the project root
    projectRootMarkers: ['.git']   # directory entries that mark the root
```

## Security

`.agents/mcp.json` entries are **executed** on session start. A cloned
repository containing this file gets to run arbitrary `command` lines on your
machine — the same trust level as an npm postinstall script. Only add this
file to projects you trust, and review it when cloning others'.

## Compatibility

Peer packages (`@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`) are provided by the DSH installation; the
bundle declares them only for version checks. Requires DSH >= 0.2.1-0 < 0.3.0.

## Development

All ESM, no build step: the source is the published artifact. `npm test` runs
`node --test`; `npm pack --dry-run` must list every runtime file. Conventions
live in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/micln/dsh-mcp-autoload/blob/master/AGENTS.md);
release and awesome-list submission are documented in
[PUBLISHING.md](https://github.com/micln/dsh-mcp-autoload/blob/master/PUBLISHING.md).

decision.reason: Held for runtime execution policy acceptance. MIT exact npm gitHead and DSH 0.2.1 range are explicit. On agent creation, native code reads project .agents/mcp.json, translates command/env or HTTP targets and mounts MCP clients. No project trust approval is established before executing repository-controlled server commands. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-quick-reply

Adds a quick-send button to the DeepSeek Harness composer. Save the phrases you
keep retyping, then send any of them to the current session with one click.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

![Quick reply panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/micln/dsh-quick-reply/master/docs/panel.png)

## What it does

- **One-click send.** Clicking any phrase in the panel sends it as a message to
  the current session and collapses the panel.
- **Skill shortcuts.** A phrase may contain `/skill-name`, which is equivalent to
  typing that skill by hand. When adding or editing, type `/` or press the `/`
  button to list the skills available in the current session.
- **Custom order.** Hold `⋮⋮` and drag up or down to reorder.
- **Edit in place.** ✎ edits a phrase, `🗑` deletes it, `✓` saves, `✕` cancels.
- **Add any time.** The `+` in the panel's top-right corner appends an entry
  (at most 20 phrases, 2000 characters each).

Four phrases ship by default: `按推荐执行`, `我已做完，你继续`, `端到端测试一下`, and
`/handoff` (the last one is a skill shortcut and only fires when the session has a
`handoff` skill).

## Install

Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0`. Install through `dsh plugin`, replacing
`--profile` with the instance you use (`web` or `desktop`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-quick-reply
```

Afterwards restart that instance (`dsh web` or the desktop app), then hard-refresh
the browser (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R).

Update to the latest version:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-quick-reply@latest
```

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-quick-reply
```

## Usage

- Phrases live in the **current browser's** `localStorage` (key
  `dsh-quick-reply:items:v1`); they are **not synced across browsers or devices**.
  Switching browsers or clearing site data means adding them again.
- The skill list comes from the current session, so the available skills change
  when you switch sessions.
- A mistyped skill name does not raise an error: the text is sent as plain text.

## Caveats

- Clicking a phrase sends its content straight as a message, exactly as if you had
  typed it yourself — there is no extra confirmation step.
- The plugin only sends text; it never runs commands on your behalf.

---

## Development

The rest of this document is for plugin developers.

### Layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `client.js` | Browser-side UI bundle: dock button, panel, editing, drag-reorder, skill suggestions |
| `index.js` | Host-side no-op plugin that only declares its name |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch, declared by `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json` |
| `locale/{en,zh}.json` | Plugin title and description |
| `client.test.mjs` | `node --test` cases |

### Dependencies

- Skill suggestions come from `remote.skills` (`skills/list`). When that service is
  unavailable the plugin still works — you just get no suggestion list, and typing
  `/name` by hand still works.
- Messages are sent through the session's `conversation` service, `send(text)`,
  submitted in `queue` mode.

### Local debugging

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-quick-reply
```

Editing `client.js` hot-swaps on save: the host's built-in client HMR polls the
loaded client assets every 500 ms (`{mtimeMs, ctimeMs, size}`), pushes a `rebuilt`
frame over `/plugins/events`, and the browser swaps that plugin's bundle. **No
instance restart and no page refresh is needed** (the bundle reload resets that
plugin's front-end state). If a change does not show up, retry from
Settings → Plugins.

The host half (`index.js`) is outside that HMR path, so restart the instance after
changing it.

### Tests

```sh
npm test
```

The tests evaluate `client.js` in Node with a stub loader and only cover the
exported pure functions: storage normalization, reordering, and `/name` syntax
parsing and filtering.

Before releasing, check the publish manifest with `npm pack --dry-run`: every
runtime file must be listed (both READMEs included) and test or temporary files
must not be.

### Release

A tag triggers CI to publish to npm (Trusted Publishing, with provenance):

```sh
# edit package.json's version so it matches the tag
git commit -am "chore: release X.Y.Z"
git push origin master
git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

CI creates a GitHub Release afterwards.

# dsh-im-rich **Telegram rich-message tools for DeepSeek Harness** — send a message as a structured rich-text block tree, as rich Markdown, as rich HTML, as classic `parse_mode` HTML, or as plain text; then read back what the Telegram server actually stored, edit it in place, or delete it. `v0.1.0` · MIT · Node.js >= 22.19.0 · no vendor code patched **English** | [简体中文](README-zh.md) Nothing in `@xmanrui/dsh-im` (or any other vendor bundle) is modified. The plugin consumes only the host's `tools` service and the integration's own on-disk state (`~/.dsh/integrations/dsh-telegram/{config.json,workspaces.json}` plus the `tokenRef` entry in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`). --- ## Installation ### Prerequisites - Node.js **>= 22.19.0** (declared in `package.json#engines`). - A DeepSeek Harness profile — the examples below use the `web` profile at `~/.dsh/profiles/web`. - The Telegram channel bundle `@xmanrui/dsh-im` installed in the same profile, with a bot configured in its `dsh-telegram` integration (`config.json` + a `tokenRef` in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`). The plugin never reads the token itself: it resolves `tokenRef` the same way the vendor channel does. See the next section. ### Install DeepSeek Harness first The plugin only exists inside a DSH profile, so `dsh` itself comes first. With Node 22.19 or newer on `PATH`: ```bash npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh dsh --version ``` The Desktop build ships its own runtime and needs no global install — use the command it provides, or the Web **Plugins** page described below. The first `dsh web` initializes `~/.dsh/profiles/web` from the shipped template. ### Required plugins (install these first) `dsh-im-rich` is a sidecar: it holds no Telegram credentials of its own and ships no transport. It reads the Telegram channel's on-disk state instead, so that channel must be installed in the same profile, with at least one bot configured: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @xmanrui/dsh-im # Telegram channel bundle, 5.9.1 at the time of writing ``` `@xmanrui/dsh-im` is a public package, so `dsh plugin` resolves it from the registry and enables the bundle in the same step. The plugin itself only asks the host for the `tools` service, which means it still loads when the channel is absent — but every send fails until the channel exists. Finish the channel's own setup, because these are the exact files `dsh-im-rich` reads: | File | Owner | What the plugin takes from it | | --- | --- | --- | | `~/.dsh/integrations/dsh-telegram/config.json` | channel bot settings | bot id, `tokenRef`, send rate limit | | `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` | channel credential store | the secret behind `tokenRef`, resolved at call time | | `~/.dsh/integrations/dsh-telegram/workspaces.json` | channel target settings | delivery targets (`tgt_…`), chat ids, forum topics | Add a bot with its BotFather token in the channel's integration settings, then add at least one delivery target. Confirm with `dsh_im_rich_info`: your bot must appear with `tokenAvailable: true`, followed by the targets you configured. An empty list means the channel is installed but not initialized — the plugin reports that as an error instead of inventing a default bot. ### Option A — one command with the `dsh` CLI (recommended) `dsh plugin` forwards its arguments to the package manager inside the profile directory and, when the install succeeds, records the dependency and appends the name to `dsh.profile.bundles` — a newly installed bundle is enabled by default, so nothing has to be edited by hand: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:milangree/dsh-im-rich ``` GitHub specs are pre-checked with `git ls-remote` before the package manager runs, and the repository ships `lib/` pre-built with no `prepare` script, so a git install needs no build step. To point it at a working copy instead, pass an absolute path: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-im-rich ``` The same operation works without a terminal: **Plugins** in the Web sidebar (or the `plugin_manager` tool) installs a bundle from the same spec and enables it. Restart the host afterwards unless the profile runs with HMR enabled. ### Option B — install with the package manager directly ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web pnpm add github:milangree/dsh-im-rich # or: npm install github:milangree/dsh-im-rich ``` The repository ships `lib/` pre-built and has no `prepare` script, so a git install needs no build step. Because `package.json` declares `"private": true`, the package can be installed from git but is not published to the npm registry — git and local `link:` are the two supported install paths. Pin a revision if you want reproducibility: ```bash pnpm add github:milangree/dsh-im-rich#main ``` ### Option C — clone and link a working copy ```bash git clone https://github.com/milangree/dsh-im-rich.git ~/src/dsh-im-rich cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web pnpm add link:~/src/dsh-im-rich # writes "dsh-im-rich": "link:…" into dependencies ``` Editing `~/src/dsh-im-rich/lib/*.mjs` is picked up by the host's HMR patch (the profile patches the plugin directory as the HMR base) on the next tool call — no restart needed for `lib/` changes. Changing `package.json` does need a restart. **Junction variant (no package manager involved).** On Windows you can wire the working copy straight into the profile's `node_modules` with a directory junction, then declare the dependency by hand: ```bat :: cmd.exe — directory junction, no admin rights needed mklink /J "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-im-rich" "%USERPROFILE%\src\dsh-im-rich" ``` ```powershell # PowerShell equivalent New-Item -ItemType Junction ` -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-im-rich" ` -Target "$env:USERPROFILE\src\dsh-im-rich" ``` ```jsonc // ~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json — declare it as a local link { "dependencies": { "dsh-im-rich": "link:~/src/dsh-im-rich" } } ``` The junction must still be paired with the `bundles` entry described below — a resolvable `node_modules/dsh-im-rich` alone does not load the plugin. ### Option D — install from a release zip ```bash unzip dsh-im-rich-0.1.0.zip -d ~/src/dsh-im-rich cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && pnpm add link:~/src/dsh-im-rich ``` Release zips use POSIX entry names (`lib/index.mjs`), so `unzip` on macOS/Linux and `Expand-Archive` on Windows both work. ### Register the bundle (manual installs only) Options B to D only put the package on disk — the profile still has to load it as a bundle. Option A already did this. For a manual install, add the name to the bundle list in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`: ```jsonc { "dependencies": { "dsh-im-rich": "link:/path/to/dsh-im-rich" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ // … existing entries … "dsh-im-rich" ] } } } ``` The package carries its own cordis patch (`package.json#dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`), which inserts the plugin into the composition tree: ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-im-rich name: dsh-im-rich ``` ### Restart and verify A running host loads bundles at start — **restart DSH** after wiring the package. ```bash # 1. the six tools must be registered (no network) cd /path/to/dsh-im-rich && npm run selfcheck # → 18 assertions, exit 0 # 2. after restart, the model sees dsh_im_rich_* tools; ask for one: # dsh_im_rich_info → configured bots and delivery targets ``` ### Uninstall Remove the dependency line and the `bundles` entry; delete the checkout (and the junction, if you created one). No other file is touched, and nothing is written outside `node_modules` and the profile's `package.json`. --- ## Quick start ```text # 1. discover targets dsh_im_rich_info → bots, targetId, chat id, forum thread # 2. look up the vocabulary before writing anything exotic dsh_im_rich_schema # 3. send Markdown; headings automatically become collapsed sections dsh_im_rich_send target=tgt_… text="# Title\n\nintro\n\n## Details\n\nbody" # 4. prove what the server stored dsh_im_rich_inspect chatId=846514744 messageIds=[123] # 5. fix or clean up dsh_im_rich_edit target=tgt_… messageId=123 text="## rewritten" dsh_im_rich_delete target=tgt_… messageIds=[123] ``` --- ## Tools | Tool | Purpose | Required arguments | | --- | --- | --- | | `dsh_im_rich_send` | Send one message in any of the five modes, optionally folded, uploaded, as a draft | `text` _or_ `blocks` | | `dsh_im_rich_edit` | Re-render an existing message in place (rich `markdown`/`html`/`blocks`, or `classic`/`plain`) | `messageId`, plus `text` or `blocks` | | `dsh_im_rich_delete` | Delete messages this bot sent, with per-id results | `messageIds` | | `dsh_im_rich_inspect` | Read back the server-side storage shape without touching the body | `messageIds`, `chatId` | | `dsh_im_rich_info` | List configured bots and delivery targets | — | | `dsh_im_rich_schema` | The measured vocabulary: input forms, block fields, inline nodes, syntax maps, limits, dropped fields | — | Every tool returns a `structuredContent` object; long reports also come back as text. None of them reads credentials beyond resolving the configured `tokenRef`. --- ## Supported rich messages Everything below was confirmed against the live Bot API by sending a payload and reading back the server's own normalized message, not taken from the public documentation. `19` block types and `22` inline types are the exact `BLOCK_TYPES` / `INLINE_TYPES` sets in `lib/md2blocks.mjs`; the five media blocks are `MEDIA_BLOCK_TYPES` in `lib/media.mjs`. ### Input forms — 3 | Form | Wire shape | How to reach it | | --- | --- | --- | | `blocks` | `rich_message: { blocks: [...] }` | `mode=blocks` (default), or pass `blocks` directly for a hand-written tree | | `markdown` | `rich_message: { markdown: "…" }` | `mode=markdown` | | `html` | `rich_message: { html: "…" }` | `mode=html` | `rich_message` accepts exactly one of those three keys. Unknown sibling keys (`text`, `plain`, `content`, `media`, `files`, `entities`, …) are silently ignored, and an empty object returns `rich message must be non-empty`. The outbound key spelling is the snake_case `rich_message`; the model-facing argument is `blocks`. ### Block types — 19 accepted `heading` · `paragraph` · `pullquote` · `list` · `blockquote` · `table` · `divider` · `pre` · `details` · `footer` · `anchor` · `slideshow` · `collage` · `map` · `photo` · `video` · `animation` · `audio` · `document` Required fields and the notes that matter in practice: | Block | Required | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `heading` | `text`, `size` | `size` 1–6; missing → `Can't find field "size"`, 0 or >6 → `invalid section heading size specified` | | `paragraph` | `text` | string or an array of inline nodes | | `pullquote` | `text` | content lives in `text`; passing `blocks` → `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` | | `list` | `items` | item fields `label`, `blocks`, `has_checkbox`, `is_checked`, `type`, `value`; ordered items use `type:"1"` + `value:n` + `label:"n."`, unordered use `label:"•"`; mixing both in one list → `list must be either ordered or unordered` | | `blockquote` | `blocks` | nests | | `table` | `cells` | plus `caption`, `is_bordered`, `is_striped`; cell fields `text`, `is_header`, `align`, `valign` | | `divider` | — | alone in a message → `RICH_MESSAGE_EMPTY` | | `pre` | `text` | plus `language` | | `details` | `summary`, `blocks` | `summary` is a plain string; `is_open: true` expands by default; nests | | `footer` | `text` | server keeps only `text` (`blocks` is dropped) | | `anchor` | `name` | zero-width; alone → `RICH_MESSAGE_EMPTY` | | `slideshow` | `blocks` | media blocks only; a `paragraph` inside → `RICH_MESSAGE_BLOCK_UNEXPECTED` | | `collage` | `blocks` | same rule as `slideshow` | | `map` | `location` | `{latitude,longitude}` rounded to 5 decimals; `caption` must be an object (`RichBlockCaption must be an object`); `zoom` 0, `width`/`height` 800×400 by default | | `photo` | `photo` | `{type:"photo", photo:{type:"photo", media:""}}` | | `video` | `video` | same media object; missing media → `RICH_MESSAGE_VIDEO_NO_MEDIA_FOUND` | | `animation` | `animation` | must be real animation content; a 1×1 GIF → `RICH_MESSAGE_VIDEO_INVALID`, mp4 input is normalized into a `video` block | | `audio` | `audio` | same media object | | `document` | `document` | same media object; `attach://` upload confirmed | ### Inline types — 22 accepted `bold` · `italic` · `underline` · `strikethrough` · `spoiler` · `code` · `marked` · `mention` · `text_mention` · `url` · `subscript` · `superscript` · `custom_emoji` · `hashtag` · `cashtag` · `bot_command` · `phone_number` · `email_address` · `anchor` · `reference` · `anchor_link` · `reference_link` Notes from the probes: `underline`/`subscript`/`superscript` only come from HTML tags in Markdown input (``, ``, ``); `marked` from `==x==`; `spoiler` from `||x||`; `text_mention` needs a `user` object (`[Name](tg://user?id=N)` works, and `user.id` is required); `url` requires the `url` field; `custom_emoji` requires a usable `custom_emoji_id` with a matching `alternative_text`; `reference`/`reference_link` have no Markdown syntax (`` is dropped) and must be hand-written; `anchor`/`anchor_link` come from `` / ``. ### Media blocks — 5 `photo` · `video` · `animation` · `audio` · `document` Each takes one media sub-object. `media` must be a **string** — an HTTPS URL, a Telegram `file_id`, or `attach://field` for a multipart upload. Captions accept a string or `{text: …}`. ### Markdown syntax map (server-side parse) | Written as | Becomes | | --- | --- | | `# … ######` | `heading` size 1–6 | | `**b**` `__b__` / `*i*` `_i_` / `~~s~~` / `==m==` / `\|\|s\|\|` | `bold` / `italic` / `strikethrough` / `marked` / `spoiler` | | `u` `2` `2` | `underline` / `subscript` / `superscript` | | `` `code` `` and ```` ```lang ```` fences | `code` and `pre(language)` | | bare `http(s)://…`, `@user`, `#tag`, `$AAPL`, `/cmd`, `+79991234567`, `mail@example.com` | `url`, `mention`, `hashtag`, `cashtag`, `bot_command`, `phone_number`, `email_address` | | `[Name](tg://user?id=N)` | `text_mention` | | `t` / `t` | `anchor` / `url("#x")` | | `-` `*` `+` bullets, `- [ ]` / `- [x]` checkboxes, `1.` ordered | `list` (with `has_checkbox`/`is_checked`, ordered `type:"1"`) | | `> …` (nestable), `---` | `blockquote`, `divider` | | `\| a \| b \|` + separator row | `table` (`is_bordered`+`is_striped`, header centred, body left) | | `

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
