evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-workspace-control

A DeepSeek Harness plugin for workspace-level maintenance: rename, delete, rebuild onto another directory, merge, and move single sessions between workspaces.

One panel for DeepSeek Harness workspaces: rename, delete, rebuild onto another
directory, merge, and move single sessions between them — without losing
anything. A session's working directory is baked into its stored header and into
the session-store directory name, so the UI cannot change it after creation; this
plugin does that through the supported persistence seam.

## What it does

The panel lives in its own central view, opened from its icon in the sidebar's
panel row (工作区管理 / Workspaces):

| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **重建… / Rebuild…** | Pick a new directory for a whole workspace. Every session it holds moves with it, the record at the new path inherits the title and the sidebar position, and the old record is removed once it is empty. |
| **合并… / Merge…** | Pick other workspaces. Their sessions move into this one's directory, and a source record is dropped once nothing is left in it. |
| **重命名 / Rename** | Change only the sidebar title. The directory is untouched. |
| **删除 / Delete** | Remove the workspace record. Its sessions are archived first, and the directory with all session files stays on disk — the workspace can be added back at the same path later. |

Every row also reports, *before anything is clicked*:

- how many sessions the directory really holds;
- **占用 N / N held** — how many of those cannot move right now, because a turn is
  running (`running`) or because the app still holds the session log (`open`, which
  makes the store refuse to publish a successor artifact). Rebuild, merge and
  delete stay disabled on such a row, and the held sessions are named in the row,
  so a refusal is visible up front instead of arriving after the fact.

Single sessions still have their own entry: **移动到工作区… / Move to workspace…** in
the session row's `...` menu moves just that session to a directory. If the target
is already a workspace, the session joins it; if not, the workspace is created.

The move keeps the session id, title, every committed event (history, tool calls,
approvals) and the format version, then regroups the session under the workspace
that owns the target directory. If that workspace does not exist yet, it is
created.

## How the move works

The session store is append-only and refuses rewritten history, so the move
materializes a **successor artifact** through the supported persistence seam
instead of editing bytes:

1. `sessionPersistence.stat(id)` — read the header (id, version, cwd, lineage).
2. `sessionPersistence.open(id, 'read')` — copy every committed event. A read
   handle never takes write ownership, so this works while the UI holds the
   session open.
3. Park the old session directory (atomic rename, same volume), so the id leaves
   the store before the successor claims it.
4. `sessionPersistence.create({ ...header, cwd }, { inheritedEventCount })` +
   `append(events)` + `flush()` — the backend writes a correct header frame with
   the new `cwd` in the current format.
5. Read back `stat(id)` and verify the stored `cwd`; then update the workspace
   registry: `resolveByPath(target) ?? create(target)`, `attachSession(id)`, and
   `detachSession(id)` on the old workspace.

Failure handling: if step 4 fails, the parked directory is renamed back and the
result says the move was rolled back. A rebuild rolls every session it already
moved back to the old directory, and removes the record it created at the target.

Two different states are refused up front, and the difference matters:

- `running` — a turn is in flight. A live agent keeps the old directory as its
  process cwd and permission root, so moving under it would be wrong. The signal
  is the turn boundary in the session log (`turn/start` with no `turn/end` after
  it), **not** `agents.get(id)`: an idle session that the app merely has open also
  has a live agent, which is why the sidebar can say 「空闲」 while a naive check
  says "running".
- `session-open` — the session is open in the app, so its log is in memory and the
  store owns that id. `create` then refuses the successor ("already exists"), so
  the move cannot work until the tab is closed; refusing here names the real
  reason instead of failing halfway through a rebuild.

Two more guards keep a half-done move from eating history:

- A header-only session (no committed events) is refused, because `create` writes
  nothing and only the first `append` publishes — moving it would delete the
  original and produce no successor.
- If the store still reports the id right after the directory was parked (an
  index-based resolution), the parked copy is restored and the move reports
  `store-cached` instead of failing with a misleading write error.

After a move the registry is settled in the same process. `WorkspaceRegistry`
builds its canonical-cwd header index once, in `[Service.init]`, and
`attachSession` validates against that index (`readSessionHeader` prefers a live
Session, then the cached header, and only re-reads the store when neither
exists). The plugin therefore drops the moved session's stale index entry before
attaching — the fields are plain `Map`s on the service instance — so the next
validation re-reads the rewritten header from the store. That is the state a
restart would produce, without a restart. The Client then asks
`sessions.refreshProjections(id)` to rebuild the derived view, and any other
workspace that still lists the session is detached.

If the attach is still refused (for example while the session is open in a tab,
where a live Session still answers with the old header), the move is recorded as
pending and settles automatically on the next start.


### Workspace membership is verified, and repairable

`attachSession` is judged by the canonical-cwd index, which the harness builds at
startup. A session whose header was rewritten *during this run* may therefore be
rejected until the harness restarts. The Host never reports that as a plain
success:

- `moved` — header rewritten, read-back matched, workspace reported the session.
- `moved-unattached` — the file moved but the workspace did not accept it yet.
- `attached` — the session already lived in the target directory (an earlier
  move left the membership behind); this run only completed the membership.

Repeating the same move is the repair action: when the stored cwd already equals
the target, the plugin skips the file work and only settles the workspace
membership, so a partial move is finished by the same command that made it.
`workspace-unattached` means even that failed; restart DSH and repeat once the
index is fresh.

The unattached case also heals itself on startup: the Host records the pending
`(sessionId, target)` pair in `.remaker-pending.json`, and two seconds into the
next boot — after the registry has rebuilt its index — it settles the membership
and clears the entry. So a move that landed its file but not its membership needs
one restart, not a second click.

Both halves also refuse to break application start: a throwing Client factory
degrades to an absent plugin instead of failing the Web boot gate (which fails
the whole app with `1 entry did not activate`), and a throwing Host `apply` is
logged to `.workspace-control.log` instead of failing the entry.

### The workspace title follows its directory, unless you renamed it

`create(path)` derives a title from the last path segment, so a title that still
equals its own basename was never typed by the user: a rebuild carries that kind
of title over to the new directory name (`ce` rebuilt onto
`D:\Github\workspace test` becomes `workspace test`). A title that differs from
its basename is treated as a deliberate rename and is preserved untouched.

Records created by an earlier build ignored that rule and kept the pre-rebuild
title. The workspace row in the manager offers a one-click repair for exactly
that shape — the button only appears when the stored title differs from the
folder name — and it calls `retitleWorkspace(workspaceId, title)`, which uses the
supported `Workspace#setTitle` and needs no restart.

## Install

From npm — the package, the repository and the plugin entry all use one name,
`dsh-workspace-control`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-workspace-control
```

Or from a local checkout:

```bash
plugin_manager install_bundle target=D:\Github\dsh-workspace-control
```

Then verify the loader row exists:

```bash
cordis_inspect_query Config.listConfigs name=dsh-workspace-control
```

Replacing an older install: this plugin shipped as `dsh-workspace-remaker` and later
`dsh-workspace-manager`, so drop whichever one is listed:
`plugin_manager remove_bundle target=dsh-workspace-manager`.

### The panel reports the same activity the sidebar does

A workspace row says `N running` only when a session really is mid-turn, and it
gets that answer from the same two sources the shipped sidebar uses:

```js
useSessionStatus().get(sessionId)?.running ?? useSessions().byId[sessionId]?.running
```

A session the app merely keeps open is shown as `N open · idle`, its buttons stay
enabled, and the host releases it before touching any file. When neither source
knows the session, the panel falls back to the host's own summary instead of
inventing an answer.

## The panel

The panel is a card grid rather than a table: each workspace is an
`article.wsm-card` carrying a status dot, its name, the canvas path, activity
badges and four actions (rebuild / merge / rename / delete). Actions disable
themselves only while a session is *running* — a workspace that is merely open
still operates, because an idle holder is released before the move.

Styling rides on the host theme instead of hard-coded colours, so the panel
follows the Harness light/dark switch:

```css
.wsm-card {
  border: .5px solid var(--dsw-alias-settings-card-stroke);
  border-radius: var(--dsw-radius-xl);
  background: var(--dsw-alias-settings-card-fill);
}
.wsm-card:hover { background: var(--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-hover); }
```

While the first read is in flight the grid shows three pulsing skeletons, so the
panel never flashes an empty state. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns the pulse off.

## Tests

```bash
node --test
```

The suite runs without the harness: `test/fakes.js` stands in for the storage,
the workspace registry, `sessionController` and the agent registry, publishing
real files into a throwaway `DSH_HOME`.

- `paths.test.js` — `samePath` / `titleFollowsPath` / `encodeId` edge cases.
- `move.test.js` — the whole move transaction: success, a held session, a turn in
  flight, an empty log, a failing publish, a successor that reads back short, a
  store that still lists the parked id, and the repair path when a move is
  repeated.
- `contract.test.js` — loads `client.js` in a `vm` and asserts the Client mounts
  exactly the descriptors the Host registers (ids, namespaces, parameter wires)
  and that both locale dictionaries carry the same keys.

## Notes and limits

- Moving a session does not move the files on disk. Only the session's recorded
  working directory changes.
- Nested workspaces are legal in current DSH builds, so nesting is not refused;
  only a target that cannot host a workspace (missing, not a directory, not
  writable) is.
- Sessions stored in an older format report `migration-required`; open them once
  so the harness upgrades them, then move them.
- A forked session keeps its `parentSession` link and its inherited event offset;
  the parent stays where it is, so move parents first if you want the whole tree
  in one directory.
- The move is refused while the session runs. Stop it, move it, re-open it.
- A session the app has open but idle used to be refused: the store keeps its write
  ownership, so no successor artifact can be published for it. The plugin now
  releases an idle holder first (`#releaseHeld` disposes the agent's own Cordis
  scope and re-reads the registry to confirm) and only refuses when the release
  did not happen. A session mid-turn is still refused: it has real work to finish.
- Every seat draws the same occupancy chips from `listWorkspaces`, so a blocked
  workspace is visible before a button is pressed.
- `删除 / Delete` removes the record only; the directory and its session files are
  left on disk, and the sessions are archived so they are easy to find again.
- The plugin never edits committed bytes: it publishes a successor through
  `sessionPersistence`, so the store's no-rewrite rule and framing checks stay
  intact.

## Verification

```bash
# 1. the loader row exists and the bundle applied
cordis_inspect_query Config.listConfigs name=dsh-workspace-control
# 2. the Client half registered its three seats (live Slots tree)
cordis_inspect_query Slots.listSubTree root=sidebar.panellist
cordis_inspect_query Slots.listSubTree root=main
cordis_inspect_query Slots.listSubTree root=sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item
```

`sidebar.panellist` and `main` both carry the id `workspace-control`; the first is
the sidebar button, the second the panel it dispatches. The same panel is also
reachable from `settings.section` (id `workspace-control-settings`).

Finished results retire on their own after a few seconds, so an operation that
succeeded cannot leave a banner sitting in the panel.

The offline checks (no harness needed) cover the refusal paths, `inspect`, and the
boot self-heal against a fake registry:

```bash
node .scratch/smoke.mjs
```

The same operation is reachable by the agent as the `workspace_control` tool, so
the move can be exercised without the UI:

```
workspace_control { "action": "inspect", "sessionId": "session-<uuid>" }
workspace_control { "action": "move", "sessionId": "session-<uuid>", "target": "D:\\target" }
```

`action=listWorkspaces` reports every workspace with its real session count and
its blockers (`running` / `open`), which is the same data the panel draws its
occupancy chips from. `action=inspect` is read-only and reports the recorded
directory, the owning workspace, whether the session runs, and the storage format. `action=move`
performs the move. Every step appends a line to `.workspace-control.log` next to this
package, which is the first place to look when a move refuses.

## The cached title follows the header

The Session list builds its projection column from
`sessionProjectionCache.cachedSnapshot(header)`, and that read only matches a
stored record whose lifecycle identity (`formatVersion`, `createdAt`, `cwd`,
`isSeeded`) equals the header it is handed. A move rewrites `cwd` in the header,
so the record written before the move stops matching and the sidebar renders the
row as “未命名” (unnamed) even though the cached title row is intact.

A move therefore ends with a cold projection read off the complete log
(`sessionProjectionCache.coldSnapshot(header, inheritedEventCount, events)`),
which folds the log against the new identity and writes a fresh checkpoint
back. `action=move` reports the outcome as `projections: { asOfSeq, keys }`, and
repeating a move to the directory a session already lives in re-runs only this
repair step.

## Reloading the plugin without restarting the harness

The host half is reloaded by toggling its entry through the plugin manager —
`plugin_manager` `set_plugin` with `target: "include:workspace-control"`,
`enabled: false` then `enabled: true` — which re-imports `index.js` in place. The
client half is refreshed with the page. Neither needs a DSH restart.

# billion-context

English | 中文

Context-compression plugin — billion-context is all you need.

small context windows (100K is enough) · 5× fewer tokens · month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) · high compression quality

npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local

                                           

--- > **Cache health at a glance:** a healthy session keeps a **95–97%** prefix-cache hit rate — compression itself costs ≤2%. Sustained lower? Check attribution with `/acp` or `/acp-cache` (see [FAQ](#faq)); usual causes, in order: upstream cache TTL expiry · model switch · a bili bug (please report) · other/unknown. ## Community QQ Group: 1056132097 (full) 1108730198 (full) 1129868472 (open) --- ## 📄 Paper / Preprint - **[Model-Driven Incremental Hierarchical Compression: Training-Free Multi-Generational Context Management for Long-Lived Coding Agents](./paper/model-driven-incremental-hierarchical-compression-training-free-multi-generational-context-management-for-long-lived-coding-agents.md)** (English, v0.2) > 📝 **The paper itself is open-sourced under the MIT License as part of the codebase (`paper/`). It is a living document — anyone may edit it; improvements are welcome via pull request.** A production-scale longitudinal study: 4.5 months, three hosts, 174,327 model calls, 18.76B cumulative input tokens (~24.7B across all hosts), zero window violations on 204,800-token models, marathon sessions of 8,584–12,049 calls. ### 📊 Independent Third-Party Benchmarks - **[1,500-Item Cross-Benchmark Evaluation (`LongMemEval-S` · `ContextBench` · `MemoryAgentBench`)](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.md)** ([中文版](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.zh-CN.md)) — head-to-head comparison of `billion-context` (`v0.1.202`) against `full` context and 3 RAG arms (`bm25`, `embedding`, `embedding-rerank`) with `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash`, `Qwen3-Embedding-8B`, `Qwen3-Reranker-4B`, and `Pi Agent`: **#1 on ContextBench** (`0.3097` Utilized F1, `-58.3%` cost vs `full`), **+16.6% over best RAG on LongMemEval-S** (`79.20%` vs `62.60%`, `-71.1%` independent-session cost vs `full`), and **100% survival on 1.48M-token MemoryAgentBench TTL** (`30×` steady-state compression where `full` fails `199/199`). --- `billion-context` sits between **any** agent and its model API, rewriting Anthropic/OpenAI streams with [acp-kernel](https://github.com/ranxianglei/acp-kernel) compression. The model decides **when** and **what** to compress into high-fidelity summaries — not a hard truncation limit. ## Why Long coding sessions blow up context. Each provider charges per token, and once you pass the context window the session degrades or dies. `billion-context` compresses consumed conversation into layered summaries so you can run a single session for days — billions of tokens through one context window. Unlike a host's built-in summarizer, compression here is **incremental, reversible, and prefix-cache friendly**: summaries are written in small ranges, can be decompressed on demand, and the cache prefix stays intact. ## How it works ``` Agent (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Aider ...) │ you point the agent's base URL at the proxy ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ billion-context│ 1. parse the request (Anthropic or OpenAI shape) │ proxy │ 2. run acp-kernel compression on the conversation │ │ 3. inject a `compress` tool + compression philosophy │ │ 4. forward to the real model API │ │ 5. rewrite the streaming response └─────────────────┘ │ ▼ real model API (Anthropic / OpenAI / compatible) ``` ### Context-management tools The proxy injects four context-management tools into the conversation; the model calls them itself as context grows, and the proxy executes `compress` server-side so folded ranges stay summarized in history until restored: - **`compress`** — fold a message range into a detailed summary. - **`decompress`** — restore a compressed range when exact details are needed again. - **`search_context`** — keyword search over compressed summaries and visible messages. - **`acp_status`** — context-usage overview plus which ranges are still compressible. ## Which do I need? Pick by your client: | Client | Use | |---|---| | **pi** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili pi` (launcher) or `bili plugin install pi` (native); standalone [`billion-context-pi`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi) remains usable — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#pi-pidev-coding-agent) | | **opencode** (1.x / 2.x) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili opencode` (launcher) or `bili plugin install opencode` (native); standalone [`opencode-acp`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/opencode-acp) remains usable on 1.x — full guide: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) | | **omp** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili omp` (built-in plugin) or `bili plugin install omp` (self-spawning native plugin, no launcher) | | **dsh** | `bili dsh` (launcher — full native plugin via `--patch`) or `bili plugin install dsh` ≡ `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` (one unified lane) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **kimi** | `bili plugin install kimi` (self-spawning native, Kimi Code ≥ 2.0.0) or `bili kimi` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **hermes** | `bili plugin install hermes` (self-spawning native, Python plugin #958) or `bili hermes` (cert-MITM) | | **zcode** (Z.ai / bigmodel coding plan) | `bili plugin install zcode` (self-spawning native, #1145) or cert-MITM via the GUI's Settings → Network or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **claude** | `bili claude` (launcher) or `bili plugin install claude` (native posture, #964 — managed settings block + session-owned proxy; see the notes below) | | **codex** | `bili codex` (launcher — the full zero-config posture) or `bili plugin install codex` (MCP-shell tools companion: **start bili first** — the shell never spawns a proxy and never routes codex's own traffic) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli) | | **jcode** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili jcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (compiled Rust binary, no plugin seam, [#962](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/962)) | | **gemini** (Gemini CLI) | `bili gemini` (launcher, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix — launcher-only (no in-loop tool seam, #1043) | | **iflow** (iFlow CLI) | `bili iflow` (launcher, `IFLOW_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix | | **qwen** (Qwen Code) | `bili qwen` (launcher, cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix | | **antigravity** (Antigravity CLI / agy, Google) | `bili antigravity` (launcher, `CLOUD_CODE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — Antigravity's real default upstream, #3129) or `/bili/` prefix — no plugin seam (closed Go language_server; its user-plugin surface is additive-only, #2115) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **mcode** (MiniMax Code) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili mcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (event hooks only, no model-request seam, [#1050](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1050)) | | **aider** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili aider` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (shell-command-only hooks, no tool-injection seam, [#1048](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1048)) | | **copilot** (GitHub Copilot CLI) | `bili copilot` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **amp** (Amp CLI) | `bili amp` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **crush** (Charm Crush) | `bili crush` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Go binary, no plugin seam; built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `base_url`s auto-discovered from crush.json (#2340) | | **zed** (Zed editor) | `bili zed` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Rust editor, no plugin seam; reqwest honors HTTPS_PROXY, CA via SSL_CERT_FILE (Linux env probing); built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `api_url`s auto-discovered from settings.json; loopback providers (ollama/lmstudio) stay direct via NO_PROXY (#2340) | | **goose** (Goose CLI) | `bili goose` (launcher) — rustls trusts no CA file, so no cert-MITM: openai/anthropic legs via `OPENAI_HOST`/`ANTHROPIC_HOST`, custom providers via a regenerated `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT` overlay (#1049) | | **everything else** (no context hook) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili ` (launcher, preferred) or `/bili/` prefix | **Native mode vs standalone extensions.** The host-native plugins (`bili plugin install …`) and the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) are **mutually exclusive** — both active means double compression. The installer makes the switch: it replaces the legacy entries (bare name, `npm:` alias, versioned, path form; array or object shape) and snapshots the original config to `.bili-bak` once; a **project-local** install is not touched — remove that one by hand. As a runtime safety net for manual installs, the native entries set `BILLION_CONTEXT_NATIVE=` synchronously at load so a standalone extension can stand down at action time. On the pi side the marker needs `billion-context-pi` **0.1.72+**, and the pi-native entry scans both pi settings files once its proxy is up and warns loudly when it spots a co-resident legacy entry the installer never saw — that warning is the only visible signal while an old `billion-context-pi` silently double-compresses. ## Install Linux / macOS — install with a user-level prefix (no `sudo`, no npm config changes, and `bili`'s self-update never hits permission errors): ```bash npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local ``` The `bili` command lands in `~/.local/bin` — already on PATH in most distros; if not, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. On nvm or Homebrew Node the default prefix is already user-owned — a plain `npm install -g billion-context` works as-is. On Windows the default prefix (`%APPDATA%\npm`) is also user-writable — plain `npm install -g billion-context`. This installs the `bili` command (`bili-proxy` is kept as an alias). Hitting `EACCES` with an old root-owned prefix? Reinstall with `--prefix=~/.local` (pass the flag again on any future npm reinstall of `bili`) — that is the permanent fix; avoid `sudo`. Prefer containers? A `Dockerfile` ships at the repository root — see [Running in Docker](#running-in-docker) below. ## Quickstart Three ways to use it — pick one: - **Native plugin (most native):** `bili plugin install ` — bili becomes a plugin inside the client; start the client as usual. - **Launcher (config-free):** one `bili ` command brings up the proxy and the client together — no real config file is ever touched. - **URL change (most universal):** prefix your client's baseURL with the proxy origin + `/bili/`. Mechanism details behind these three options (plugin lifecycle, runtime-info protocol, injection priority) live in [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Ports, briefly (#1660): `bili start` (manual) owns `8787`. Everything a lane spawns for you (native hooks, launcher lanes) lives in a separate self-managed zone starting at `18787` — collisions hop +1 and each lane remembers its drift, so zero-config installs never fight you for a port, and a deliberate `bili start` daemon is attached by default. Attach is lane-aware (#2905): a hook rides its own lane's instance first, NEVER another declared lane's — except lanes you list in `native.attachLanePriority` — and the 8787 user-zone daemon stays the LAST-resort fallback. An upgrade-restart that finds the previous build still draining on the lane's port waits for it to release (up to 5s) and rebinds the SAME port instead of drifting (#1723); only a genuinely occupied port hops +1 — and that hop is now logged loudly. ### Option 1 — Native plugin (`bili plugin install pi` / `omp` / `opencode` / `dsh` / `kimi` / `hermes` / `zcode`) The proxy lives inside the client: install once, then start the client exactly as you always do — no launcher command, no env vars, no fixed port, no URL edits. Supported today for **pi**, **omp**, **opencode** (1.x and 2.x), **dsh**, **kimi**, **hermes** and **zcode**: ```bash bili plugin install pi # registers a "billion-context" entry in pi's settings (npm form when bili itself was npm-installed) bili plugin install omp # registers an extensions entry in omp's config.yml (~/.omp/agent/config.yml) bili plugin install opencode # registers the plugin in opencode's real config + disables native auto-compaction bili plugin install dsh # runs 'dsh plugin --profile add billion-context' for every existing profile bili plugin install kimi # writes $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/billion-context/kimi.plugin.json (+ installed.json record); per-session routing block lands in config.toml on first start (Kimi Code >= 2.0.0) bili plugin install hermes # copies the Python plugin into ~/.hermes/plugins/billion-context/ (+ machine-owned bili.json sidecar) and enables it via `hermes plugins enable billion-context` bili plugin install zcode # writes hooks.enabled + a SessionStart hook + mcp.servers.bili into ~/.zcode/cli/config.json; per-session routing lands in the bigmodel provider store on first start bili plugin remove # undo (dsh removes through the same channel; config snapshots go to .bili-bak) ``` Where a client has its own plugin channel you can also install natively, skipping bili commands entirely: - **dsh:** `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` is the very command `bili plugin install dsh` drives per profile (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry — pasting a GitHub address installs source without `dist/` and the bundle never loads) — same end state either way (pnpm into the profile, bundled patch layer mounted by dsh itself); remove through the same channel. See the dsh section below. - **opencode:** add the bare npm name to your real config's plugin list — `"plugin": ["billion-context"]` (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry). The package publishes `exports["./server"]` → `dist/agent/opencode-native.js`, so opencode loads it through its own Npm.add machinery and the plugin self-spawns exactly like the bili-installed form. Do the two things the bili installer would have done for you too: set `"compaction": { "auto": false }` in the same config (otherwise OpenCode's native auto-compaction double-compresses) and keep a manual backup of the file first. - **claude:** this repository doubles as a Claude Code plugin marketplace — `/plugin marketplace add ranxianglei/billion-context`, then `/plugin install billion-context@billion-context`, then run `/billion-context:bili-setup` (it drives `bili plugin install claude` for you and tells you to restart). Same end state as the bili installer; the plugin ships no hooks or MCP entries of its own, so nothing double-registers. For pi / omp / kimi / claude there is no client-side channel — `bili plugin install ` writes their config entries for you (kimi's declarative `kimi.plugin.json` + registry record, claude's managed settings block, …). Notes: - Native mode is **mutually exclusive** with the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) — the installer swaps the entries and snapshots the original config (`.bili-bak`). - **pi:** native installs wire in built-in subagents by default (`acp_delegate` / `acp_delegate_wait` / `acp_delegate_cancel`) — how to disable them while keeping context compression: [Pi built-in subagents](#pi-built-in-subagents). - OpenCode legacy sessions, V1/V2 shapes and caveats: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode). - `kimi` reports runtime-info at bootstrap only (static headers can't carry per-request window/model values); subagent tool calls are routed by the proxy's outbound tool-use witness ring (#1685) — no model-visible conversation id. - `hermes`'s native plugin is Python: it points hermes' httpx stack at the proxy via env vars after a health check and stamps per-request headers through an `llm_request` middleware. - `codex` is the one client a plugin install cannot make self-sufficient: codex routes model traffic via env only (no config-file routing seam for the default ChatGPT-login provider — a managed `model_providers` block would force API-key auth and drop subscription login), and an MCP server cannot inject env into its parent. `bili plugin install codex` writes a single `[mcp_servers.bili]` block into `~/.codex/config.toml` (command = node, args = dist/mcp.js) exposing the four ACP tools; at session start the shell resolves a proxy — env `BILI_MCP_PROXY` > the live-instance record (any lane's proxy or a `bili start` daemon) > the 8787 user-zone default (#1660 removed the install-time origin bake, #403) — nothing reachable → `tools/list` fails with -32003. So: start bili first (`bili start` or any client's lane proxy), export HTTPS_PROXY yourself if you also want compression, or use `bili codex` for the zero-config full posture. Mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli). - `claude` has a native posture (#964): managed settings block + `SessionStart` hook + MCP shell; the hook rides the self-managed port zone (#1660) and re-pins the managed URL to the live origin each session, so port drift self-heals. Since #1821 the MCP shell also watches the proxy mid-session (30 s tick × 3 failures) and respawns a dead lane proxy itself, so model requests recover within ~90 s instead of a new session (same semantics as the zcode lane). Opt out with `BILI_NATIVE_CLAUDE=0` (passthrough). Mechanics: [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). **Known limitation (#2290):** the Claude Desktop app's Code tab (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-desktop`) sets its own `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on its embedded Claude Code, overriding the managed one — desktop sessions bypass the proxy entirely while the managed block's `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1` still applies, so they get neither bili compression nor native auto-compaction. The hook warns loudly at session start (and records it for `bili doctor`, which also flags machines where Claude Desktop is installed alongside the native lane); terminal sessions are unaffected. **Field-tested 2026-10-06 (#2290):** putting `HTTPS_PROXY` in the settings `env` block produced zero CONNECT traffic to a live MITM-enabled proxy on Claude Desktop 2.19675.1 / embedded CC 2.1.288 (Windows 11) — the variable reaches no network stack there, matching the CLI behavior of that era — note that newer builds (CC 2.1.301+) DO honour `HTTPS_PROXY` on the CLI, which is why `bili claude` routes via the `/bili/` base-URL rewrite — the launcher gives this lane no proxy and no CA at all, and a child that brings a proxy of its own gets the loopback hosts merged into `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` so that leg stays direct regardless of its proxy behavior (#3446). As of that version there is no usable routing seam on the desktop Code tab; the lane stays tracked in [#2290](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/2290) in case upstream changes behavior. Desktop-only users can restore native auto-compact with `bili plugin remove claude`. Since #5095 the managed block also installs a `SubagentStart` hook (`node /dist/claude-subagent-hook.js`) that mints a per-dispatch lane token into each subagent's context: subagents that ride the parent's session id with no agent-id headers (the VS Code extension build, #4352) key onto their own `|sub:…:t:` compression lanes, so parallel same-type dispatches stop merging (and the token disappears from later requests once the first message folds — those fall back to the fingerprint lane). Uninstall removes the hook with the managed block. - `zcode` has a native posture (#1145): managed `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` block + per-session provider `baseURL` rewrite. Full mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md). - `jcode` and `aider` have no native mode (no plugin/MCP/tool-injection seam: #962, #1048) — use `bili jcode` / `bili aider`. - `copilot`, `amp` and `goose` are launcher-only (#1049); goose cannot be cert-MITMed (rustls trusts no CA file) and rides plain-HTTP base-URL redirects instead. ### Option 2 — Launcher (`bili pi` / `bili codex` / `bili claude` / `bili omp` / `bili opencode` / `bili hermes` / `bili dsh` / `bili codebuddy` / `bili qoder` / `bili trae` / `bili jcode` / `bili kimi` / `bili gemini` / `bili iflow` / `bili qwen` / `bili antigravity` / `bili mcode` / `bili aider` / `bili copilot` / `bili amp` / `bili goose`) The launcher wraps a client in one command: it starts a proxy on an independent port (a fresh instance is always spawned — a port is never reused), then points the client at it — **certificate-based MITM** where the client honors proxy/CA env vars, or an isolated **`/bili/` config rewrite** where it doesn't. No real config file is ever edited; the client's own config is READ to discover which HTTPS upstream hosts it talks to, and those hosts are whitelisted for MITM so the proxy can TLS-terminate exactly them and blind-tunnel everything else. ```bash bili pi # launch pi through the proxy — file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider, real ~/.pi untouched bili codex # launch codex through the proxy bili claude # launch claude through the proxy bili omp # pi-style, file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider + compaction cancel, real ~/.omp untouched bili opencode # OpenCode (1.x & 2.x): full guide in the [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) section below bili hermes # file-free (#535): hermes proxy env (HTTPS_PROXY + combined CA bundle via SSL_CERT_FILE) — https via CONNECT MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; real ~/.hermes untouched bili dsh # deepseek-harness: full native plugin injected via --patch (#941) — real dsh tools, session-bound /acp + /acp-cache (plugin mode); non-loopback upstreams ride proxy envs, loopback keeps the overlay DSH_HOME rewrite (#535); evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH Tool Router

Lazy tool discovery for DSH: hides every tool schema from the model's prefill
and reveals exactly one tool on demand through a **decision model API**.

- **Prefill cost:** one small `find_tool` schema instead of every mounted tool
  (26 schemas on a default Standard profile — see [Why?](#why)).
- **Stage 0** — full-surface send: every mounted tool (≤ 24) carries a
  160-char criterion, ordered by a stopword-filtered lexical rank (the rank
  only bounds pathological mounts — d1-omni does not saturate as the choice
  count grows; see [Why?](#why)).
- **Stage 1** — one `POST /v1/systemone` to the decision model API: a
  `bestTool` choice plus a `usable` question kept as telemetry only
  (~235–500 tokens, ~6–7 s on-device).
- **Stage 2** — accept iff `confidence >= 0.70`: return the winner's JSON
  Schema and reveal exactly that one tool; otherwise return a
  **probability-ordered shortlist** whose reason names the closest match, so
  the model can retry with that exact tool name (or send an empty request to
  get the whole catalog). Exact tool-name requests skip the decision call and
  reveal instantly.

## Why?

Fresh session, first message, server-reported `usage.prompt_tokens` —
the DSH **Standard preset** (the platform default) versus this plugin's
`no-prefill` preset:

| Cost before the first word | Standard | no-prefill |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prefill tokens | **6,559** | **283** |
| System prompt | 5,816 chars | 372 chars |
| Tool schemas shipped up front | **26 schemas (21,417 B)** | 1 schema (697 B) |

Standard makes the model ingest a 5.8k-character system prompt plus **every**
mounted tool schema — 6,559 tokens — before it emits a single word, and pays
it again on every subsequent turn. `no-prefill` ingests 283 tokens (**23×
less**, 96% smaller prefill): a slim persona plus the single `find_tool`
schema. On the measured backend that difference was ~40 s versus ~14 min of
prompt evaluation for the first reply.

What that buys you:

- **Latency** — time-to-first-word scales with the whole tool shelf today.
  Reveal-on-demand makes it scale with the tool you actually call.
- **Context budget** — 6.5k tokens of standing preamble is 6.5k tokens you
  don't have for code, conversation, and results. On a 32k window that's ~20%
  of the model's world spent before work starts.
- **Reliability on small models** — a model reading 26 schemas behaves like a
  model reading 26 instructions it must never violate. One schema at a time is
  one schema to follow; the rest of the shelf doesn't exist for it.
- **Pay for what you use** — a turn that calls no tool costs 283 tokens
  instead of 6,559. A turn that calls one tool reveals that one schema once;
  the other 25 are never sent.

If a session ends up using most tools anyway, the gap narrows — but the unused
half of the shelf is exactly what a default profile charges for from word one.

## What the bundle patch declares

`cordis.patch.yml` (applied when the bundle is selected):

1. **`preset-no-prefill`** — an agent preset whose composition is only
   `persona` + `dsh-tool-router`. The persona tells the model: no tools are
   declared; call `find_tool` first — and if a result carries no schema,
   retry with an exact tool name or an empty request instead of giving up.
2. **Host tool rows enabled** — `tool-bash`, `tool-fs`, `tool-fs-search`,
   `tool-todo`, `tool-web` flipped to `disabled: false`, plus a `present`
   row inserted. Discovery needs the tools to exist somewhere; preset-scoped
   registrations shadow host ones, so other presets keep their own behavior.
   The slim preset keeps the Agent Presets page showing only `find_tool`.

## Prerequisites

- DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 (bundles mechanism with `dsh.bundle.patch`).
- A running **decision model API** that speaks `POST /v1/systemone`
  (the router defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/systemone`; edit
  `ROUTER_BASE` in `index.js` to point at another host or port).
- `pnpm` on PATH of the host running DSH (the plugin manager installs
  through pnpm; the CLI forwards pnpm arguments).

## Install

**From GitHub (recommended):** Plugins → install → spec

```
git+https://github.com/residenthiago2011/DSH-Tool-Router.git
```

or via the CLI:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add git+https://github.com/residenthiago2011/DSH-Tool-Router.git
```

**From a prebuilt tarball:** download
[`dsh-tool-router.tgz`](https://github.com/residenthiago2011/DSH-Tool-Router/releases/latest/download/dsh-tool-router.tgz)
from Releases, then install from the local path (also accepted: absolute
path, git URL, or an npm registry name after publishing):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-tool-router.tgz
```

Then select the bundle on the Plugins page (installation enables it by
default) and restart DSH if the profile runs without HMR.

## Uninstall

Deselect/remove the bundle on the Plugins page. The preset row and the host
tool flips vanish with the bundle patch; other presets are untouched.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | The router plugin: registers `find_tool`, masks every other tool per agent, runs the 3-stage decision. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The bundle patch: preset declaration + host tool enablement. |
| `tool-registry.json` | Stage-0 labels and Stage-1 criteria (25 tools, both shells incl. `bash`). |

## Tests

```sh
node router-import-test.mjs   # module shape (no dependencies)
node rank-sim.mjs             # Stage-0 ranking on sample queries (needs tool-registry.json)
node router-e2e-test.mjs      # full flow: arm/deny-set/live reveal — requires the decision endpoint at 127.0.0.1:8081
node restrict-scope-test.mjs   # deny-set vs the global registry (agent-scoped tools)
node router-storm-test.mjs     # mask lifecycle without a decision endpoint; no tools/change listener
```

`router-e2e-test.mjs` uses a stub DSH context that emits `tools/change`
synchronously (the worst case that once caused a ~970x feedback loop), then
drives the real `find_tool` against a live decision endpoint: armed-once,
deny-set dedup, late registration, reveal re-arm, empty-request catalog hint,
and the exact-name fast path. `ALL_PASS` is expected.

`router-storm-test.mjs` needs no endpoint. It pins the three properties that
matter for survival: (1) no `tools/change` listener exists after mount, so a
foreign event storm cannot re-enter the plugin — 200 injected events must
produce 0 `restrict()` calls; (2) an agent that existed before the plugin
mounted is adopted at its first step boundary; (3) a re-mount rebuilds
`revealed` from the session log, so tools the conversation already used are not
hidden again, and asking for one of them answers `already_available: true`
without a registry write.

## Notes

- `find_tool` registers with a standard JSON Schema
  (`type/properties/required/additionalProperties`). A raw register with
  author-style parameters reaches the LLM unconstrained — the model then
  calls with `{}`. Always compile.
- The empty-request catalog hint and the exact-name fast path exist for
  small models; see `execute()` in `index.js`.
- Diagnostics go to stderr and are mirrored to `~/.dsh/tool-router.log`
  (`DSH_TOOL_ROUTER_LOG` overrides the path, `DSH_TOOL_ROUTER_LOG=0` disables
  the mirror). The harness does not keep plugin stderr, and the log is what made
  the two host-killing incidents below diagnosable after the fact.

## Reconcile at the agent step boundary, never inside `tools/change`

This is the load-bearing design rule, learned from two hosts that died.

`tools.restrict()` and `tools.register()` publish `tools/change` **synchronously**,
so a listener that reacts to `tools/change` by changing the registry re-enters
itself. Two such plugins form a publication/withdrawal feedback loop. Measured:
532 events in two seconds, then 136 in one second, then `crash-*-host.log`
(`~/.dsh/tool-router.log`, 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-28; the 10-26 storm grew the
log to 130.5 MB). In the second incident the router was *inert* — every line was
`1 armed, 0 pending`, zero re-arms — because the other half of the loop was a
different plugin that also reconciles on `tools/change`.

The fix is structural, not a guard: **the router subscribes to nothing in that
event.** Late registrations are picked up at `agent/pre-step`, and `recompute()`
still dedups on the deny-set key, so an unchanged surface performs no registry
write at all. The trade-off is bounded and cheap: a tool registered in the
middle of a step stays visible until the next step boundary.

## Rebuild `revealed` from the session log, not from plugin memory

`revealed` (the set of tools already handed to the model) is derived state. It
must survive a host restart, because the *conversation* survives: the model keeps
calling tools it used before the restart.

Measured on 2026-10-28 (session `35a5fef0`, turn 17): the host restarted, the
fresh plugin instance armed its mask with `revealed=0`, and `bash` / `read` /
`edit` — used 19 / 5 / 9 times in the previous turn — became invisible. The model
kept calling them, got `Error: unknown tool "bash"`, called `find_tool`, retried.
Each retry resent the whole context: **419,672 input tokens, 98.9% of that
turn**, for three tool calls that the model already knew how to make.

`adopt()` therefore seeds the set from `ctx.get('sessions').get(agent.id).snapshotEvents()`,
adding every `tool/call` name. Re-mounting after this change restores 8 tools on
that same session and produces zero `unknown tool` errors.

`find_tool` answers `already_available: true` when the requested tool was already
visible, and a seeded tool asked for again makes **no** registry write — measured
`restrict()` call count unchanged, and the log line reads
`"bash" was already available via exact name match (no re-arm)`.

## An agent that predates the plugin

`agent/created` does not fire for an agent that already exists when the plugin
mounts (a live bundle enable, an HMR reload, a resumed session). `agent/pre-step`
adopts such an agent on its first step; without that it stays untracked and never
gets a mask — every schema stays in prefill, silently.

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# Respire for DeepSeek Harness

English | [简体中文](https://github.com/risense-ai/respire-dsh/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md) **npm package: [@rsrsai/dsh](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rsrsai/dsh)** ## Install with AI — copy this prompt Paste the entire prompt into **the assistant inside DeepSeek Harness**: ```text Install the Respire memory plugin @rsrsai/dsh in my current DeepSeek Harness profile. Read and follow https://github.com/risense-ai/respire-dsh#readme, then perform the installation rather than only explaining the steps. Check Node.js 24+, Harness compatibility (validated against 0.2.1-rc.2), and plugin_manager availability. Reuse my existing rsrs environment; if rsrs is missing, install it with npm install -g rsrs-cli@latest in the profile's execution environment. Run rsrs --version and rsrs --client-only status --json. Report any required login, library unlock, model setup, or host runtime action for me to complete in rsrs; do not request secrets in chat or manage the runtime. Inspect installed bundles first. If the old @rsrsai/respire-dsh bundle exists, disable and remove that bundle through plugin management before installing its replacement. If the manager requires a profile stop or restart, tell me the required action before proceeding. Preserve my memory library, account, rsrs configuration, and unrelated plugins. Avoid duplicate installation if the new bundle is already present. Use plugin_manager with {"action":"install_bundle","target":"@rsrsai/dsh"}. Install the npm bundle, not a Git dependency or only a terminal npm install. Verify that exactly one enabled respire-memory entry comes from @rsrsai/dsh. Tell me when to restart Harness, then verify recall in a new conversation. Ask me for a non-sensitive test fact before testing storage and check the actual record. Verify the stop reminder in a separate recall turn without a successful explicit store. Report the installed version, checks actually performed, and remaining user actions; do not claim end-to-end success before observing it. ``` ## Overview Native TypeScript memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness. It registers stable rules with `systemPrompt.section`, recalls memory through `agent/pre-step`, and checks for new findings through `agent/turn-stopping`. Respire (`rsrs`) owns storage, deduplication, encryption, model inference, accounts, and synchronization. ## Install Requires Node.js 24+, DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2**, and an installed `rsrs` CLI. The plugin uses the Harness `agents`, `systemPrompt`, `subprocess`, and `workingDirectory` services already provided by the standard desktop profile. Other Harness versions have not been validated. Install the engine separately if needed: ```sh npm install -g rsrs-cli@latest rsrs --version rsrs --client-only status --json ``` Configure accounts, unlock the library, and install optional semantic models with the CLI's own interactive workflow. The plugin does not install software, collect passwords, start a runtime, or change account configuration. It always calls `rsrs --client-only`, so a running host runtime is required. In Harness, ask the agent to invoke `plugin_manager` with: ```json { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "@rsrsai/dsh" } ``` For local development, use this checkout's absolute directory as `target`. Compiled `lib/` files are included in Git and release archives; installation requires no build scripts. Restart Harness after replacing an installed version. The published package is [@rsrsai/dsh](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rsrsai/dsh). Use a versioned target such as `@rsrsai/dsh@0.1.3` to pin an installation. `@rsrsai/cli` is the engine; `@rsrsai/dsh` is the Harness plugin. Running `npm install @rsrsai/dsh` in a regular terminal does not activate the plugin in a Harness profile. After installation, restart Harness and check that exactly one enabled `respire-memory` entry comes from `@rsrsai/dsh`. npm installation and module loading have been verified; a full desktop conversation has not. ### Migrate from the previous Git installation If `@rsrsai/respire-dsh` is installed, remove that old bundle in Harness plugin management, then install `@rsrsai/dsh` as above. Disable the old bundle first if it is still in use; stop the profile if the manager requests it. Keep the existing memory library, account, and `rsrs` configuration. ## Behavior | Trigger | Result | | --- | --- | | First accepted user input per live agent | Read engine status; report missing runtime, locked library, missing session, or a small library when applicable | | Accepted user message | `recall --titles --json`; inject at most 5 titles into the same model step | | `记：`, `存：`, `记录：`, `记住：`, `remember:` | Attempt `remember` once, then inject a success, pending, or failure receipt | | `/nomem` or `#nomem` followed by whitespace/end | Skip that message's automatic recall; status and stop checks remain enabled | | `$skill: name` prefix | Remove the skill selector from the recall query | | Natural stop | At most one reminder per agent/turn; a successful explicit store suppresses it | Only messages attributed to the human (`source.kind === 'user'`) trigger work. Plugin contexts, tool loops, and reminder continuations do not trigger recall or store. Repeated admission of the same message ID in one turn is ignored. A new user message with identical text is still processed. Downstream rejection and cancellation prevent new work. A cancelled or timed-out write is **unconfirmed**, not automatically retried: it may already have committed. `pending` means **not written**. The agent must read candidates and decide whether to update, merge, or attach to a parent. Success requires a valid returned ID. Explicit storage initially uses an extracted title and `important`; the receipt and rules tell the agent to refine the title and follow the library workflow. The stop reminder asks the agent to evaluate new facts; it does not automatically archive an entire transcript or guarantee that the model will store a finding. ## Configuration Override the installed row in the user's Harness patch layer. A matching row's `config` is replaced as a whole; unspecified plugin fields use the defaults. ```yaml - id: respire-memory config: enabled: true rsrsPath: rsrs recallLimit: 5 recallThreshold: 0 budgetChars: 1500 minPromptChars: 2 storeNudgeEvery: 1 timeoutMs: 20000 ``` `rsrsPath` is an executable name or absolute path, not a shell command. `storeNudgeEvery: 0` disables reminders; `N` checks every N user-bearing turns per live agent. Changing profiles or reloading the plugin resets volatile reminder state. Recall has a strict character budget; storage receipts are kept intact. ## Privacy and failure behavior - Recall results and storage receipts become model-visible, persistent Harness messages. They may be sent to the configured model provider. Local encryption does not make injected context private from that provider. - Common credential patterns are rejected before recall or explicit storage. This heuristic is not a complete secret scanner. Remove secrets from input; retain only safe purpose/location references in memory. - Logs contain operation/error categories, not prompts, memory bodies, raw CLI errors, or credentials. No plugin-owned files are written to the library. - Engine failure produces a bounded notice and lets the primary task continue. Windows arguments travel as JSON stdin to a constant PowerShell script; POSIX arguments are passed directly. Neither embeds user text in shell source. - Processes run in the agent's verified working directory through the Harness subprocess provider. Its execution environment determines where `rsrs` and the memory runtime must be installed (including remote profiles). ## Development and release ```sh npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run check npm run build npm test npm pack ``` Tests exercise real Cordis event dispatch with a controlled subprocess service; they never write the user's memory library. Production targets the published Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 API. `package-lock.json` locks the verification dependencies. CI runs type checking, build, tests, distribution checks, and generated-file consistency on Linux, macOS, and Windows. To release, update `package.json` and the lockfile, rebuild and commit `lib/`, then push `v`. The release workflow reuses the full CI matrix before publishing `@rsrsai/dsh` to npm with provenance, then uploads the same `.tgz` and SHA-256 checksum to GitHub Releases. Stable versions use `latest`; prereleases use `next`. Ordinary main/PR pushes do not publish. npm publishing uses GitHub OIDC, not a stored npm token. After the initial authenticated publish, configure the package's Trusted Publisher with owner `risense-ai`, repository `respire-dsh`, workflow `release.yml`, and permission to run `npm publish`. Leave the environment blank. The workflow requires `id-token: write` and a GitHub-hosted runner. ## References - [respire-dimcode](https://github.com/risense-ai/respire-dimcode): behavior reference. - [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): host APIs. The plugin icon is a single adaptive SVG: it shows the light variant by default and switches to the dark variant when the Harness theme requests a dark color scheme. The standalone light and dark variants live under `docs/`. The icon is original artwork distributed under this repository's MIT license.

14 个 cherry_* 工具"] --> P W["设置页
设备 · 配对 · 启用范围"] --> P P["dsh-cherry-bridge
连接池 · 订阅缓存 · 作用域"] P <-->|"ws:// · Noise XX"| C["Cherry Studio 桌面端
二维码配对 · 审批"] ``` - 包名：`dsh-cherry-bridge`，插件 id：`cherry-remote` - 传输：默认 `ws://` + Noise XX（加密由 Noise 记录层提供）；桌面端位于 TLS 前置之后时拨 `wss://`，私有 CA 的信任由 `wsTls` 提供 - 工具面：14 个 `cherry_*` 工具，**按工作区**启用，默认**谁都没有**（见「启用范围」） - 设置页与 HTTP 面：宿主 Web 服务器上的同源前缀 `/cherry-remote/api` ## 安装 > **DSH 版本需求**：`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`（由 `package.json` 的 `engines.dsh` 声明；不满足时 bundle 被跳过、设置页里该插件的行被禁用，确需在区间外使用可用 `dsh plugin allow-version` 精确豁免。0.3.0 需重新评估兼容性后再放开）。 > > **Cherry Studio 兼容范围**：桌面端 **2.1.4 – 2.1.8 已实测**——`v3` 自定义地址二维码需 **2.1.8+**，2.1.4–2.1.7 的 `v2` 二维码同样可用。区间外未经验证：握手只协商协议版本 `[1]`，不兼容时会以 `unreachable` 明确失败，不会静默出错。协议包钉在 `0.7.0` / `0.2.5`，即桌面端 2.1.8 所携带的版本。 ```bash # 从 npm 安装（推荐，钉住版本） npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge@0.2.0 # 安装 npm 最新发布版 npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge # 从 GitHub 源码安装（与 npm 发布同一提交） npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:SAXEM1997/dsh-cherry-bridge#v0.2.0 ``` 本包自带 `cordis.patch.yml`（`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向它）， dsh-plugin-manager 据此自动插入插件行。手工加行等价于： ```yaml - id: cherry-remote name: 'dsh-cherry-bridge' config: perSessionCacheBytes: 2097152 rateBudgetPerSecond: 32 ``` ### 首次配对 1. 在 Cherry Studio 桌面端打开 **remote access → 添加设备**：该界面显示**二维码**， 配对信息要点开扫码后的页面才看得到。 2. **扫这个二维码**（微信、浏览器等均可），复制页面上显示的配对信息。 3. 在 DSH 里调用 `cherry_pair`（设置页向导亦可），粘贴这段配对信息。 4. **双向核对 6 位验证码**：与桌面端显示的数字人工比对一致后再在桌面端批准。 5. 批准后设备档案写入数据目录（`devices.json`，`0600`），其 `desktopIdentity` 被 pin 住， 此后每次连接都校验 Noise 对端静态公钥与 pin 一致，防二维码被劫持后的中间人替换。 ## 快速上手 ```text cherry_pair → 粘贴扫码页的配对信息，核对 6 位验证码 cherry_devices → 看设备与连接状态（前缀即可选中，如 "dev-A"） cherry_agents → 列设备上的 agent，拿 agentId cherry_sessions → 列某 agent 的会话，拿 sessionId cherry_read → 读会话历史（默认取最新 100 条，从新到旧） cherry_send → 发消息并等待终态，返回助手文本 cherry_interactions → 看待答的提问/审批卡；cherry_respond 作答 ``` ## 配置 | 键 | 类型 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dataDir` | string | `$DSH_HOME/cherry-remote`（回退 `~/.dsh/cherry-remote`） | 插件数据目录，存放 `identity.key` 与 `devices.json`（均 `0600`）。 | | `perSessionCacheBytes` | number | `2097152`（2 MiB） | 每个会话的**本地**订阅事件缓存上限，超出按 LRU 丢弃最旧事件并 `warn`。 | | `rateBudgetPerSecond` | number | `32` | 每设备平滑请求预算（请求/秒）。桌面端共享额度在 ≤2.1.6 是 64 req/s、≥2.1.7 是 256 req/s，且只有新版本才把超限降级为单请求 `RATE_LIMITED`（旧版本直接 close `1011` 终止会话），故按更严格的一代取保守值。内容读取（`agent.content.read`）按 8:1 派生独立一档，且**封顶 512/s**（该额度两代一致）。 | | `wsTls` | object | — | 每次 `wss` 拨号的**扁平** `tls.connect` 选项（只接受 `rejectUnauthorized` / `ca`），供桌面端位于私有 CA 或自签 TLS 前置之后时由运维提供信任；配对与重连**两个拨号点**共用。**不写入设备档案、不写日志、不进诊断报告。** 整个对象要么按原样生效、要么整体忽略：未知键或不可用值按名 `warn` 后回退 Node 默认信任库（不部分应用）。 | > `wsTls.ca` 是 **PEM 内容**（证书文本本身），不是文件路径。 > ⚠️ `cordis.patch.yml` 的 `config` 是**整体替换**，不与默认值合并。删掉一个键得到的是 > 插件默认值；键存在但值非法（`0`、负数、字符串）会按名 `warn` 后回落默认值。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `cherry_devices` | 列出已配对设备及连接状态（`connected`/`connecting`/`offline`/`disabled`/`identity-mismatch`）。 | | `cherry_agents` | 列出某设备上可用的 agent（分页）。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`（`limit` 或 `safety-bound`，后者是 1000 条内部上限）；停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用同一 device 与过滤条件把它回传为 `cursor` 即可从停点继续（此时 `limit` 约束的是下一次回答）；跨工具/设备/过滤条件的令牌会被**本地拒绝**，不会转发给对端。 | | `cherry_workspaces` | 列出某 agent 的**已注册**工作区，以及是否存在系统工作区。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`；停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用相同过滤条件回传为 `cursor` 即可续读。 | | `cherry_sessions` | 列出某 agent 的会话，可按工作区过滤。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`（`limit` 或 `safety-bound`），停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用同一 device 与**相同过滤条件**把它回传为 `cursor` 即可从停点继续（此时 `limit` 约束的是下一次回答）；跨工具/设备/过滤条件的令牌会被**本地拒绝**。 | | `cherry_read` | 读会话消息历史快照，**从新到旧**返回（`limit` 丢掉的是**最旧**的消息）。失败消息在桌面端给出时附带 `failure: {reasonCode, retryable, message}`（对端分类、是否值得重试、对端自己的有界摘要；其 `source`/`context` 不投影到回答里）。附件 part 只回 `name`/`mediaType`/`byteLength`，`content` 为空——字节不取。这覆盖桌面端可能发来的两种形状：`file` part（`name` 即文件名，`byteLength` 取自它的 ref）；以及桌面端用于**未上传**附件的旧式 `data` part——`name: "file"`，元数据以 JSON 形式放在 `content.text` 里（`{"mediaType":…,"filename":…}`），同样字段被取出结构化，`filename: null` 则不报 `name`，且只有当该对象里的每个键都是这两个上报字段时才清空 `content`（带额外键时保留原始文本）。其他 `name` 的 `data` part（例如任务事件）不是附件，原样透传。被截断时 `truncated` + `truncationReason` 一定说明：`limit` 表示你设的条数到了，提高 `limit` 即可；`aggregate-bytes` 表示单次回答达到了**输出大小上限**——与 `limit` 无关，提高 `limit` 只会多付往返、仍停在同一预算。**被挡下的更旧消息用 `messagesResumeCursor` 续读**：把本次返回的 `messagesResumeCursor` 原样传给下一次调用的 `messagesResumeCursor` 参数即可从停点继续（`limit` 此时约束的是**从停点起**本次最多返回多少条），长历史分几次回答读完。停点不可命名时**没有**这个令牌（`truncated` 仍为 `true`，**缺失本身不代表历史已到底**；补救按 `truncationReason` 分：`limit` 可以提高 `limit`，`aggregate-bytes` 不行——被挡住的旧消息在这一回答里拿不到，详见[错误与限制](#错误与限制)）。两种令牌：`cursor:`（整窗读完后的 peer 分页位置）与 `after:`（停在窗内，续读从最新端扫到该消息、返回它更旧的那些）。不是本工具发出的令牌会被**本地拒绝**（不转发给桌面端——桌面端会静默回退到最新页）；`after:` 锚点在历史里找不到则**报错**，不会返回空结果。 | | `cherry_events` | 读取该会话缓冲区内比 `cursor` 更新的事件，并在投递后 ack。返回 `{events, nextCursor}`；把 `nextCursor` 作为下次的 `cursor` 传回即可续读。 | | `cherry_create` | 在 agent 工作区创建会话（工作区选择**必填**；创建后回读身份）。 | | `cherry_send` | 向会话发消息，默认等待运行到终态并返回助手文本；`wait: false` 立即返回命令回执。内容被截断时 `messagesTruncated`/`messagesTruncationReason` 说的是**消息**被截断（丢更旧的）；`deadline` 表示**回答自身的装配时限**到了（见下），已读到的内容照常返回。 | | `cherry_wait` | 只等待该会话在途执行收敛（不发送新消息）。 | | `cherry_interactions` | 列出该会话**待答**的交互卡（提问 / 审批）。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`；停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用 `sessionId` 相同的调用回传为 `cursor` 即可续读（`limit` 计的是过滤**前**的对端条目）。 | | `cherry_respond` | 应答交互卡：提问必须全量作答，审批走 `decision`。 | | `cherry_cancel` | 取消会话在途执行（`expectedExecutionId` 必填）。 | | `cherry_pair` | 用「扫码后页面显示的配对信息」建立与桌面端的配对。 | | `cherry_unpair` | 解除配对：断开连接并从设备档案删除。 | `device` 参数接受**精确 `deviceId`**，或 **`deviceId` 前缀 / 显示名前缀**；多项命中返回 `ambiguous-device` + `candidates`，一个都没命中返回 `not-found` + `known`。 `cherry_send(wait: true)` / `cherry_wait` 的 `status` 有 **8 个取值**：四个协议终态 （`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`interrupted`），加上 `awaiting-interaction`（出现待答 交互卡，运行仍活着）、`timeout`（窗口用尽，**不是失败**，随附部分内容，停点可命名时再带游标）、 `idle`（`cherry_wait` 遇到没有在途执行的会话，立即返回快照）、`subscription-lost` （事件订阅丢失且重建失败，运行结局**不可知**，随附修复指引）。 ## 错误与限制 - 读方法在重连后**单次**重放；桌面端 ≥2.1.7 的限流拒绝（`RATE_LIMITED` + `retryAfterMs`） 也在调用方预算内等待后**单次**重放。**命令永不重放**——写操作丢失应答时，携**原 `commandId`** 重试即可，桌面端的命令账本会回放原回执。命令被限流拒绝是另一回事：桌面端在**派发前**就拒绝， 命令根本没执行，错误文本会说明这一点、给出对端要求的等待时间（`retryAfterMs`，对端没给就不写）， 并提示该检查的 `rateBudgetPerSecond`（默认预算远到不了限流）。 - 单个外置内容上限 32 MiB，超过的 part 标 `unavailable`，不回无法校验的部分内容。 - **外置内容装配是进程级限流的**：同时最多 4 个 `{ref}` 在装配（官方客户端的读并发策略）。 单个 ref 的装配峰值约 3× 它的大小，所以**装配峰值**上界是 4×3×32 MiB = 384 MiB，日常远低于此 （4×3×声明大小）。它约束的是**正在装配**的内容，不是全部驻留：已经装配完、被各调用自己持有的内容 不在这个乘积里（每次并发读最多再带一整条消息，因为输出预算只在消息之间检查），parts 缓存另计。 等待槽位也计入等待类回答的时限：排到时限就放弃并把这一 part 标 `unavailable`。 - 历史走查被截断时一定说明（`truncationReason`，`limit` / `aggregate-bytes` / `deadline` 三种含义不同，见上）， 并在停点可命名时给出 `messagesResumeCursor` 续读令牌。**停点不可命名时就不给**：对端位置为空、 带首尾空白或任意控制字符、形如已停用的 v1 令牌、令牌会超过 4096 字符上限、或没有可当锚点的 消息 id——此时 `truncated` 仍为 `true`，**缺失本身不代表历史已到底**。补救按 `truncationReason` 分：`limit` 停点只有在调用方自己握着上限时才靠更宽的 `limit`（`cherry_read` 与四个列表工具）； **wait 类回答的 `limit` 是它自己的固定条数额度**，更旧的历史要用 `cherry_read` 去读。 `aggregate-bytes` 停点不行——预算是它停下的原因，更宽的 `limit` 只会多付往返，被挡住的旧消息 在这一回答里拿不到；`safety-bound` 停点是内部熔断，调用方动不了它；`deadline`（只出现在 wait 类回答）同样改用 `cherry_read` 续读，它没有时限。 **两个面是同一条规则**：消息面的 `messagesResumeCursor` 与四个列表工具的 `resumeCursor` 都只发出本工具会收回的令牌；位置内部的普通空格合法，不会因此被拒。 某条消息自身 parts 没读全时带 `incomplete: true`（wait 类回答里被时限截断的那条消息会带 `partsTruncated: "deadline"`）。 - **等待类回答有自己的装配时限**：`cherry_send(wait: true)` / `cherry_wait` 在窗口结束后仍要读一段历史 （消息页 + 每条消息的 parts + 每个外置 `{ref}` 内容），这一步现在是**有时限的**——截至「你的窗口 + 同样长度的时间」，下限 1 秒、上限 15 秒（即窗口 1 秒 → 最多再等 1 秒；窗口 20 秒 → 最多再等 15 秒）。 链路抖动时不会再有「每个请求各等 5 秒重连」把回答拖到几分钟之后；时限用尽就停走查， 已读到的内容照常返回并标 `messagesTruncationReason: "deadline"`，更旧的历史用 `cherry_read` 续读。 同一条时限也覆盖 **终态与超时回答**所读的会话快照：快照读不到时 回执降级（`aggregateError` + `guidance`），不会把已经确定的运行结局（`status` 与各 id）一起丢掉。 `cherry_wait` 判断「会话是否还有在途执行」的那次**前置快照**同样有时限（从工具入口起算「窗口 + 尾」）： 它在预算内读不到时直接**失败并给出修复指引**——此时还没有回答可降级，运行状态**不可知**，重试是恢复路径； 「500 毫秒窗口却先等 5–10 秒重连与重放」的旧形态因此消失（#51）。前置快照成功之后， idle 回答的历史走查仍从那一刻起算自己的预算（慢但成功的快照不会把走查挤成零）； 代价是两段预算**分开计**，病态调用可能把两段都花掉。 - **已知限制**：`cherry_respond` 让 DSH agent 可代替用户批准 Cherry 端审批卡（MVP 不加拦截层， 信任 DSH 自身的工具审批）；每设备仅申请 `agent` capability；传输默认 `ws://`， `wss://` 要求桌面端位于 TLS 前置之后（本插件不做 TLS 终止；私有 CA 的信任由 `wsTls` 提供）。 > 传输重放、32 MiB/≈3× 内存、空页与游标容忍、完整性语义等工程细节见 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)。 ## 设置页与启用范围 插件同时是 **web client bundle**（`package.json` 的 `dsh.client`，导出 `./client`），通过 `settings.section` 槽位注册 **`cherry-remote`**（导航标签「Cherry 互联」）页面： 设备卡片（启用/停用/删除）、配对向导（粘贴 → 6 位验证码 → 终态）、启用范围面板，以及经 `/cherry-remote/api/events` SSE 推送的实时状态。 14 个工具**按工作区**决定是否出现，机制是**隐藏而非拒绝**（不在范围的会话里不进工具表，省上下文）： - **默认谁都没有**：作用域文档不存在、损坏或读不出来，都按 `selected` + 空列表处理（fail-closed）。 - **`仅选定工作区`**：只有勾选的工作区里的会话才可能出现这些工具；没有工作区的会话始终没有。 - **`全局`**：所有工作区都可见，面板勾选不参与判定。 - **保存即时生效**：对所有 live agent 重装/释放限制层，**下一轮**即生效，无需重启或新建会话。 - **范围只管工具**：设置页与 `/cherry-remote/api` 不受范围影响，被排除的工作区也能自救。 - **不假装**：宿主能力 `pending` / `unsupported` 时面板如实说明，这些工具都**不注册**（fail-closed）。 开发时可单独跑 `npm run dev:ui`，前提是宿主已在 `http://127.0.0.1:23023` 运行； `CHERRY_DEV_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:` 可改端口。作用域文档在 `/scope.json` （`0600`、原子写入、`revision` 单调），HTTP 端点与错误码见 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)。 ## 开发 ```bash npm test # vitest 全量（含 tests/contract/） npm run typecheck # 服务端 + UI 两侧 npm run build # tsdown → dist/index.mjs + dist/index.d.mts npm run build:client # vite → lib/client.js npm run dev:ui # 设置页 dev server（需宿主在 127.0.0.1:23023 运行） npm run prepublishOnly # 发布前闸门：typecheck + test + build + build:client + npm pack --dry-run ``` `dist/` 与 `lib/` 是**随仓库提交**的产物：改完 `src/` 或 `ui/` 必须重跑 `npm run build && npm run build:client` 再提交。开发约定、构建事实、协议依据与设计决策见 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)；发布前请走完 [`docs/e2e-checklist.md`](docs/e2e-checklist.md) （配对 / 发送 / 交互应答 / 断连恢复 / 多设备并存需真机人工核验）。 ## License MIT

manifest.description: Keep the Auto permission preset across DSH restarts: drop the auto-review unload migration during application shutdown, and reopen stored Auto sessions without their integration instead of failing publication

# dsh-auto-preset-guard **让「自动审批」熬过重启 —— 退出 DSH 不再被改写成「完全权限」** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3E63DD?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522.19-3E63DD?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](https://nodejs.org) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/English-version-8B5CF6?style=flat-square)](#english-version)
--- ## 🌟 这是什么 会话里选过 **自动审批**（`auto`），关掉 DSH 再打开，它变成了 **完全权限**（`danger-full-access`，审批策略 `never`）。 不是没保存，是退出时被主动改写了，而且改成了更大的权限。 [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 在退场（effect disposer）里会把所有当前是 `auto` 的会话迁移到完全权限： ```js for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) { if (permissionPresets.current(session) !== AUTO_PRESET) continue permissionPresets.set(session, 'danger-full-access') // 写进会话日志 } ``` `set()` 不是改内存：它往会话日志追加 `permission/preset: danger-full-access` 和 `approval/policy: never`，所以这个迁移是持久的。 问题在于**这个 disposer 在「应用退出」时同样会跑**，而它本意只在「运行中把插件卸载掉」时才该跑——上游的设计笔记写得很明确：关闭应用应当保留选择，只有活体卸载才迁移。插件自己分不清这两件事，于是每次退出都执行了迁移。 上游已在 `4923f3cb`（「fix(auto-review): preserve Auto during application shutdown」）修掉，判据是 `ctx.root.fiber.state` 是否仍是 ACTIVE；该修复进入 `0.2.2-alpha.2` 及以后，`0.2.1-rc.*` 仍是裸循环。 同一个 bug 的第二个后果：存着 `auto` 的会话在集成缺席时无法重新发布，`pinInitialPermission` 抛 `permission: cannot restore preset "auto" without its active integration`，这种会话干脆打不开。 ## 🧩 它做两件事 本插件是常驻的 host 行，只在运行期包裹 `permissionPresets` 服务，**不修改安装目录里的任何包**，升级 DSH 不会被覆盖。 | # | 行为 | 说明 | |:--|:--|:--| | 1 | 关机窗口内的 `set(session, 'danger-full-access')` 被忽略 | root fiber 不是 ACTIVE（PENDING / LOADING / FAILED / DISPOSED / UNLOADING）且会话当前是 `auto` 时不写入，会话日志零事件 | | 2 | `pinInitialPermission` 不再为「auto 缺集成」抛错 | 会话按存储的身份正常打开，不追加降级事件 | 判据来自 cordis 自身的卸载顺序：root 先进入 `UNLOADING`(5)，**之后**才逐个跑子插件的 disposer。因此在 disposer 阶段读到的 root 状态就是「应用正在退出」。运行中把插件卸掉时 root 仍是 ACTIVE，迁移照常发生——这是上游本来就要的行为，插件不干预。 两个包裹都只在服务实例上装一次（`Symbol.for` 标记）。**dispose 时故意不解包**：本行通常先于 `auto-review` 被 dispose，在那里还原原方法等于把关机迁移还回去。 宿主无法识别时不做事：`root.fiber.state` 不是数字，一切调用保持原样。 ## 🚀 安装 ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:SternChiri/dsh-auto-preset-guard" ``` 装完重启 DSH。`package.json` 声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，reconciliation 会自动插入这一行： ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-auto-preset-guard name: dsh-auto-preset-guard ``` 卸载： ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-auto-preset-guard ``` > 关掉或移除本插件后，若安装的 DSH 仍带裸循环，退出时就会重新迁移。要不要用它，取决于你的版本是否已含上游修复。 ### 让本机 Agent 替你装 把下面这段原样丢给本机 DSH： ```text 请帮我安装 dsh-auto-preset-guard（仓库：https://github.com/SternChiri/dsh-auto-preset-guard）。先读该仓库 README 的「安装」，用 dsh plugin 把它装进 desktop profile，重启 DSH 后确认插件行为 active，并告诉我怎么验证「自动审批」在重启后被保留。 ``` ## ✅ 验证 `test/` 里两个脚本直接跑**安装目录里真实的 cordis 运行时**，不需要 DSH 启动： ```sh node test/verify.mjs # 关机保留 / 活体卸载仍迁移 / 缺集成不抛 / 无关错误照抛 node test/proxy-check.mjs # 服务代理语义：提前捕获的引用也能派发到包裹后的方法 ``` 默认从 `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 解析运行时（在 profile 里安装时就是宿主那份）。DSH 装在非常规位置或运行时在归档（asar）内时，用 `DSH_CORDIS` 指向它的入口文件： ```sh DSH_CORDIS=/path/to/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/cordis/lib/index.js node test/verify.mjs ``` `verify.mjs` 覆盖四项：运行期卸载集成仍把 `auto` 迁到完全权限；root 进入 UNLOADING 后迁移零写入且身份仍是 `auto`；缺集成的会话打开不抛错；其它发布错误照常抛出。 `proxy-check.mjs` 验证插件唯一依赖的运行时假设：`auto-review` 在 apply 时捕获的 `const permissionPresets = ctx.permissionPresets`，在包裹之后仍派发到包裹后的方法，而普通预设写入仍到达服务本体。 设 `DSH_AUTO_PRESET_GUARD_DEBUG=1` 可打印每一次被拦下的写入。 ## 🗺️ 已知边界 - 只拦 `auto → danger-full-access` 这一种写入，其它预设变更一律放行。 - 只在本行处于 active 时生效。若安装的 DSH 仍带裸循环而本插件被禁用，退出照样迁移。 - 不碰沙箱值、持久终端、会话数据；无 UI、无设置项。 - 依赖 cordis 的卸载顺序，属于运行时实现细节。上游修复落地后，本插件可原样卸载，无需清理。 ## 📄 License MIT —— 详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 --- # dsh-auto-preset-guard **Keep the Auto permission preset across DSH restarts — quitting no longer rewrites it to Full access.** ## 🌟 What this is Pick **Auto review** (`auto`) in a session, quit DSH, open the session again: it is now **Full access** (`danger-full-access`, approval policy `never`). It is not a lost save. The preset is rewritten on the way out, upward. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review` migrates every live `auto` session to Full access from its effect disposer: ```js for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) { if (permissionPresets.current(session) !== AUTO_PRESET) continue permissionPresets.set(session, 'danger-full-access') } ``` `set()` persists: it appends `permission/preset: danger-full-access` and `approval/policy: never` to the session log. The migration is meant for **removing the integration while the app runs**. It also runs during **application shutdown**, where the selection should survive. Upstream fixed that in `4923f3cb` ("fix(auto-review): preserve Auto during application shutdown") by checking `ctx.root.fiber.state`; the fix ships from `0.2.2-alpha.2`, while `0.2.1-rc.*` still carries the unconditional loop. The same bug has a second edge: a session stored as `auto` cannot be republished without the integration — `pinInitialPermission` throws `permission: cannot restore preset "auto" without its active integration`, and the session fails to open. ## 🧩 What this plugin does One always-on host row that wraps the live `permissionPresets` service. It patches no shipped package, so a DSH upgrade does not remove it. | # | Behaviour | Detail | |:--|:--|:--| | 1 | `set(session, 'danger-full-access')` is dropped inside the shutdown window | When the root fiber is not ACTIVE and the session is currently `auto`, nothing is written — zero session events | | 2 | `pinInitialPermission` stops throwing for "auto without its integration" | The session opens with its stored identity and no downgrade event | The signal comes from cordis itself: the root enters `UNLOADING`(5) **before** any child disposer runs, so a disposer that reads the root state knows the app is shutting down. Removing the plugin while running keeps ACTIVE, so the stock migration still happens — that is upstream's intent and is left alone. Both wrappers install once per service instance (`Symbol.for` marker) and are deliberately **never unwrapped on dispose**: this row usually unloads before `auto-review`, and restoring the original method there would hand the shutdown migration back. Unknown hosts are untouched: if `root.fiber.state` is not a number, every call behaves exactly as before. ## 🚀 Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:SternChiri/dsh-auto-preset-guard" ``` Restart DSH afterwards. `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so reconciliation inserts the row automatically. ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-auto-preset-guard ``` > Disable or remove this plugin while the installed DSH still ships the unconditional disposer, and quitting migrates again. ## ✅ Verify ```sh node test/verify.mjs # shutdown preserves, live removal still migrates, missing integration no longer throws node test/proxy-check.mjs # service proxy semantics ``` Both drive the **real** cordis runtime shipped in the installation. Resolution defaults to `@deepseek-ai/cordis`; point `DSH_CORDIS` at its entry file when the runtime lives inside an asar archive or an unusual location. Set `DSH_AUTO_PRESET_GUARD_DEBUG=1` to log every suppressed write. ## 🗺️ Known limitations - Only the `auto → danger-full-access` write is suppressed; any other preset change goes through untouched. - Effective only while this row is active. Disabled, and the shipped loop migrates as before. - No sandbox, terminal, or session-data changes; no UI, no settings. - Depends on cordis unload ordering, a runtime implementation detail. Once the upstream fix is in your build, uninstall this plugin. ## 📄 License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
