# dsh-ros2-vision

Realtime **vision** — 7 tools + the `vlm/` and `offscreen/` ROS2 packages + `robot-state-vision-analysis` skill.

- `ros2_image_snapshot` / `ros2_vlm_analyze` / `ros2_vision_topics` / `ros2_vision_analyze` / `ros2_vision_describe` / `ros2_vision_doctor` / `ros2_vision_set_key`
- **Upload gate** on `ros2_vision_describe`: the type is sniffed from the file **content** (not the extension), the path must be a **regular file**, and it must be **≤ 20 MiB** — a budget violation is refused from `stat`, without reading a byte. The bytes that pass go to a third-party gateway, so both gates are about what is allowed to leave.
- **Capture destination gate** on `ros2_image_snapshot`: the default output is the absolute
  `$TMPDIR/dsh-ros2/snapshot_<ts>.jpg`; a path outside the capture directory requires approval;
  a symlink / directory / device destination, a non-`.jpg` name, or a missing parent is refused.
  The capture directory must be **ours and private (0700)** — a fixed name under `$TMPDIR` can be
  pre-created by another local user. The same criterion now also guards the **standalone CLI**
  (`scripts/image_snapshot.py`): its default directory is created/tightened to 0700 and a symlink or
  a foreign owner is a refusal (exit code 3), and the JPEG bytes are written 0600 through a temp file +
  `os.replace` so a symlink planted at the destination is replaced, not followed.
- **Publishes the `dshRos2.vision` service** (gemini / openai / mock provider) consumed optionally by `dsh-ros2-core` (`ros2_gui_observe`) and `dsh-ros2-profile` (`ros2_zero_pose_semantics`)
- **npm `files` includes `vlm/` + `offscreen/`** (fixes the monolith publish defect): build them into a colcon workspace (`ln -s <pkg>/vlm <ws>/src/dsh_ros2_vlm`, same for offscreen), then source the workspace.

**Config**: run seam + `vision { provider, apiKey, model, baseUrl }`.

**Dependencies**: `dsh-ros2-common`. Ships `scripts/simplify_visual_meshes.py`.


# dsh-ros2

> ROS2 debugging toolset and robot-state vision analysis for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), shipped as a plugin. 中文版见 [README_CN.md](README_CN.md).

[![CI](https://github.com/StvLi/dsh-ros2/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/StvLi/dsh-ros2/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/StvLi/dsh-ros2)](https://github.com/StvLi/dsh-ros2/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![ROS2](https://img.shields.io/badge/ROS2-Jazzy-orange)]()
![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen)
![Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-83-blue)

> **版本对应关系**：npm 上的 `dsh-ros2@0.1.0` 就是本仓库当前版本（monorepo 布局）。
> GitHub 的 `v0.8.0 ~ v0.15.0` 标签是已废弃的旧单体布局历史，从未发布到 npm。
> 版本号在 2026-08 monorepo 拆分时重新基线。详见 [docs/versioning.md](docs/versioning.md)。


**dsh-ros2** gives a DSH agent full robot development / debugging capabilities on any host with ROS2, organized in four capability tiers:

| Tier | Capability | Safety boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L1** | Read-only diagnostics: package/workspace/dependency checks, node/topic/service/action/param/interface enumeration, one-shot topic sampling, TF tree queries, whole-graph topology JSON, `ros2doctor`, bag summaries, MoveIt discovery, robot-profile load, safety-state read & VLM semantic arbitration | Pure read-only, no approval |
| **L2** | Approval-gated management: `colcon build` (background job), `rosdep install`, message skeleton generation, `param set`, bounded `bag record`, one-click ROS2 install, launch management, rosbag replay, MoveIt motion, zero-pose calibration, robot registration & topology learning, **safety_monitor start / human-gated lock / unlock** | Writes always ask first (fail-closed) |
| **L3** | Visualization: RViz2 / rqt lifecycle management, screenshots, multimodal vision description, xdotool-level window interaction | Local session operations; interaction is confined to an application allowlist and asks first outside it |
| **L4** | Realtime vision: parallel VLM ROS2 node + image-topic acquisition (headless; `vision_bringup` periodically refreshes per-topic bridges), plus **RViz2 offscreen rendering** (OGRE kernel → `/rviz/scene` topic) | Pure software/GPU rendering, no display needed |

All tools run plain `ros2` / `colcon` / `rosdep` CLI commands on the host; L1 never modifies anything, L2 always asks first.

---

## Screenshots

| RViz2 offscreen render (latest `lite_urdf`, real material colors) | Head camera | Wrist-left camera | Wrist-right camera |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![mesh render](docs/images/robot_mesh_full.jpg) | ![head cam](docs/images/camera_head.jpg) | ![wrist left](docs/images/camera_wrist_left.jpg) | ![wrist right](docs/images/camera_wrist_right.jpg) |

> Left: `rviz_offscreen_node` renders with the real rviz stack (OGRE) and publishes to the `/rviz/scene` image topic. Right: three frames grabbed from live camera topics by `ros2_image_snapshot` (1280×720). Full test record: [`docs/test-robot-state-vision.md`](docs/test-robot-state-vision.md).

---

## Features

- **Zero-intrusion diagnostics**: 83 tools cover most ROS2 debugging scenarios — from "is the package installed?" to "what is on this topic right now?", one command, one answer;
- **Whole-graph topology**: `ros2_graph` folds nodes/publishers/subscribers/services/actions into one JSON — see the system structure in seconds;
- **Approval-gated writes**: builds, dependency installs, message scaffolding etc. go through the DSH approval service; fail-closed, denial = failure;
- **Visualization as a service**: "see" headlessly — screenshots / multimodal description / window interaction are fully local, no remote display;
- **Parallel realtime vision**: the VLM runs in a separate ROS2 process (`vlm_node`, service `/vlm/describe`); images come from topics (`sensor_msgs/Image` / `CompressedImage`); `vision_bringup` auto-creates one bridge per image topic, headless-ready;
- **RViz2 offscreen rendering (motion render ~22 Hz on llvmpipe; 30 Hz full rate with GPU)**: the real rviz render kernel (`rviz_common` + OGRE) renders any `.rviz` scene on a virtual display and publishes it as an image topic — no screenshots, no X11 window-stacking dependency. **Performance optimizations**: open3d low-poly meshes (`scripts/simplify_visual_meshes.py`) + direct OGRE pixel read (no PNG round-trip) + double-render elimination → motion rendering 1.9 → ~22 Hz on llvmpipe (11×), and **30 Hz full rate with NVIDIA GPU passthrough** (v0.9.3), memory −2.5×;
- **Real-time safety framework** (`safety_monitor` node + `robot_safety_*` tools, see [Safety framework](#safety-framework)): layered defense — tool-layer safety gate (pre-execution `/safety/state` check) → reactive monitors (motion tracking/stall with hysteresis, joint-feedback loss, watchdog, optional torque) → event-driven VLM semantic arbitration → human arbitration. Latched `NORMAL`/`LOCKED` state machine (lock persists until a human unlocks; non-fatal events never lock); every threshold/topic/lock-action is registered per robot in the profile `safety` section; the geometric pre-check (joint limits / velocity / FK self-collision) is a reserved layer;
- **Bundled skills (9)**: one carrier per recurring journey — `ros2-diagnostics` (which tool when, narrow-down methodology), `ros2-bringup-recovery` (environment → launch → verify), `ros2-liveness-triage` (rates and payload in one or two calls), `ros2-tf-integrity` (edges, lookups, missing broadcaster), `robot-registration` / `robot-retrieval` (body profile and instant reuse), `robot-state-vision-analysis` (status → render → VLM → cross-check), `robot-motion-control` (the one plan → validate → approve → execute → verify path) and `robot-safety-procedure` (latch, LOCKED, boundaries).

---

## Quick start

### Requirements

- A host with ROS2 (**Jazzy** verified; Humble should work), `ros2` on `PATH`;
- Node `^22.19 || >=24` (DSH host requirement);
- L4 vision additionally needs Python 3 `rclpy` and an OpenAI-compatible VLM gateway (e.g. Gemini or a self-hosted gateway).

### Install the plugins (9 npm packages, since the monorepo split)

Install the domain bundles you need — or the **`dsh-ros2` aggregate**, which
mounts core/profile/moveit/safety/vision (81 tools + the 9 skills). Add the
optional `dsh-ros2-state` for the family's full 83 tools. All packages are
published to npm at **0.1.0** (see [docs/versioning.md](docs/versioning.md) for
the GitHub ↔ npm version correspondence).

**Via the DSH plugin CLI** (recommended; resolves through npm):

```bash
# full set (aggregate; pulls core/profile/moveit/safety/vision as deps)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ros2
# or lean installs — e.g. diagnostics only:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ros2-core
# dsh-ros2-common is a plain library, auto-installed as a dependency.
```

**Via npm directly** (same packages; useful for inspecting/installing the
optional add-ons):

```bash
# the aggregate (mounts dsh-ros2-common/core/profile/moveit/safety/vision = 81 tools)
npm install dsh-ros2
# optional add-ons — the sidecar data plane + its control-plane state client.
# `dsh-ros2-state` is NOT part of the aggregate's patch; its own 2 tools
# (state_get / state_snapshot) are what take the family from 81 to 83:
npm install dsh-ros2-state dsh-ros2-sidecar
```

> Package roles: `dsh-ros2` (aggregate) · `dsh-ros2-common` (shared library) ·
> `dsh-ros2-core` (core diagnostics) · `dsh-ros2-profile` (profiles/topology) ·
> `dsh-ros2-moveit` (MoveIt motion) · `dsh-ros2-safety` (safety framework) ·
> `dsh-ros2-vision` (vision pipeline) · `dsh-ros2-state` (state client) ·
> `dsh-ros2-sidecar` (data-plane daemon).

> **Prompt guidance.** `dsh-ros2-core` contributes a system-prompt section that
> points the model at this toolchain for ROS2 work — discover the graph with
> `ros2_*`, load the body with `robot_load`/`robot_topology`, plan and act through
> `moveit_*`/`robot_safety_*` (approval-gated, gated on `/safety/state`) — instead
> of ad-hoc `ros2` CLI calls or private `rclpy` scripts. Any install that includes
> core therefore carries it, the `dsh-ros2` aggregate included.
>
> The section is rebuilt on every assembly from the tools that are registered at
> that moment, so a core-only install is never told to call `moveit_move` or
> `robot_safety_*` it does not ship. It is registered with the plugin's own
> lifetime: disabling or removing the plugin removes it from the prompt, so an
> unloaded dsh-ros2 leaves no residue.

### Minimal configuration (per-bundle, whole-object replacement)

After the split, each bundle carries its **own run-seam config** (same keys
repeated per id) and the vision provider lives only on `dsh-ros2-vision`:

```yaml
# fragment of a DSH profile patch (id-targeted config overrides)
- id: dsh-ros2-core                 # also: -profile / -moveit / -safety
  config:
    rosSetup: source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash &&   # prepare the ROS2 environment
    workspaceRoot: /home/you/ros2_ws                 # default cwd for colcon/rosdep
- id: dsh-ros2-vision
  config:
    rosSetup: source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash &&
    vision:
      provider: gemini                               # mock | gemini | openai
      apiKey: ${VLM_API_KEY}                         # ${ENV} 引用从环境变量解析，勿明文写 key
- id: dsh-ros2-safety
  config:
    safetyStrict: warn                               # 'warn' (default) | 'reject' (fail-closed); LOCKED always rejects
```

### Three-minute taste

```bash
ros2_topology --tf                  # WHOLE system (nodes/topics/services/actions/TF) in one call
ros2_graph                          # whole system topology in one shot
ros2_topic_list                     # all topics and types
ros2_topic_echo /joint_states       # sample one frame of joint states
ros2_tf_list                        # TF tree edges
ros2_doctor                         # system health report
```

---

## Tool reference

> Tools live in domain packages: L1/L2/L3 → `dsh-ros2-core`; `motion_validate`/`moveit_*` → `dsh-ros2-moveit`; `robot_*`/`ros2_zero_pose_semantics` → `dsh-ros2-profile`; `robot_safety_*` → `dsh-ros2-safety`; vision tools → `dsh-ros2-vision`.

### L1 read-only diagnostics

| Tool | Command behind it | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ros2_pkg_list` | `ros2 pkg list` | Installed packages (optional substring filter) |
| `ros2_pkg_prefix` / `ros2_pkg_executables` | `ros2 pkg prefix <pkg>` / `ros2 pkg executables [pkg]` | Install prefix of a package / executables (structured) |
| `ros2_colcon_list` | `colcon list` | Packages in a colcon workspace |
| `ros2_rosdep_check` | `rosdep check --from-paths src --ignore-src` | Dependency health (missing deps = finding, not error) |
| `ros2_node_list` | `ros2 node list` | Running nodes |
| `ros2_node_info` | `ros2 node info <node> [-v]` | Subscribers / publishers / services / actions of one node |
| `ros2_topic_list` | `ros2 topic list -t` | Topics with types |
| `ros2_topic_find` | `ros2 topic find <type>` | Topics carrying a message type |
| `ros2_topic_info` | `ros2 topic info <topic> [-v]` | Topic metadata / QoS |
| `ros2_topic_echo` | `ros2 topic echo <topic> --once` | One message sample (JSON when possible); `--qos-reliability` / `--qos-durability` overrides reach TRANSIENT_LOCAL latched topics |
| `ros2_topic_hz` | `ros2 topic hz <topic> [--window N]` | Measure publish frequency (average/min/max/std dev over the window); natural termination = measurement timeout |
| `ros2_env_check` | resolved-setup probe | Self-check the environment: which setup is sourced, path existence, visible packages/nodes |
| `ros2_workspace` | `source <ws>/install/setup.bash &&` | Switch/show the workspace in-session (use/show/reset) — no config edit, no restart. `use` **requires approval**: sourcing the file *executes* it, and the override then applies to every later command |
| `ros2_topic_bw` / `ros2_topic_delay` | `ros2 topic bw|delay <topic>` | Measure topic bandwidth / end-to-end delay; timeout-terminated |
| `ros2_service_list` | `ros2 service list -t` | Services with types |
| `ros2_service_type` / `ros2_service_find` | `ros2 service type|find ...` | Service type / find services by type |
| `ros2_action_list` | `ros2 action list -t` | Actions with types |
| `ros2_action_info` | `ros2 action info <action>` | Action type & status |
| `ros2_action_type` | `ros2 action type <action>` | Action type |
| `ros2_param_list` | `ros2 param list <node>` | Parameters of a node |
| `ros2_param_get` | `ros2 param get <node> <param>` | Read one parameter value |
| `ros2_param_dump` | `ros2 param dump <node>` | Dump all parameters of a node |
| `ros2_interface_show` | `ros2 interface show <type>` | Full field definition of a message/service/action |
| `ros2_interface_list` / `ros2_interface_prototype` / `ros2_interface_package` | `ros2 interface list|prototype|package ...` | All interface types / default-value prototype / types in a package |
| `ros2_graph` | `ros2 node list` + per-node `node info` | Folded JSON topology graph |
| `ros2_topology` | one `rclpy` process (no per-verb CLI spawns) | **Whole-system snapshot in one call**: nodes with their pub/sub/services, topics with types and pub/sub counts, services, actions, plus optional TF frames and parameters. Prefer it over several narrower calls |
| `ros2_tf_list` | same `rclpy` snapshot | TF edges from `/tf` **and** the latched `/tf_static` (both dynamic and static frames) |
| `ros2_tf_echo` | same `rclpy` snapshot | Transform between two frames, including the inverse edge |
| `ros2_doctor` | `ros2 doctor` | System health report |
| `ros2_bag_info` | `ros2 bag info <path>` | Bag summary |
| `moveit_discover` | scans MoveIt packages + parses SRDF + probes move_group | Discover MoveIt2 config packages (any package shipping an SRDF), their planning groups and named poses, and whether `/move_action` / `/execute_trajectory` / `/compute_cartesian_path` are online. Pass `srdf` to parse a specific file directly — generic, not bound to a specific package |
| `robot_safety_state` | `ros2 topic echo /safety/state --once` | Read the latched safety state (NORMAL / LOCKED + severity + trigger cause + detail); reports `monitor_running: false` when the monitor is offline |
| `robot_safety_arbitrate` | `ros2 run dsh_ros2_safety safety_vlm_arbitrate ...` | Event-driven VLM semantic arbitration (plan change / post-anomaly): fixed-format prompt + fresh offscreen frame via `/vlm/describe`; any non-safe verdict flags human arbitration |
| `motion_validate` | `motion_validator.py --trajectory <file> --config <json>` | Deterministic pre-execution validation (read-only): joint limits, NaN/Inf, names & group coverage, timestamps/duration, freshness, optional workspace box, fingerprint + TTL — collision/singularity stay with MoveIt planning |

### L2 management (approval-gated)

Every L2 tool performs a **write operation** and asks the user first via the DSH approval service (fail-closed when unavailable or denied). The read-only helpers `ros2_jobs_list` / `ros2_job_status` need no approval.

| Tool | Command behind it | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ros2_colcon_build` | `colcon build [--packages-select ...] [--symlink-install]` | Runs as a **background job** (`ctx.jobs`); returns `jobId`, track with `ros2_job_status` |
| `ros2_rosdep_install` | `rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -y` | `dryRun` previews with `--simulate` |
| `ros2_interface_create` | writes `<root>/<pkg>/<msg\|srv\|action>/<Name>.*` | Skeleton generator; **never overwrites** existing files |
| `ros2_param_set` | `ros2 param set <node> <param> <value>` | JSON numbers/booleans are typed, other values treated as strings |
| `ros2_bag_record` | `ros2 bag record <topics...> --output <dir>` | Bounded recording: stops automatically after `duration` seconds |
| `ros2_jobs_list` | `ctx.jobs.list` | Background jobs of this agent (read-only) |
| `ros2_job_status` | `ctx.jobs.get` | Status of one job by id (read-only) |
| `ros2_install` | FishROS one-click installer (interactive PTY session) | When ROS2 is missing: `check` probes (installed / installed-not-sourced / absent); `start` (approval) launches the installer; `send` / `status` / `stop` drive and observe the interactive menus |
| `ros2_bag_play` | `ros2 bag play <path> [--topics ...] [--rate X] [--loop] [--start-offset S]` | Replay a rosbag into its topics (approval-gated; publishes to the graph); foreground for `timeoutMs` |
| `ros2_topic_pub` | `ros2 topic pub <topic> <type> "<yaml>" [-r Hz] [-n N|--once|-t sec]` | Publish messages (approval-gated; mutates the graph). Bounded publish + QoS overrides (--qos-reliability / --qos-durability) |
| `ros2_run` | `ros2 run <pkg> <executable> [args]` | Run any installed ROS2 executable (approval-gated): foreground (bounded) or background job |
| `ros2_process_cleanup` | `pgrep -f '[p]attern'` + `kill` | Kill leftover ROS2 processes matching a pattern (self-safe); approval-gated |
| `ros2_service_call` | `ros2 service call <svc> <type> "<yaml>"` | Call a service (approval-gated); response parsed from the repr |
| `ros2_action_send_goal` | `ros2 action send_goal <action> <type> "<yaml>" [--feedback]` | Send an action goal (approval-gated); returns goal id + status |
| `ros2_daemon` | `ros2 daemon status|stop|start` | Daemon status (L1) / stop-start (L2 approval) — re-discover a stale graph |
| `ros2_param_delete` | `ros2 param delete <node> <param>` | Delete a node parameter (approval-gated) |
| `ros2_lifecycle` | `ros2 lifecycle get|list|set <node> [state]` | Lifecycle state get/list (L1) or set (L2 approval) |
| `ros2_component` | `ros2 component list` / `load <container> <pkg> <type>` | Component containers list (L1) / load (L2 approval) |
| `ros2_launch` | `ros2 launch <pkg> <launch_file> [args]` | Launch a launch file as a **background job** (approval-gated; returns jobId, stop via DSH job controls) |
| `ros2_zero_pose_semantics` | publish-zero → offscreen render → VLM → confirm | Calibrate zero-pose semantics interactively (generic): `analyze` renders the all-zero pose and asks the VLM its posture across three aspects (arm: lateral_raise/hanging, elbow: forward/upward, palm/camera-mount: up/forward/down); `confirm` records the user-approved combo (or a `customText` free-text description) to `~/.dsh-ros2/zero-pose.yaml` for skills |
| `robot_register` | collects URDF/TF/cameras/MoveIt/zero-pose → writes `~/.dsh-ros2/robots/<name>.yaml` | Register a robot body profile on first contact (approval-gated) for instant later reuse |
| `robot_load` | reads `~/.dsh-ros2/robots/<name>.yaml` | Load a registered robot profile as structured JSON (fast path — no discovery); empty name lists all profiles |
| `robot_topology` | aggregate snapshot + progressive node learning (strict schema) | Robot comms topology trade-off: `snapshot` (approval) records node/topic/service lists (light, not verbose); `learn` (approval) records ONE important node's role/description + pub/sub/srv/act; `show` (read-only) reads them back |
| `moveit_move` | unified: `/move_action` + `/execute_trajectory` | **One tool, five essential modes** (approval-gated): `joint_abs`, `joint_rel`, `pose_abs`, `pose_rel` (frame ee/world), `trajectory`. Generic: standard moveit_msgs + SRDF only. **Single motion path: plan → deterministic validation (motion_validator, `robot` profile for full limits) → human approval (validation summary shown) → execute → verify**. Gates on `/safety/state` (LOCKED always rejected; monitor-down per `safetyStrict`) |
| `robot_safety_start` | `ros2 run dsh_ros2_safety safety_monitor --profile <yaml>` | Start the generic safety monitor as a **background job** (approval-gated); all robot-specific values come from the profile `safety` section |
| `robot_safety_lock` / `robot_safety_unlock` | `ros2 service call /safety/set_lock|unlock ...` | **Human-gated** explicit lock / unlock (L2 approval before the call); lock is latched until a human unlocks (recovery: unlock → re-home → resume) |
| `moveit_status` | probes move_group interfaces + samples `/joint_states` | Runtime status: online probe + current joint state + SRDF planning frame (read-only) |

### L3 visualization

GUI lifecycle + screenshots + multimodal vision ("see first, then move") + xdotool-level interaction ("see and move"). Screenshots use Pillow `ImageGrab` on X11 (no extra CLI install); vision providers are pluggable; interaction requires `xdotool` (`sudo apt install xdotool`).

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ros2_gui_start` | Launch RViz2 (with `-d config`) / rqt_graph / rqt on the host display; sessions are tracked |
| `ros2_gui_list` | Tracked sessions + X11 windows (`wmctrl -lG`) |
| `ros2_gui_close` | Close a session (SIGTERM) |
| `ros2_screenshot` | Capture the screen or one window to a PNG |
| `ros2_vision_describe` | Describe an image with the configured multimodal model (Gemini / OpenAI / mock). The path must be a real PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP — the **content** is sniffed before anything is uploaded — and **at most 20 MiB**; a larger or non-regular file is refused without being read |
| `ros2_gui_observe` | Ensure a GUI is running → screenshot → return the multimodal description (the "see it" workflow) |
| `ros2_gui_interact` | unified xdotool interaction: `action=click` (click/scroll, `button` 4/5 = scroll), `action=drag` (press-drag-release: RViz2 orbit/pan/zoom), `action=key` (combos like `ctrl+shift+r` or typed text). **Confined to an application allowlist** (default `rviz2` / `rqt` / `rqt_graph`, configurable via `guiAllowedApplications`); any other target — including omitting `windowTitle`, which acts on whatever is focused — **requires approval** |

Interaction recipes (model-facing): orbit the RViz2 view with `ros2_gui_interact {action: "drag", windowTitle: "rviz2", button: 1, toX: <dx>, toY: <dy>}`, zoom with `action: "drag", button: 3`, reload a display config with `ros2_gui_interact {action: "key", keys: "ctrl+shift+r"}`. When `wmctrl` cannot enumerate windows (e.g. no window manager on the display), window-relative interaction reports "window not found" — fall back to absolute screen coordinates, which now **asks for approval** because it targets whatever window is focused.

**Why the allowlist**: `action=key` types arbitrary text into the targeted window, so an unrestricted target is a host-level input-injection path (typing into a terminal runs commands). The allowlist is a convenience control — any process can retitle its own window, so a title match is not proof of identity; the **approval gate is the boundary**, and it fails closed (no approval service = denial). See [`docs/safety.md`](docs/safety.md).

### L4 realtime vision (parallel VLM over ROS2, headless image topics)

Perception matches the robot-control stack: the VLM runs in a **separate ROS2 process** (`vlm_node`, service `/vlm/describe` + cached topic `/vlm/description`), and images come from **`sensor_msgs/Image` topics, never X11 screenshots** — headless-ready. Acquisition (`ros2_image_snapshot`) needs **no custom package** (plain rclpy); only `ros2_vlm_analyze`/`ros2_vision_analyze` require the `dsh_ros2_vlm` ROS2 package (`vlm/`) — build/run see [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) §4. When the pipeline is down, `ros2_vlm_analyze`/`ros2_vision_analyze` return an explicit `VLM_UNAVAILABLE` + degradation hint, and the snapshot JPEG can be read directly by the Agent's own multimodal model.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ros2_image_snapshot` | Grab one frame from a topic (raw/compressed) and save as JPEG — plain rclpy script, **no custom ROS2 package needed**; `--v4l` ffmpeg fallback for silent topics; the JPEG is ready for the Agent's own multimodal model |
| `ros2_vlm_analyze` | Analyze an image file or the bridge's latest frame (`useBridge`) via the parallel VLM |
| `ros2_vision_topics` | List live image topics with their auto bridge service names |
| `ros2_vision_doctor` | One-shot pipeline self-check: vlm workspace built / vlm_node+vision_bringup running / gateway reachable / visible image topics / apiKey resolution status (config/env/secrets/missing) + build-launch guidance |
| `ros2_vision_set_key` | Store the user-provided VLM API Key into `~/.dsh-ros2/secrets.json` (0600, outside the repo — never committed, never uploaded, never echoed); use it when a tool returns `VLM_API_KEY_REQUIRED` |
| `ros2_vision_analyze` | Analyze any topic's latest frame via its auto bridge (`ros2_vision_analyze {topic, prompt}`) |

```bash
# build + launch the vision pipeline (auto bridge per image topic)
# Build the workspace OUTSIDE /tmp: a reboot wipes /tmp, and a `rosSetup` that
# sources a deleted workspace is the misconfiguration documented in
# docs/feedback-env-recovery.md. Use any persistent path (`~/vlm_ws` here).
mkdir -p ~/vlm_ws/src && ln -s <repo>/vlm ~/vlm_ws/src/dsh_ros2_vlm
cd ~/vlm_ws && colcon build --symlink-install && source install/setup.bash
VLM_API_KEY=... ros2 run dsh_ros2_vlm vlm_node &       # parallel VLM process
ros2 run dsh_ros2_vlm vision_bringup &                 # discover topics, one bridge each
```

### RViz2 offscreen rendering (`dsh_ros2_rviz_offscreen`)

The real rviz rendering stack (`rviz_common` + OGRE + `rviz_default_plugins`) loads a `.rviz` scene offscreen under Xvfb and publishes it to the `/rviz/scene` image topic — read from the render kernel, not X screenshots, no window-stacking dependency.

```bash
# build (needs a colcon workspace like vlm_ws — keep it out of /tmp)
ln -s <repo>/offscreen ~/vlm_ws/src/dsh_ros2_rviz_offscreen
cd ~/vlm_ws && colcon build --symlink-install && source install/setup.bash
# run (config_path points at a .rviz scene file)
xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x800x24" ros2 run dsh_ros2_rviz_offscreen rviz_offscreen_node \
  --ros-args -p config_path:=/tmp/robot_scene.rviz -p topic:=/rviz/scene \
  -p width:=800 -p height:=600 -p rate:=5.0
```

**Robot body mesh rendering essentials** (pitfalls collected; details in [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) §4.4):

1. **Jazzy RobotModel properties**: use `Description Source: Topic` + `Description Topic: <topic>` (the legacy `Robot Description:` is ignored → `Links` empty);
2. **mesh paths**: use absolute paths or a `file://` prefix in the URDF (bare paths fail in `resource_retriever`); the description publisher must stay alive (transient-local, late subscribers miss it otherwise);
3. **URDF must bind to TF by name**: URDF link names must exactly match the live TF frame names (publishing the robot's actual `/robot_description` works). **Mismatch → every link transform lookup fails → all meshes pile at the fixed-frame origin**;
4. **View distance**: Orbit `Distance` ≈ 1.5–2.0 m for an RViz-like close full-body view (> 5 m shrinks the robot to a tiny center blob);
5. **Health signal**: ~3 s after startup the node logs `FM: ... frames=N` and `transformHasProblems(...)=0` — meshes correctly bound to TF.

**Design intent.** Robot motion through MoveIt is, at its core, only five
operations: set joints absolutely, nudge joints relatively, place the

| `moveit_status` (L1) | Runtime probe: interfaces online + current `/joint_states` sample + SRDF planning frame |

# dsh-plugin-wechat-mp

[中文说明](README.zh.md) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin · MIT

WeChat official account (公众号) skills for DeepSeek Harness. Two skills, no MCP server, no third-party Python, no cloud round-trip:

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `wechat-mp-content` | Read an `mp.weixin.qq.com` article **and its 留言/comments**, using the live session the WeChat PC client keeps in its own unlocked `Share Data` file. Also searches 公众号 articles by keyword. |
| `wechat-mp-corpus` | Archive a whole 公众号 locally: watch `Share Data` while you click through the account's history, then auto-download each new article's text, original HTML, and images into an indexed corpus. |

Both skills exist because of one hard fact: **article bodies are easy, comments are not.** A logged-out browser is served an empty comment module and "open this article in WeChat"; the comment API (`mp/appmsg_comment`) needs `uin` / `key` / `pass_ticket`, which only exist inside the WeChat client's browser profile — in a plain, unlocked file. Reading that file first is the whole trick. Everything else in the skills (the failed approaches, the error codes, the pagination dead end) is there so an agent does not re-discover it the slow way.

## Requirements

- **Windows** with the WeChat PC client — the session source is `%APPDATA%\Tencent\xwechat\radium\web\profiles\multitab_<hash>\Share Data` (older installs: `%APPDATA%\Tencent\WeChat`).
- **Python 3.9+** on `PATH`. The helpers use the standard library only — `pip install` is not needed.
- **DeepSeek Harness** with the skill registry mounted (any profile built on `dsh-base`, e.g. `web` or `desktop`).
- Node.js 20+ for the plugin itself (the host provides it).

## Install

The plugin is a DSH bundle: installing it adds one row to the profile's Cordis tree, which registers a read-only skill provider.

```sh
# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:/path/to/dsh-plugin-wechat-mp

# or from the registry, once published
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-wechat-mp
```

`dsh plugin` appends the bundle to `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically. Alternatively, use the **Plugins** page in the Web UI (sidebar → Plugins) and install from a path or package name.

After the profile loads, the two skills appear in the agent's skill catalog. With HMR enabled in the profile — the default for `dsh-base` profiles — the catalog updates **without restarting**: the new skills are visible in the very next turn. Otherwise restart the app.

Verify:

```sh
node --test                                   # 10 checks: provider contract, catalog, bodies, portability
python -m unittest discover -s test -p "test_*.py"   # 4 checks: URL-query fallback for biz/mid/idx/sn
```

## Use

Just ask. The skills are model-invocable and user-invocable, so either of these works:

- "读一下这篇文章和它的留言：https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/…"
- "把这个公众号的文章都存档到 D:\wx_corpus\某号"
- `/wechat-mp-content` (explicit invocation, if your UI exposes skill commands)

The article and comment helpers are also directly runnable — the skills tell the agent to substitute the base directory the runtime reports:

```sh
python "<skill>/scripts/wx_mp.py" probe
python "<skill>/scripts/wx_mp.py" article  <url|sn> --out OUT
python "<skill>/scripts/wx_mp.py" comments <url|sn> --out OUT
python "<skill>/scripts/wx_mp.py" search   "关键词" -n 10
```

## How it works

```
dsh-plugin-wechat-mp/
├─ package.json            # "dsh.bundle.patch" → cordis.patch.yml
├─ cordis.patch.yml        # inserts row: id skill-wechat-mp
├─ lib/index.js            # ~200 lines, zero dependencies
└─ assets/skills/
   ├─ wechat-mp-content/   # SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/wx_mp.py
   └─ wechat-mp-corpus/    # SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/
```

`lib/index.js` exports the Cordis plugin triple `name` / `inject` / `apply`. `apply` registers one provider on `ctx.skills`; the provider enumerates `assets/skills/*/SKILL.md`, parses the frontmatter, and returns the candidates. Bodies are read from disk on demand (`get`), so a skill costs nothing until it is loaded, and a missing or broken asset tree yields an empty catalog instead of taking down the profile.

Each skill's `resourceBase` is its own directory, which is what makes the instructions portable: the runtime hands the model "Base directory for this skill: …", and the skills say `scripts/wx_mp.py` / `references/…` relative to it. No absolute path is hardcoded anywhere — a regression test enforces that.

## Porting a Codex skill bundle

The layout is deliberately close to a Codex plugin (`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` + `skills/`), so the port is mechanical:

| Codex | DeepSeek Harness |
|---|---|
| `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` (name, interface, `skills: "./skills/"`) | `package.json` with `dsh.bundle.patch` + `keywords` |
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` + `references/` + `scripts/` | identical under `assets/skills/<name>/` |
| `agents/openai.yaml` (per-skill UI hints) | dropped; `metadata.short-description` kept |
| Codex loads the folder | a ~40-line provider registers the same tree on `ctx.skills` |
| absolute script paths from the install location | relative paths + `resourceBase` |

Only the path convention and the registration glue change; the instructions and helper scripts ship unchanged.

## Limitations, by design

- **Windows only.** The session and the archive watcher both depend on the WeChat PC client's `Share Data`. There is no macOS/Linux equivalent in this plugin.
- **You must open the article in WeChat.** Session parameters live for tens of minutes; after `ret=-3 no session`, reopen the article and rerun.
- **Only 精选 comments are public.** `elected_comment` is what the API returns; `elected_comment_total_cnt` can be smaller than `total_count` and the rest has no public endpoint. Pagination does not work (`offset` is ignored, `continue_flag=false` means end).
- **Image-only posts** need OCR; the skill documents the Windows `zh-Hans-CN` path and warns that OCR text is not reliable evidence.
- **No listing API.** Archiving requires the user to click through the account's history in WeChat — that is the reliable path, not a workaround.
- **Read-only.** Nothing writes to the WeChat data directory, injects into the client, or copies the locked `Network\Cookies` store.

## Privacy

The plugin reads local WeChat files and fetches public `mp.weixin.qq.com` pages. It contains no telemetry, no analytics, and no remote endpoint of its own. Archived corpora are written wherever you point `--out`. Only collect articles you are entitled to read, and do not redistribute them.

## License

MIT © 2026 TaoLiu

DSH Capsule · Capability Guard

简体中文 · English

批准一次，换一段有期限的免打扰——到期自动收回，随时能提前收回，全程有记录。

DSH Capsule 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Capability Guard：
把 DSH 的「每次都要问」变成「有界、可复用、可撤销、可审计」的短期授权。

**30 秒看懂**：装完即用、不用先写配置。Agent 反复要求同一类提权时，你批准一次，接下来一段时间它不再问你； 提示条一直告诉你「放开了什么、还剩多久、到期会怎样」，时间一到自动收回；想提前收回点一下就行。 > [!IMPORTANT] > **项目定位已经变化。** 当前仓库是纯 TypeScript 的 Capability Guard，不再包含旧版 Python / Docker / Unix Domain Socket 隔离 Runtime。本文只描述当前代码真实存在的能力。2026-10-30 按项目决策移除凭证代理、命令凭证绑定及 Managed SDK/示例，当前聚焦通用短期授权。 > [!WARNING] > **Developer Preview。** 核心链路（Lease、沙箱升级有界授权、Audit、Console）已在仓库实现，有**真 cordis 集成测试**守护 hook 接线与完整权限生命周期，并已在本机 desktop profile 中实跑。 > > DSH 本身仍在快速迭代：本仓库与本机安装版源码的核对结论记录在 `docs/集成基线-真实DSH行为.md`，**升级 DSH 后请重跑该文档第 10 节的检查清单**。 --- ## 为什么需要它？ DSH 原生的权限体系有两层，中间是空的： | DSH 原生 | 粒度 | 代价 | |---|---|---| | `permission-presets`（会话级沙箱 + 审批组合） | 一次生效、覆盖面广 | 粗：一放开就是整个会话 | | `allowed-once`（单次审批） | 精确到这一次调用 | 细但每次都要问 | 缺的那一层是：**「这个 Session 内、这个工具、这类操作，在一段时间内已经批过了」**——既有界、又能复用、还能撤销与审计。 它能帮到的具体场景（也是它唯一值得装的理由）： - 让 Agent 连续跑十几分钟的重构 / 测试循环，而你不想每 30 秒点一次「允许一次」； - 需要临时写工作区外的东西（跑脚本、生成产物），但又不想把整个会话永久放开； - 事后要回答「刚才那半小时，究竟是谁把权限放宽到哪一档、什么时候收回的」。 它能帮不到的（请务必看清）： - **不是安全沙箱**：它不放宽、也不收紧 DSH 本身的进程隔离能力；需要强隔离请用 DSH 原生 Sandbox； - **不能阻止其他插件**：`approval/request` 是开放瀑布，任何插件都能抢先认领或直接改会话权限； - **不做凭证代理**（2026-10-30 已按项目决策移除），凭证交给 DSH 原生。 DSH Capsule 补的就是中间那一层： | 问题 | DSH Capsule 的处理方式 | |---|---| | 同一个安全操作反复弹审批 | `allowed-once` 后签发短期 Lease，在相同 Scope + Session 内复用 | | 授权范围太宽 | Lease 绑定 `Session × Tool × Scope × TTL` | | 授权无法自动收回 | TTL 到期回收；沙箱模式提升还会**回滚到批准前的档位** | | 发生了什么难以追踪 | 授权决策记录（谁批的 / 复用几次 / 怎么结束）+ 只读治理台 | | 安全失败被静默放行 | 关键路径统一 **Fail Closed** | 一句话理解： > **把一次明确批准变成有 Session、Scope 与 TTL 边界的短期授权。** --- ## 通用短期授权 ### Universal Mode — 已有插件零改造获得短期授权 Guard 工作在 DSH 原生工具管线的**四个** hook 上（`tools/pre-execute` / `tools/execute` / `approval/request` / `tools/result`），原始语义保持不变： - 原始 `deny`：始终保持 `deny`，Lease **不能覆盖拒绝**； - 原始 `allow`：直接透传，Guard 不制造新的 Approval； - 原始 `ask`：先查找匹配 Lease；命中则临时 `allow`，否则继续 `ask`； - 用户返回 `allowed-once` 后，Guard 才签发带 Scope 与 TTL 的 Lease； - `rejected` / `cancelled` / `unavailable` 均不签发。 > **沙箱升级（sandbox escalation）是当前最有价值的一条链路。** 它经过了与本机安装版 DSH 源码的逐行核对（结论见 `docs/集成基线-真实DSH行为.md`）： > > DSH 的 `tools/pre-execute` **落底决策就是 `allow`**，标准 profile 下没有任何随产品交付的监听器会返回 `ask`。真实审批来自 pwsh/bash/fs **工具体内部**的 `approveEscalation → ctx.approval.request(...)`（例如文件写入越出工作区时，模型带 `sandbox_permissions` + `justification` 重试）。 > > 因此 Guard 的接入点是：在 `tools/execute`（工具体之前、参数仍可用）识别这次升级并按 **`(toolName, 目标模式)`** 生成语义 Scope；用户批准一次后签发 `sandbox-mode` Lease，并**提升该会话的沙箱模式**——后续同类升级不会被沙箱拒绝，也就**不再需要审批**。 > > 到期或撤销时，模式会**回滚到批准前的档位**；若用户在此期间手动改过模式，Guard 跳过回滚并记录审计，**绝不覆盖用户的选择**。 这意味着 Universal Mode 的价值是**减少重复审批，同时保持 DSH 原有权限语义不变**。

## 整体架构 Guard 接在 DSH 原生工具与审批管线上，保持原有审批与沙箱职责。 - UniversalGate：四个 hook，关联 callId、观察审批、签发与复用 Lease。 - ScopeResolver / PolicyResolver：确定性范围解析与 TTL 配置。 - LeaseManager / MemoryLeaseStore：Session 绑定、有效期与撤销。 - SandboxGrantManager：会话沙箱模式提升、失效回滚与用户改动冲突检测。 - AuditService / GovernanceConsole：脱敏审计、授权剩余时间与运行期策略。 ### 与 DSH 原生机制的边界 DSH Capsule **不是第二套 Harness**。它有意复用 DSH 已有机制： - Approval 仍由 DSH 原生 `approval/request` Answerer 决定（Guard 只观察结果，**从不合成**）； - Tool 最终是否允许执行仍受 DSH 其他 Gate / Guard 约束； - 凭证管理仍由 DSH 原生服务或相关工具负责，Guard 不解析或注入凭证； - 进程 / 文件 / 网络隔离仍由 DSH Sandbox 或外部安全机制负责； - 沙箱档位本身仍由 DSH 的会话状态承载，Guard 只是**给它的变更加上时间边界与回滚**。 Guard 只新增一件事：**把一次明确的授权变成受 Scope、Session 与 TTL 约束的短期 Capability。** --- ## Capability Lease 一份 Lease 的核心身份不是“这个插件被允许了”，而是： ```text Session × Tool × Scope × TTL ``` 默认 Scope 按工具名与 canonical JSON 参数生成 SHA-256；沙箱升级按工具名与目标模式生成 Scope。 ### Lease 生命周期 ```text ASK └─ allowed-once └─ ISSUE ────────┐ │ ACTIVE ├─ match → REUSE ├─ TTL → EXPIRED └─ revoke→ REVOKED ``` - TTL 在 `find` / `validate` 时通过当前时间实时判断，正确性不依赖后台定时器； - Lease 始终绑定 Session；缺少可信 `agent.id` 时不会创建匿名 / 全局 Lease； - `revoke(leaseId)` 可撤销单条 Lease； - `revokeSession(sessionId)` 可一次撤销整个 Session 的 Lease； - 当前默认存储是 `MemoryLeaseStore`，重启后不会保留。 --- ## Scope：决定“授权可以复用到哪里” ### `exact-arguments` — 默认 默认 Scope： ```text SHA-256(toolName + canonical JSON(arguments)) ``` 只有 Tool 与参数完全一致时才能复用，是 Universal Mode 最保守的零配置策略。 ### `fields` — 显式放宽 只把指定字段纳入 Scope。例如只按 `repo` 与 `branch` 授权，其他参数变化不会重新 Ask。 ### `tool` — 最宽 同一 Session 内只按 Tool Name 复用。它必须显式配置，不能成为默认行为。 ### `sandbox-escalation` — 沙箱升级语义 Scope 只对带 `sandbox_permissions` + `justification` 的调用生效，Scope Key 为： ```text SHA-256(toolName + 目标沙箱模式) ``` **刻意不把 `justification` 或参数原文纳入 Scope**：前者是模型每次现写的自由文本，纳入就等于把安全边界建立在模型输出上，且措辞一变授权立即失效；后者在升级场景里复用率几乎为零。按 `(工具, 目标模式)` 取键，语义恰好是「本会话内该工具可以升到这一档」。 启用方式（默认**不启用**，不配置就完全不改变 DSH 行为）： ```jsonc { "rules": [ { "match": "pwsh", "scope": { "mode": "sandbox-escalation" }, "ttlSeconds": 300 } ] } ``` 授权真正生效依赖宿主服务（`ctx.sessionProjections` + `session.append("sandbox/mode", …)`）；服务缺失时该链路自动降级为"不提升"，即回到 DSH 原生逐次审批，**不会越权**。 ## 界面：一眼、详情、配置 > 顶部那张图是**结构示意**，不是截图；下面描述的是真实槽位与真实行为。 治理界面按「先会话、后全局」组织；前两个入口都挂在**会话作用域**上，组件直接拿到宿主传入的 `sessionId`， 因此显示的一定是当前会话： 1. **【一眼】对话内常驻提示条**：输入框上方（`conversation.input.dock`），打开会话就能看到 「放开了什么 / 还剩多久 / 到期会怎样 / 提前收回」，**不需要点开任何东西**； 2. **【详情】会话内「能力授权」标签页**：排在 对话 / 轨迹 之后的第三个 tab（`conversation.view`，order 20）， 整页展示本会话的每条授权、权限级别状态、到期后果、技术详情与本会话最近记录； 3. **【配置】设置 →「能力授权」页**（`settings.section`，order 25）：默认范围挡位、TTL 上下限三项运行期配置， **待回滚** | **授权已失效，但档位还没收回**——倒计时归零并不等于恢复完成，页面会明确显示并提供「立即回滚档位」 | | 已恢复 | 授权已失效，档位已回滚 | | 无法确认 | 读不到宿主档位（能力缺失），页面不会假装已恢复 | | 不涉及沙箱档位 | 本会话只有普通工具授权 | 原始 `Lease ID`、`sessionId`、Scope 哈希与完整 Scope 串只出现在「技术详情」展开区；会话名来自 DSH 的会话标题（`ctx.sessionTitle`），读不到时降级为工作目录名或短 ID。 ### 授权决策记录（而不是"事件流"） 会话内 tab 展示的是**一条授权一份记录**：批准了什么 → 被复用了多少次 → 权限级别抬高/收回没有 → 最后怎么结束的。 `PASSTHROUGH_ALLOW` / `TOOL_SUCCESS` 这类属于遥测，默认折叠在「原始事件（排障用）」里——把几百条遥测摆在用户面前， 等于没有审计。 每条记录可以「复制 JSON / 复制 Markdown」，机器可读版本由 `GET /api/decisions` 提供（同一份数据）。 会话顶部还有一行**价值指标**： ``` 本次会话：少点了 12 次批准 · 最长一次放开了 4 分 51 秒 · 待收回 1 项 ``` `少点了 N 次批准` = 该会话里授权被复用的次数（每一次复用，都是你不用再点一次「允许一次」）。 ### 免打扰窗口（唯一由页面发起的放宽） 在会话 tab 里选「工具 + 目标档位 + 时长」，点一下就把「允许一次」提前批量给自己： ```text [ pwsh ▾ ] [ 升到「完全访问」▾ ] [ 30 分钟 ▾ ] [ 开启窗口 ] ``` - 点击即同意（等价一次 `allowed-once`），但**有界**：TTL 必须是正整数且不得超过 `maxTtlSeconds`，不静默裁剪； - 只对配置为 `sandbox-escalation` 的工具生效（`allowTool` 校验），不能拿它当任意工具的放宽通道； - 开窗失败（拿不到会话对象 / 提升失败）会撤销刚签发的授权，不留"授权了却没生效"的半成品； - 到期自动收回，随时可「提前收回」；审计记 `WINDOW_OPENED`，决策记录里能看到是谁在什么时候开的多长窗口。 > **安全提示**：治理接口是本机 loopback 上的**无鉴权面**——"能开窗"就等于"本机进程也能放宽权限" > （上限受 `maxTtlSeconds` 约束）。不信任本机进程时，请把 `console.enabled` 设为 `false`。 档位自动回滚（`sweepIntervalMs`，默认 **30000**，`0` 表示关闭）： ```ts { sweepIntervalMs: 30000, // 每 30s 结算一次「授权已失效但档位还没收回」的会话 console: { enabled: true, host: "127.0.0.1", port: 8787 } } ``` > 定时器**不是安全机制**：授权是否有效始终在读写时实时判定；关掉它只会让回滚推迟到「下次任意工具调用」或用户点按钮。 配置（默认**已开启**；端口被占用时自动回退到系统分配的随机端口，实际地址写在 stderr 里）： ```ts { console: { enabled: true, host: "127.0.0.1", port: 8787, } } ``` 只提供： ```text GET / 前端页面（独立入口；支持 ?session= 聚焦会话） GET /console.js 共享前端脚本（面板与独立页面复用） GET /api/snapshot 治理快照（会话视图 + 每条授权的剩余毫秒；可带 ?session=） GET /api/audit 审计过滤查询（原始事件流，含遥测） GET /api/decisions 授权决策记录（一条授权一份：批准/复用/权限级别/结束方式；可带 sessionId/toolName/limit） GET /api/config 运行期策略 + 挡位目录 + 收缩动作可用性 + 自动回滚节拍 PATCH /api/config 写接口：defaultScope / defaultTtlSeconds / maxTtlSeconds POST /api/revoke 收缩型动作：action=revoke（撤销本会话全部授权）| restore-sandbox（只回滚档位） POST /api/window 免打扰窗口：{sessionId, toolName, mode, ttlSeconds}（唯一由页面发起的放宽，有界且可收回） ``` 此外，插件会尝试把同一组接口挂到 DSH Web 服务器上的**同源**前缀 `/guard/…`（`registerGuardWebRoutes`）。 同源入口可用时面板优先走它（无跨源请求）；不可用时回落到独立端口（Console 对 loopback 来源开放 CORS）。 `/guard/` 与独立端口**互为备份**，任一可用治理台就能工作。 ### 范围挡位（默认匹配范围） 治理台里可选的挡位，同时也是 `rules[].scope.mode` 的取值： | 挡位 | 复用范围 | 可否作为默认值 | |---|---|---| | `exact-arguments` | 工具名 + 参数逐字节一致 | ✅（零配置默认） | | `fields` | 只按指定字段取键 | ❌ 必须按工具显式配置 `paths` | | `sandbox-escalation` | 工具名 + 目标沙箱档位 | ✅ | | `tool` | 同一 Session 内该工具的全部调用 | ❌ 必须按工具显式配置 | > `tool` 被刻意排除在默认值之外（规格第 7 条）：默认值决定了「任意一次批准能复用多大范围」， > 不允许它悄悄变成整个工具。 > > `fields` 同样不在默认值里（2026-10-31 起）：兜底路径是 `path` / `file_path`，而多数工具（如 `pwsh`） > 的参数里并没有这两个字段；`ScopeResolver` 遇到缺失字段会 **Fail Closed 抛错**，Guard 因而不接管本次调用—— > 结果不是"复用键更窄"，而是**这条授权永远用不上、每次都要问**。它只能在 `rules[]` 里按工具配置明确的 `paths`。 ### 治理台的写权限边界 - 策略写接口只能改 `defaultScope` / `defaultTtlSeconds` / `maxTtlSeconds`； - `enabled` 与 `rules` **接口层不可写**（返回 400）——页面不能关掉 Guard，也不能凭空新增授权规则； - 运行期改动**不落盘**：Guard 不改写 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`，重启后回到 profile 配置值； - **收缩型动作**（`POST /api/revoke`）只有两个方向，且都只能让权限变小： - `action=revoke`：撤销该会话仍有效的全部授权，并回滚会话沙箱档位； - `action=restore-sandbox`：只结算该会话中**已经失效**的授权并回写档位，仍有效的授权原样不动。 - 两者都写审计（`LEASE_REVOKED` / `SANDBOX_MODE_RESTORED`），都遵守「用户手动改过档位则跳过回滚」的红线。 - **唯一由页面发起的放宽**（`POST /api/window`，即「免打扰窗口」）：用户显式点击＝一次 `allowed-once`， 签发有界 `sandbox-mode` 授权并立即提升会话档位。约束：TTL ≤ `maxTtlSeconds`（不静默裁剪）、 工具必须已配置为 `sandbox-escalation`、必须能解析到真实 Session（否则拒绝）、失败会撤销刚签发的授权。 - 页面**不做审批**：审批永远走 DSH 原生流程；开窗只是把"你已经同意的这件事"提前落地成有界授权。 安全属性： - 默认仅监听 `127.0.0.1`；Host 头必须是 loopback（DNS rebinding 防护）； - 跨源只回显 loopback 来源，非 loopback 来源直接 403； - 写接口要求自定义头（`x-dsh-guard`）＋ `application/json`，靠浏览器预检挡住 CSRF； - 响应使用 `no-store`、`nosniff` 与 CSP；前端所有动态数据通过 `textContent` 渲染； - 只展示白名单投影，不包含 Credential、Authorization Header 或原始 Tool Arguments。 --- ## 快速开始 ### 环境要求 - Node.js `22` - pnpm `11.25.0`（仓库 `packageManager` 已固定版本） - Windows / macOS / Linux 均可运行核心 TypeScript 代码；CI 已配置三平台矩阵 > [!NOTE] > `@dsh-capsule/adapter` 已声明 ```bash git clone cd dsh-capsule pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm build pnpm test ``` Workspace： ```text @dsh-capsule/adapter ``` ### 接入 DSH profile 插件包的 `package.json` 声明了 bundle patch，因此用 DSH 自带的 pwsh ttlSeconds: 300 scope: { mode: sandbox-escalation } - match: deploy.preview ttlSeconds: 120 scope: { mode: fields, paths: [project, environment] } ``` > 本仓库的 `adapter/cordis.patch.yml` 可用 `dsh --profile --dump-config --patch <该文件路径>` 单独验证语法，无需真正安装。 > > 改完插件代码后需要**重启 DSH**：profile 的 HMR 只重组配置，不会重新加载已装载模块的新一代 JavaScript。 ### 默认策略 ```ts { enabled: true, defaultTtlSeconds: 60, maxTtlSeconds: 1800, defaultScope: "exact-arguments", rules: [] } ``` 其中 `defaultScope`（默认范围挡位）与两个 TTL 可以在 DSH Web GUI 的治理台里运行期切换； `enabled` 与 `rules` 属于部署配置，只能在 profile patch 里改。 ### Tool 级规则 ```ts { enabled: true, defaultTtlSeconds: 60, maxTtlSeconds: 1800, defaultScope: "exact-arguments", rules: [ { match: "deploy.preview", ttlSeconds: 120, scope: { mode: "fields", paths: ["project", "environment"] } }, { // 沙箱升级：本会话内该工具可升到 danger-full-access，批准一次后 300 秒内免问， // 到期回滚到批准前的档位。默认不配置 = 完全不改变 DSH 行为。 match: "pwsh", ttlSeconds: 300, scope: { mode: "sandbox-escalation" } }, { match: "dangerous.admin", enabled: false } ] } ``` 当前 V1 的 `match` 是**精确 Tool Name 匹配**，不是 glob / regex。 --- ## Fail-Closed 错误模型 关键安全失败使用结构化错误码，而不是静默降级： ```text LEASE_REVOKED LEASE_EXPIRED LEASE_TTL_INVALID LEASE_SCOPE_INVALID LEASE_POLICY_INVALID ``` 核心原则： > **无法校验身份、Scope 或 TTL 时，不签发或复用 Lease，保留原生审批语义。** 沙箱升级链路同样遵循这一原则，且可审计的治理事件是完整的（放宽与收回都有记录）： ```text SANDBOX_MODE_RAISED 会话沙箱模式被提升（含工具与目标档位） SANDBOX_MODE_RESTORED Lease 结束，模式已回滚 SANDBOX_MODE_SKIPPED_USER_OVERRIDE 检测到用户已手动改动模式，跳过回滚并交还控制权 ``` --- ## 安全边界与非目标 这是当前项目最重要的边界说明： ### Universal Mode 能承诺什么 - 为原本触发 `ask` 的 Tool（以及沙箱升级）增加短期 Lease； - Session / Tool / Scope / TTL 绑定； - 过期、撤销、复用与审计； - 沙箱模式提升会在 Lease 结束后**回滚**，且不覆盖用户的手动改动； - 不覆盖 DSH 原始 `deny`； - 不修改已有 Tool 代码即可接入。 ### Universal Mode **不能**承诺什么 - 不能保证任意第三方插件看不到 Credential； - 不能阻止插件自己发网络请求； - 不提供进程、容器、VM 或 microVM 级恶意代码隔离； - **不能阻止其他插件认领 `approval/request`**：这是 DSH 的开放瀑布事件，"谁认领谁说了算"。任何插件都可以零交互返回 `allowed-once`，也可以抢先认领从而遮蔽 Guard 的观察位置。这是 DSH 事件模型的固有性质，不属于本插件能防御的范围； - **不能阻止其他插件直接改写会话权限状态**：`setSandboxMode(session, mode)`、`ctx.permissionPresets.set(...)`、`ctx.approval.setPolicy(...)` 在 DSH 中都是公开 API，Guard 只是选择"只用其中最小的一档并加上边界"。 ## 当前状态 | 能力 | 状态 | |---|---| | Universal Lease Gate（四 hook） | ✅ 已实现 | | Session / Scope / TTL / Revoke | ✅ 已实现 | | 沙箱升级有界授权（`sandbox-escalation` + 模式提升与回滚） | ✅ 已实现 | | 真 cordis 集成测试（真实 `Context` / `waterfall` / `emit`） | ✅ 已实现 | | 权限生命周期端到端集成测试（ask→签发→复用→过期/撤销） | ✅ 已实现（`integration/permission-lifecycle.test.ts`） | | DSH 行为基线核实（逐行核对已安装版本源码） | ✅ 已完成（`docs/集成基线-真实DSH行为.md`） | | 治理台：会话视图 / 授权剩余时间 / 两状态（授权有效 vs 档位已恢复）/ 审计 / 范围挡位 | ✅ 已实现（Web GUI 面板 + 独立页面 + `/guard/` 同源路由） | | 治理台收缩型动作：立即收回 / 立即回滚档位（只收缩，带审计） | ✅ 已实现（`POST /api/revoke`） | | 档位自动回滚（`sweepIntervalMs`，默认 30s，可关） | ✅ 已实现（非安全机制，只负责及时性） | | Secret-safe Audit | ✅ 已实现 | | Ubuntu / Windows / macOS CI workflow | ✅ 已配置 | | 在真实 profile 中安装并实跑（hook 挂载 + 治理台 + 面板注册） | ✅ 已完成（本机 desktop profile） | | 可直接安装的公开 DSH Release Package（`dsh.bundle.patch`） | ✅ 已具备（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`） | | Durable Lease Store | 🗺️ Roadmap | DeepSeek Harness 本身也处于 Developer Preview 并快速迭代，因此正式接入时应始终以当前安装版本的 TypeScript 类型为准，而不是把事件签名硬编码为长期兼容承诺。**升级 DSH 后请重跑 `docs/集成基线-真实DSH行为.md` 第 10 节的检查清单。** --- ## 仓库结构 ```text adapter/ ├── client.js # DSH 治理台面板与侧栏入口 ├── cordis.patch.yml # 插件配置与默认沙箱升级规则 └── src/ ├── index.ts # 插件装配与宿主适配（含 30s 档位结算节拍） ├── capability/ # 四个 hook、Scope、Lease、沙箱提升与回滚、回滚审计 ├── integration/ # 真 cordis 接线与权限生命周期测试 ├── audit/ # 脱敏审计 └── console/ # 会话视图 / 决策记录 / HTTP 接口 / 动作（收缩 + 有界放宽）/ 会话名解析 scripts/smoke-console.mjs # 治理台冒烟脚本（示例数据 + 真实收缩动作） .github/workflows/ci.yml # Windows / macOS / Linux 构建与测试 ``` --- ## 设计原则 **Preserve DSH semantics.** Guard 只增强 `ask`，不覆盖 `deny`，不重新发明 Approval。 **Short-lived authority.** 权限必须有明确 Session、Scope 与 TTL，而不是永久授权。 **Deterministic scope.** 安全边界来自确定性规则，不让 LLM 猜授权范围。 **Fail closed.** 身份、Scope 或 TTL 无法验证时不签发或复用授权。 **Secret-safe observability.** Audit 与 Console 只保留治理所需的白名单字段。 **Small trusted core.** 核心只负责短期授权生命周期，不代管凭证或执行外部业务。 --- ## FAQ ### 这和 RBAC 有什么区别？ RBAC 更适合回答“这个角色通常拥有什么权限”。Capability Lease 回答的是：**这个 Session 在当前 TTL 内，是否允许这个 Tool 对这个 Scope 执行当前操作。** 它更适合 Agent 的动态、短时工作流。 ### Universal Mode 能保护所有第三方插件吗？ 它可以零改造地为**原本会触发 DSH `ask`** 的 Tool，以及**沙箱升级**，增加短期 Lease；但不能阻止其他插件认领 `approval/request`，也不能阻止插件访问其进程本身已经拥有的资源。 ### 为什么默认 Scope 是 `exact-arguments`？ 因为零配置情况下无法可靠猜测某个第三方 Tool 的业务资源语义。默认只复用完全相同的参数，宁可多问一次，也不扩大授权面。 **但要说实话**：在同一路径上，LLM 很少两次生成逐字节相同的参数，所以零配置的 `exact-arguments` 实际收益有限。真正省事的是显式配置 `fields`（按业务字段）或 `sandbox-escalation`（按工具与目标档位）——**收益来自显式配置，而不是默认值**。 ### 沙箱升级为什么不把 `justification` 算进 Scope？ 因为它是模型每次现写的自由文本。把它纳入 Scope 等于把安全边界建立在模型输出上，而且措辞一变授权立即失效、复用率几乎为零。Guard 只按 `(toolName, 目标模式)` 取键——这也符合"禁止用字符串启发式猜测安全边界"的项目规则。`justification` 只用于给人看（截断后展示）。 ### 沙箱升级会不会把用户手动设的权限冲掉？ 不会。回滚前会做冲突检测：如果当前模式已不是 Guard 最后写入的值（说明用户手动改过），Guard **跳过回滚**并写入 `SANDBOX_MODE_SKIPPED_USER_OVERRIDE` 审计，把控制权交还用户。 ### 支持 Windows / macOS / Linux 吗？ 当前主链路是纯 TypeScript，没有 Python / Docker / Unix Domain Socket 依赖；仓库 CI 也配置了三平台矩阵。真实 DSH 集成仍需按具体 DSH 版本做兼容性验证。 --- ## Roadmap 近期聚焦授权范围与状态展示、生命周期异常恢复、审计与 DSH 版本兼容性。新增撤销界面、续期或更细范围前，需先更新规格并验证宿主执行边界；当前不承诺这些功能已经实现。 --- ## Contributing 安全基础设施最需要的是**负向测试与清晰边界**。欢迎贡献： - Lease / Scope / Session 隔离测试； - 并发 `callId`、取消与生命周期 Race 测试； - 审计脱敏回归测试； - DSH 版本兼容性验证； - 文档、Demo 与可复现集成样例。 如果一个改动会扩大可信计算面、引入凭证执行链路，或试图绕开 DSH 原生 Approval / Sandbox，请先讨论设计再实现。 --- ## License MIT License. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-aiignore — context noise guard for DeepSeek Harness

A Host plugin that checks a workspace **when a session opens it** and tells the
agent which files would waste its context — build output, lockfiles, logs,
huge files.

The scan is the same one the [`ai-context-doctor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ai-context-doctor)
CLI runs; this package only decides *when* to run it and how to phrase the
result for the model. Everything is local: no network, no API key, no upload.

## Requirements

| | |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness | `>= 0.2.0` — the version that ships `sidebarRightTabs`; declared as `engines.dsh` in `package.json` and in every market-index entry, so an older Harness refuses the install instead of half-loading it |
| Node.js | `>= 18` — the Host half uses `node:test` and `structuredClone` |
| Permissions | none. No network, no API key, no telemetry; it reads the workspace and writes `.aiignore` and `.aiignore.policy.json` |

Without a sidebar service the same button opens the panel as a floating card,
so an older or trimmed-down Harness still gets the report, just not the tab.

## What the agent sees

When a workspace scores below the threshold, the agent receives one short note
before it starts reading files:

```text
[ai-context-doctor] This workspace scores 29/100 for context health: 71% of 1.7 MB in 24 files is likely noise.
Biggest offenders: dist/ (400.0 KB, generated build output), package-lock.json (400.0 KB, lockfile).
Suggested .aiignore: dist/, package-lock.json, *.log.
Do not read those files unless the task needs them; ask before opening large generated files.
```

Clean workspaces get no message at all — a plugin that speaks on every session
becomes noise itself.

## The panel

The bundle also ships a browser half. A folder button sits beside the add-files
button in the composer; clicking it opens the **right sidebar** on the
**AIignore** tab, and expands the sidebar if it was collapsed. On a Host without
sidebar services the same button opens the panel as a floating card instead, so
one plugin covers both.

![The Protection tab, light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/docs/assets/panel-protection-light.png)

![The Files tab: what this session read and wrote](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/docs/assets/panel-files-light.png)

Three tabs inside, and the first one exists to answer a single question: *is
this doing anything?*

- **Protection** — a score, one button, and nothing else competing with them.
  The number is the folder's own score: *before rules* on a fresh install, and
  *after rules* once rules exist, with the line underneath reading `22 → 71`
  and how many tokens stay out. A folder nobody has scanned says *not scanned
  yet* rather than printing a dash under a label that promises a number, and a
  conversation that read nothing junk-worthy says so in words instead of a
  zero. **Optimize now** is always there — it
  rescans, writes whatever is missing, re-scores, and reports what moved, so
  the interaction is: look, press, watch the number change.
  The **strength ladder** is one click away in *Fine-tune the strength*: five
  notches, each labelled with the score this folder would have there, because
  five scores at once answer a question nobody asked yet. Picking a notch
  writes it, rescans and repaints from the new report. Below that, **one notch
  stricter** with the number attached ("would block 2 more files, about
  65k–81k tokens"), then the files actually kept out and how many rules are in
  force.
- **Files** — opens on **the files this session touched** (what the agent read
  and what it wrote), then lets you browse the whole workspace a directory at a
  time. Search, filter by verdict — and when a filter has nothing in it, the
  panel says which filter that was instead of looking empty. The three verdicts
  are spelled out right under the filters: `noise` is regenerated by a build, a
  lockfile or a log; `review` is worth a look before it goes in (env files,
  deploy scripts, big data); `ignored` already has a line in `.aiignore`. Under
  that, **Worth a rule** lists what the scanner would still add (`+ *.log`,
  `+ coverage/`) — one click writes the line and rescans. A noise file's detail
  card offers the widest rule that covers it, `Add dist/`, not only its own
  path, because a per-file line is a rule you write again every build.
- **Settings** — everything you can change, off the screen that answers *is it
  working*: **Rules in .aiignore** with an × per line, the note for the agent
  with a preview of exactly the text it will read, and the five-dimension
  arithmetic folded away at the bottom. It points at Protection for the
  strength ladder instead of keeping a second copy of it — two controls for one
  setting drift, and the copy that stops being authoritative is always the one
  on the page nobody is looking at.

  It no longer asks you to imagine what the note does: three one-click
  sentences, then a preview of **exactly the text the agent will read** before
  your next message.

- **One button runs the job.** *Optimize now* reads the folder, writes the
  rules, re-scores and moves the number on screen. While it runs you see the two
  steps it actually performs, each marked done only when its work is finished —
  no percentage bar inventing progress the Host never reported.
- **The rules are visible, and removable one at a time.** Under the score sits
  **Rules in .aiignore**: every line that is in force, each with an ×. Removing
  one edits exactly that line — comments and the other rules stay — so a rule
  you disagree with is one click away instead of an all-or-nothing undo.
- **The strength is part of the score, not a separate page.** Five buttons from
  *Off* to *Strict*, each already scored against your workspace before you commit
  to one, so the difference between *Balanced* and *Strict* is a number you read
  instead of a slider you drag. There is no slider any more: two ways to say the
  same thing was one too many. Each notch says what it stops and what that costs;
  the Host stores it in `.aiignore.policy.json`; the read guard and the scan share
  the same predicate, so saving a notch re-scans and the number moves.

### The words this panel uses

Five terms carry most of the panel, and they are used the same way everywhere —
in the tabs, the tooltips, the changelog and this file.

| Term | Means | Not to be confused with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **held back** | a read your rules stopped, or would stop. The counter, the list under it and the badge all say this. | *refused* — the guard turning a read away right now | 
| **rule** | one line in `.aiignore`, matched against paths | a *note*, which is text for the agent, not a rule |
| **notch** | one of the five strength settings, from Off to Strict | the *score*, which the notch changes |
| **score** | two numbers: this conversation, and what still reaches the model | *tokens*, which are a byte-based estimate |
| **noise** | build output, lockfiles, logs, generated files and anything over 1 MB | *review*, which means look before you decide |

### Following the conversation, not a folder

The panel asks the Host who the current conversation is, and the Host reads the
session store: `<DSH_HOME>/sessions/*/session-*/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` is an
append-only zstd file whose **first frame is a JSON header** carrying the
session id and its `cwd`. The most recently written log is the conversation in
front of you, and its header names the folder — no guessing from directory
names, and no dependency on the workspace index ever having been told about that
session. The header names the workspace; the guard, the score and the file list
then all speak about that one folder.

The Chat tab's picker shows the conversations this app knows about, newest
first, with `current` on the live one. Picking an older one re-reads *that*
conversation — header title, turn count and file list all switch — and a
`showing an earlier conversation` chip appears in the header; clicking it takes
you back to the live one.

The folder button keeps a menu: **follow this conversation** (the default),
**pick another folder…**, or **stop pinning** — so a choice made once is a choice
you can take back. Every workspace this app has been used in is also listed on
the **Context across your workspaces** page in the left rail, scored with the
same rules.

### One click, with a way back

**Optimize this workspace** appends the scanner's suggestion to `.aiignore`,
keeping the lines already there, then reports the score before and after. The
previous file is held in memory for the session, so **Undo** puts it back byte
for byte — and if optimize created the file, undo removes it.

Two decisions per file, available from the tree, the session list and the report:

- **Read once** (the report calls it **Read it anyway**) pre-approves a path for
  the rest of the Host run, including one the session has not tried yet.
  Reloading the Harness forgets it — a temporary override should stay temporary.
- **Never read it** appends the path to the workspace's `.aiignore`. That is the
  durable direction, because the file is the record: it survives restarts, shows
  up in review, and you can delete the line yourself.

One workspace can hold many conversations, so the panel never averages them:
the **Chat** tab's picker lists the conversations this app knows, marks the one
currently open, and every number above it is that conversation's. There is no
separate "follow" entry in the picker — the folder button already means
follow, and two controls for one state is one control too many. When the session
store cannot answer, the panel falls back to the directory the slot hands it
(`?cwd=`), then to the agent and session registries, then to whatever was
scanned last. Only an absolute path to an existing directory is accepted.

The aggregate view lives in the left rail, under New Session: **AIignore** lists
every conversation this app has run, worst first, and can act without opening
any of them. Each row shows the conversation's title, folder, turns, files read
and size; the score on the left is the one your rules and strength leave behind,
with the pre-rule number trailing behind it when the two differ, and a
`N kept out` badge once a clean-up covers something. **Scan again** refreshes,
**Clean up N** writes that conversation's suggestions, **Open the panel** jumps
to it. It is served by `GET /aiignore/conversations` (twenty-one routes in total).

Both numbers are computed from the session projection, never from a guess: the
conversation score is what that chat was actually handed, and the effective
score re-runs the same decision the guard uses — rules, then strength — so a
conversation that read `dist/` before you had a rule shows `74` and `100`
afterwards, with the file named under **No longer reaching the model**.

Styling comes from the Host's design tokens (`--dsw-*`) with fallbacks, so the
panel follows light and dark themes instead of shipping its own palette. Every
control is reachable with `Tab`.

Loading, empty and failure are three states of one component, on all three
surfaces that fetch anything (the panel, the left page, the strength table): a
skeleton while a request is in flight, one sentence when there is nothing to
show, and an error that names what failed, carries the real status
(`status 500`), and offers a retry that repeats the same request. Nothing
silently disappears — the strength table used to vanish while it loaded — and
nothing invents a cause: an unreachable server says `network`, a rejected one
says the status.

The panel talks to the Host half over twenty-one same-origin routes
(`GET /aiignore/report`, `GET /aiignore/tree?dir=`, `GET /aiignore/overview`,
`GET /aiignore/sessions`, `GET /aiignore/workspaces`, `GET /aiignore/levels`,
`GET /aiignore/debug`,
`GET/POST /aiignore/notes`, `GET/POST /aiignore/policy`,
`GET /aiignore/upload?digest=`, `POST /aiignore/scan`,
`POST /aiignore/client-report`, `POST /aiignore/optimize`,
`POST /aiignore/optimize/undo`, `POST /aiignore/allow`,
`POST /aiignore/ignore`, `POST /aiignore/unignore`,
`POST /aiignore/rules`, `POST /aiignore/rules/delete`). The upload route serves a thumbnail and refuses
anything that is not a 64-hex digest inside the attachment store; the unignore
route removes the rule that names a file and refuses symlinks and directories,
while `rules/delete` removes one rule line by its exact text (`dist/`, `*.log`)
and never touches a comment, while `rules` writes one rule that was suggested
without a file to name (`*.log`) — it checks the shape (relative, no `..`, no
leading `/`) and clears the scan caches so the next read sees it. They
answer for the most recently scanned workspace and set `no-store`; the only one
that returns file bytes is the upload thumbnail, and it only ever returns an
image the user already handed to this session. The Host half installs them through `ctx.inject(['webServer'])`,
so a profile without a web server still gets the read guard — it just has no panel.
There is no authentication beyond a same-origin check: like every
`ctx.webServer` route, this one inherits the loopback bind of the Harness and
must not be exposed to a network.

![Settings, dark theme: rules and the note for the agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/docs/assets/panel-settings-dark.png)

### When something looks wrong

Settings ends with a **Diagnostics** fold: plugin version, Node, platform, data
folder, workspace, how many conversations it can see, how many rules are in
effect, and which surface (sidebar tab or floating card) you got. One button
copies it as plain text.

It is built to be pasted in public — the home directory is shortened to `~` and
there is no token, session id or conversation title anywhere in it.

### Looking at the panel without a Harness

`dev/preview.html` renders the real panel against the Host's real design tokens
with mock data: both themes, four scenarios (noisy, healthy, freshly opened,
request failing), and `?nosidebar=1` to see the floating-card fallback. Open the
file in a browser; no build, no server. It is a development page and is not part
of the published package.

### Behaviour tests

`test/interaction.test.mjs` mounts the real `client.js` in Node — jsdom, the real
React, a host context that records what the bundle registers, and stubbed
`/aiignore/*` routes — and then does what a person does:

```js

await panel.press('#aicd-tab-protect', 'ArrowRight');   // the tab moves
await panel.click('[data-aicd-menu-btn]');               // the menu opens
await panel.press('[role="menu"]', 'Escape');            // and closes on Escape
await panel.click('[data-wide="true"]');                 // Optimize posts once
```

The older `*.test.mjs` guards that read this file as text are still here: they
are fast and they catch a deleted string, but they could never have caught the
bug where Optimize was hidden — only mounting it could.

`docs/assets/baseline/` holds the eight screenshots the panel is measured
against: four preview scenarios (*noisy*, *healthy*, *fresh*, *broken*) in both
themes, cropped to the 420 × 660 the sidebar actually gives it. They are
committed, not generated in CI — this repository has no headless browser.

After an **intentional** visual change, re-capture all eight. Each one is a

```
dev/preview.html?scenario=noisy&theme=dark
```

## Install

Through the Plugin Manager:

- **From npm** — install `dsh-aiignore`.
- **From a checkout** — install the `plugin/` directory of this repository.

Installing a local directory links it, so re-check the files directly: `files`
does not filter a linked directory.

### From the plugin market

Harness has no central store: the **Discover** tab lists whatever indexes the
user adds. This repository publishes one at

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/market/index.json
```

To use it:

1. Open **Plugins** in the Web sidebar.
2. Beside **Experimental plugins**, open **More** and switch on **Custom plugin
   markets**. The Plugins page then gains an **Installed** / **Discover** split.
3. In **Discover**, add the index URL above.
4. Install **dsh-aiignore** from the result.

The Harness checks the declared `engines.dsh` range before installing and
refuses the plugin if the running version falls outside it.

## Configure

Values go in the plugin's `config` row in `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: ai-context-doctor
      name: 'dsh-aiignore'
      config:
        healthThreshold: 80
        maxFiles: 20000
        maxBytes: 268435456
```

| key | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healthThreshold` | `80` | Inject only when the workspace scores below this. `100` disables the notice without uninstalling. |
| `maxFiles` | `20000` | Stop scanning after this many files. |
| `maxBytes` | `268435456` | Stop scanning after this many bytes (256 MiB). |
| `readPolicy` | `deny` | `deny` refuses `read` calls on the noisy files below; `off` only warns at session start. |

The caps exist because the scan is a synchronous directory walk: without them,
opening a huge monorepo would stall the Host.

The guard also refuses anything the workspace's own `.aiignore` lists, including
files the size heuristic considers clean. A hand-written rule beats the
heuristic, and editing the file takes effect on the next read.

## What it refuses to read

With `readPolicy: deny`, the plugin installs a tool guard that refuses `read`
calls on the same files the notice names:

| refused | why |
| --- | --- |
| `dist/`, `build/`, `coverage/`, `.next/`, `.turbo/` | generated output; the source is what matters |
| `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock` | thousands of lines of resolved versions |
| `*.log` | local run output, usually stale |
| files over 1 MiB | a single read can consume the whole budget |

The refusal is a message, not a silent failure: it names the file, its size and
the tokens the read would have cost, so the agent can tell the user instead of
retrying. Templates like `.env.example` and scripts with `deploy` in the path
are **never** blocked — they are small, and a wrong guess there loses real
information.

Every refusal is recorded per workspace (`getSkippedReads`) so the UI half can
list what this session did not open.

## Limits

- The notice fires once per workspace per Host run; changing the directory in a
  session does not re-trigger it.
- The score is a size heuristic; token figures are a range from the measured
  3.08–4.32 bytes-per-token ratio, not an exact count.
- `bash`, `grep` and other tools that can read a file indirectly are not
  intercepted: the guard only sees the `read` tool.
- `.gitignore` is ignored on purpose: the point is what the agent *would* read,
  not what git tracks.
- The panel follows the conversation whose log was written last. Switching to a
  conversation you have not touched since this Host run started moves it only
  after that conversation writes something, so it can lag one click behind.
- Switching the interface language takes effect the next time the panel opens;
  the open panel does not re-render.

[中文说明](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/blob/main/docs/README.zh-CN.md)

**AI coding agents read your repository file by file. Some of those files are garbage — build output, logs, lockfiles, a 40 MB data dump. This tool finds them in a few seconds and tells you what to keep away from the agent.**

```bash
npx ai-context-doctor
```

No install, no login, no API key, nothing uploaded. It only reads file names and sizes.

## What it looks like

Real output from the demo repository in this project:

```text
AI Context Doctor

Repo: demo-ai-context-noise-repo
Scanned: 8 files, 1.50 MB

AI Context Health: 22/100
Status: Too much noise for an AI coding agent

Context noise estimate:
78% likely noise
22% likely useful source context

Top context waste:
1. data/export.json            1.00 MB   large file
2. dist/                      106.9 KB   generated build output
3. package-lock.json           35.2 KB   lockfile
4. logs/dev.log                18.4 KB   local log file
5. coverage/                   16.7 KB   test coverage output

Review before sharing:
- .env.example             environment template (usually safe to share)
- scripts/deploy.sh        deployment script

Suggested .aiignore:
coverage/
dist/
*.log
package-lock.json

Next step:
Run this before asking your coding agent to inspect a larger repo.
```

## How to read it

| Line | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Scanned: 8 files, 1.50 MB` | What was actually walked. `.git/` and `node_modules/` are skipped. |
| `AI Context Health: 43/100` | Five separate losses, subtracted from 100: noise (30), sheer size (25), one file dominating (20), file count (15), binaries (10). The first is what rules can move; the other four describe the folder itself, so a clean but enormous repository no longer scores 100. |
| `Status:` | Just the score in words: 85+ clean, 60–84 some noise, below 60 too much. |
| `Top context waste` | The five biggest offenders with the reason each was flagged. |
| `Review before sharing` | Files that look like credentials or deploy scripts. **The tool does not claim they are secret** — it says look before you paste the repo into a chat. |
| `Suggested .aiignore` | Lines you can paste into an ignore file. Nothing is written for you. |

## What you can do with it

- **Before you hand a repo to an agent** — run it, then `--write` the suggested lines into `.aiignore` instead of copying them by hand.
- **On a repo you just cloned** — see how much of it is generated output before the agent drowns in it.
- **In CI** — `--json` gives a stable object, so you can fail a build when context health drops.
- **In your own tool** — `require('ai-context-doctor')` exposes the same scan as a function.
- **Inside DeepSeek Harness** — install [`dsh-aiignore`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-aiignore) and the agent is told automatically when a session opens a noisy workspace, so you do not have to remember to run anything.

## Install

Run it without installing anything:

```bash
npx ai-context-doctor
```

Or install it once:

```bash
npm install -g ai-context-doctor
```

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

## Usage

```bash
ai-context-doctor              # scan the current directory
ai-context-doctor ../some-repo # scan another repository
ai-context-doctor --json       # machine-readable output
ai-context-doctor --write      # add the suggested rules to .aiignore
ai-context-doctor --write --dry-run   # show what --write would add
ai-context-doctor --help
ai-context-doctor --version
```

### Writing `.aiignore`

```bash
npx ai-context-doctor --write
```

`--write` appends the rules the report suggests to `.aiignore` in the scanned
directory. It only appends: comments and rules you already have stay exactly as
they are, and running it twice adds nothing the second time. If the file does
not exist it is created with a two-line header.

`--write --dry-run` prints what would be added and writes nothing.

It will not follow a symbolic link, and it refuses to replace a directory that
happens to be called `.aiignore`.

The scan is a heuristic over file names and sizes — it does not read `.aiignore`
— so the score will not change just because you wrote the file. The file is for
the other tools: your agent, your editor, your teammates.

### JSON output

```bash
npx ai-context-doctor ./some-repo --json
```

Returns `repo`, `healthScore`, `effectiveScore`, `status`, `noisePercent`, `usefulPercent`, `scannedBytes`, `scannedFiles`, `allowedBytes`, `allowedFiles`, `topNoise`, `review`, `suggestedAiignore`, `scoreBreakdown` (the five-dimension arithmetic behind each score) and `scoreLost` — plus `truncated: true` when a scan cap was hit.

With `--write` it also carries a `write` object: `path`, `created`, `added`, `written`, `dryRun`.

If the path is not a readable directory, `--json` still prints a single JSON object — never a banner — and exits with code 1, so a CI step can parse the failure:

```json
{
  "error": "not-a-readable-directory",
  "message": "/path/you/passed is not a readable directory.",
  "target": "/path/you/passed"
}
```

## Use it from code

```js
const { scanRepository } = require('ai-context-doctor');

const report = scanRepository(process.cwd());
console.log(report.healthScore, report.topNoise);
```

`writeAiignore(aiignorePath, suggested, { dryRun })` is the writer behind `--write`, if you want the same behaviour from code.

`scanRepository(root, { maxFiles, maxBytes })` is synchronous and has no dependencies. Pass a cap for huge trees; the report then carries `truncated: true`.

## DeepSeek Harness plugin

[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)

[`dsh-aiignore`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-aiignore) packages the same scan as a Host plugin. When a session opens a workspace, the agent gets one short note naming the files that would waste its context — and nothing at all when the workspace is clean.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-aiignore
```

The plugin also adds an **AIignore** tab to the right sidebar, opened from a
folder button in the composer. It opens on **Protection**: how many reads in
*this conversation* are junk and that your rules now hold back, and roughly how
many tokens never reached the model. Before you optimize it says the honest
version — "2 reads are junk and still reach the model" — so the button has
something to be measured against. One primary button, *Optimize now*, rescans,
writes what is missing, re-reads the conversation and reports the score before
and after; when nothing is missing it says so. A second line offers **one notch stricter** with
the number attached, so "raise the strength" is a decision instead of advice.
Directly under the counters is the **strength ladder**: five notches, each
labelled with the score this folder would have at that notch, so the trade is
visible before you take it — and picking one applies it and rescores the page.
**Files** browses the workspace a directory at a time and spells out what its
three verdicts mean — `noise` is regenerated by a build, a lockfile or a log,
`review` is worth a look first, `ignored` already has a rule — then offers the
rules the scanner would still add, one click each; **Settings** holds the
`.aiignore` lines with an × each, the note for the agent, and the
five-dimension arithmetic. It follows the Harness light and dark themes.

![The AIignore tab in the right sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/docs/assets/panel-protection-light.png)

It declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.0"` — the Harness checks that range before installing, and refuses the plugin rather than half-loading it — and needs Node.js 18 or newer. In the [plugin market index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/main/market/index.json) it is filed under **Context quality** with three labels: *No network calls*, *Works with no setup*, *Lives in the sidebar*. Without a sidebar service the same button opens the panel as a floating card. The source, its configuration and its limits are in [`plugin/README.md`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/ai-context-doctor/blob/main/plugin/README.md).
